+-+ {"content": "# Competition Engine\n\nThis implementation provides role-owned capabilities and explicit handovers for competition planning and operations.\n\n## Addons\n\n1. `sports_federation_competition_core`: identity, roles, lifecycle and events.\n2. `sports_federation_registration`: application queue and finalized participant sets.\n3. `sports_federation_format`: versioned logical structures and fixtures.\n4. `sports_federation_calendar`: physical match days, round allocations and capacity.\n5. `sports_federation_scheduling`: one-way fixture-to-slot assignments, pure validation and deterministic proposals.\n6. `sports_federation_schedule_approval`: independent review and immutable publication snapshots.\n7. `sports_federation_matchday`: live operational control and incidents.\n\n## Required handovers\n\nRegistration finalizes a participant set. Format freezes a structure. Calendar prepares physical capacity. Scheduling submits a complete schedule. Approval publishes an immutable snapshot. Match-day operations execute only a published snapshot.\n\n## Migration policy\n\nThe legacy monolithic engine has been removed from the addon set. New and existing operational flows use the ownership split. Databases upgraded from a release that installed the legacy addon require the normal reviewed upgrade/migration procedure before production rollout; do not silently reinterpret existing production records.\n\n\n## Schedule handoff operator handoff\n\nThe operator path is fully exposed in the backend: Schedule Planner submits a\nvalidated revision, Schedule Review Queue provides independent request-changes\nor approval decisions, Publication exposes approved schedules and immutable\npublication history, and Match-Day Operations consumes only the current live\npublication. Submission creates its pending review atomically when the approval\naddon is installed; there is no operator-visible intermediate state that\nrequires a separate \"start review\" action.\n\n## Phases 5.1.1 to 5.3: publication and live operations\n\nSchedule review decisions are command-only: ACLs are read-only and the review\nmodel rejects direct decision-field writes. Live publications are scoped and\nversioned per match day. Publication replacement uses a dedicated wizard,\nrequires a replacement reason, locks the match day during version allocation,\nand rejects stale confirmations.\n\nMatch-Day Control exposes readiness, the exact live publication, published\nmatches, court state, incidents, immutable sessions and operational deviations.\nOpening a day freezes the publication digest in a session. Live moves, delays,\npostponements and cancellations update only operational match fields; the\napproved publication and `published_slot_id` remain immutable. Every deviation\nrecords actor, reason, old/new slot, session and publication, and emits an audit\nevent.\n", "content_length": 2809, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "COMPETITION_ENGINE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "2c6a2ef0be5e1aece6060a09b33b5da37b58fc1a0bca7e3604aa9cde951df0b0", "size_bytes": 2809}

Wizards/services: put transient models in `wizards/` and algorithmic code in the owning module's `services/` package.\n5. Run module tests: `odoo-bin -d <db> -i <module> --test-enable --stop-after-init`.\n\nPR checklist (quick)\n\n- Tests added or updated for the core business behaviour.\n- Security ACLs/record rules added.\n- `__manifest__.py` updated (depends/data/version) when database changes are introduced.\n- Short README or notes added to the module.\n\nNotes for agents/readers\n\n- Prefer the `_workflows` files and `TECHNICAL_NOTE.md` as the source of truth for business behaviour and extension points.\n- When proposing code changes, keep modules focused, prefer service classes for algorithms, and add tests demonstrating deterministic behaviour (especially for schedule generation).\n\nIf you want, I can expand this summary into a short onboarding checklist, open a PR with the change, or scan `_logs/` and module READMEs to pull in extra context.\n\nRecent additions (2026-04-07)\n\nThe competition modules provide per-round scheduling and stage-graph support. For fast UI work use\n`--frontend-module`; for cross-module safety use\n`--affected-from origin/main --include-dependents`. +-+ {"content": "# Integration Contracts\n\nLast updated: 2026-08-20\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nThis document defines the stable partner-facing contracts currently supported by\nthe federation platform and the policy used to version, evolve, and deprecate\nthem.\n\nMachine-readable partner route definitions live in `openapi/integration_v1.yaml`.\nKeep the OpenAPI file, this document, and the route implementations aligned in\nthe same change set whenever a managed integration contract changes.\n\n## Contract Principles\n\n- Every external export or feed must expose an explicit contract identifier.\n- Version changes must be additive within a version whenever possible.\n- Breaking schema changes require a new contract version rather than silent\n  mutation of an existing response.\n- Deprecated routes or payloads remain available for at least one supported\n  release cycle after the replacement contract is published, unless security or\n  legal requirements force a faster removal.\n- Contract changes must be reflected in code, tests where applicable, this\n  document, and the roadmap or release notes in the same change set.\n\n## Authentication Strategy\n\nPublic tournament contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"`\n- intended for website visitors, public calendars, and read-only partner\n  consumption\n\nOperator-authenticated reporting exports:\n\n- `auth=\"user\"`\n- require an authenticated backend session\n- intended for federation operators using backend actions and reporting screens\n\nManaged partner contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"` routes protected by partner credentials\n- require `X-Federation-Partner-Code` and `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- enforce per-partner contract subscriptions before a payload is served or a\n  delivery is accepted\n- intended for explicit machine-to-machine integrations without sharing backend\n  user sessions\n\nImport contracts:\n\n- executed either through backend import wizards or through managed partner\n  delivery staging before entering the same wizard flow\n- guarded by dry-run preview, governance-job approval, and checksum matching for\n  live imports\n\n## Public Contracts\n\n## Tournament Feed\n\n- Canonical route: `/api/v1/tournaments/<slug>/feed`\n- Compatibility routes:\n  - `/api/v1/tournaments/<id>/feed`\n  - `/api/v1/competitions/<id>/feed`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_feed`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: v1`\n- Payload anchor:\n  - top-level `api_version = \"v1\"`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - top-level keys in the v1 payload are stable\n  - additive nested fields are allowed in v1 when they do not alter existing\n    semantics\n\n## Tournament Schedule Calendar\n\n- Canonical route: `/tournaments/<slug>/schedule.ics`\n- Compatibility route: `/tournament/<id>/schedule.ics`\n- Response type: `text/calendar`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_schedule_ics`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: ics_v1`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - calendar structure stays compatible with standard ICS consumers\n  - field enrichment should be additive inside event descriptions, not a change\n    to the ICS envelope\n\n## Authenticated CSV Contracts\n\nAll authenticated CSV exports expose these headers:\n\n- `X-Federation-Contract`\n- `X-Federation-Contract-Version`\n\n## Standings Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/standings/<tournament_id>`\n- Contract: `standings_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n- Notes:\n  - intended for downstream standings review and board-pack style extracts\n\n## Participation Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/participation/<season_id>`\n- Contract: `participation_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Summary Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance`\n- Contract: `finance_summary_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Event Handoff Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance/events`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Versioning anchor:\n  - detailed finance-event handoff rows expose a schema version column and the\n    matching response header contract version\n- Required handoff fields include:\n  - event identity and state\n  - handoff state\n  - fee type and amount\n  - invoice, external, accounting-batch, and reconciliation references\n  - source traceability\n  - exported, reconciled, and closed `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- Payload includes:\n  - contract code, version, direction, transport, and route hint\n  - deprecation stage and replacement contract\n  - `available` flag for database-specific operational availability\n  - partner subscription state and last-used timestamp\n\n## Partner Finance Event Handoff\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`\n- Response type: `text/csv`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Optional query parameters:\n  - `limit` to request one bounded page of rows; defaults to `200` and caps at `500`\n  - `cursor` to resume after the last row from the previous page\n- Invalid `limit` or `cursor` values return `400` with the standard `data_validation` payload.\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: finance_event_v1`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: <schema version>`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code: <partner code>`\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Mode: cursor_page` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Count: <row count>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Has-More: true|false` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Page-Limit: <effective limit>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Next-Cursor: <timestamp>|<id>` when another page is available\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n\n## Inbound Delivery Staging\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/inbound/<contract_code>/deliveries`\n- Method: `POST`\n- Request type: JSON object\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n  - optional `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key` to safely reuse the same staged delivery for matching retries\n- Request fields:\n  - `filename`\n  - `payload_base64`\n  - optional `notes`\n  - optional `source_reference`\n- Response header on every successful delivery request:\n  - `X-Federation-Delivery-Outcome: created|checksum_reuse|idempotency_replay`\n- Response headers when an idempotency key is supplied:\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key: <normalized key>`\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotent-Replay: true|false`\n- Response fields:\n  - `delivery_outcome` with `created`, `checksum_reuse`, or `idempotency_replay`\n  - delivery identity and current state\n  - partner and contract codes\n  - echoed `idempotency_key` when present\n  - payload checksum\n  - contract route hint\n- Duplicate handling:\n  - the same partner, contract, and payload checksum reuse the active staged\n    delivery while it remains in preview or approval flow and report\n    `delivery_outcome = checksum_reuse`\n  - the same partner, contract, and idempotency key replay the original delivery\n    across all states, report `delivery_outcome = idempotency_replay`, and\n    still return `400` if the key is reused for a different payload\n\n## Import Contracts\n\nReusable import templates are versioned backend template version:\n\n- `csv_v1`\n\nManaged inbound delivery policy:\n\n1. A subscribed partner posts a base64 payload to the inbound delivery route for\n  the relevant contract.\n2. The system stages a `federation.integration.delivery` record, deduplicates\n  active resubmissions by checksum, and can also bind an explicit idempotency\n  key to the request for safer client retries.\n3. If a data transformation is later required, it\nmust be introduced in a new reviewed migration with an explicit backfill and\nrollback plan; reinstalling the removed addon is not an approved rollback.\n\n## Backups\n\nThe upgrade script performs backups by default. It stores:\n\n- `modules.txt` with the exact install/upgrade module list\n- `<db>_<timestamp>.dump` as a PostgreSQL custom-format dump\n- `filestore_<db>_<timestamp>.tar.gz` when a filestore exists under\n  `./odoo-data/filestore/<db>`\n\nDo not use `--skip-backup` for production releases.\n\nRun the periodic restore drill against one of these backup directories before\nor during each release train using the restore checklist in this runbook:\n\n```bash\nbash addons/ci/restore_backup_drill.sh --backup-dir 2026-04-15_191410 --target-db odoo_restore_drill --dry-run\n```\n\n## Production Upgrade\n\nRun the upgrade and let the script restart the live Odoo service afterward so\nPython changes are loaded by the running web container:\n\n```bash\n./scripts/upgrade_sports_federation.sh --db odoo\n```\n\nFor a non-interactive upgrade that excludes demo data, use `--yes`. To include\nthe demo addon non-interactively, add `--install-demo`.\n\nThe script installs modules that are missing or uninstalled, upgrades modules\nthat are already installed, and restarts the Odoo service. It runs:\n\n- `odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d <db> -i <install_module_csv> -u <upgrade_module_csv> --stop-after-init`\n- `docker compose restart odoo`\n\nThe demo addon is excluded by default. Interactive runs ask whether\n`sports_federation_demo` should be installed. Use `--install-demo` when that\nchoice is intentional and the upgrade is non-interactive.\n\n## Post-Upgrade Verification\n\nVerify these operator checkpoints immediately after the upgrade:\n\n1. Open Federation > Reporting > Operator Checklist and confirm there are no\n   unexpected blocked queues.\n2. Open Federation > Reporting > Report Schedules and confirm there are no new\n   `Last Run Failed` schedules.\n3. Open Federation > Import Tools > Inbound Deliveries and confirm there are no\n   unexpected `failed` or `processed_with_errors` deliveries.\n4. Trigger one scheduled report manually from Federation > Reporting > Report\n   Schedules if the release touched reporting code.\n\n## Integration Partner Token Rotation\n\nAfter any release that modifies integration partner credentials, or on a\nscheduled rotation cycle, rotate partner tokens using the following procedure:\n\n**When to rotate:**\n- After upgrading `sports_federation_import_tools` (any release that changed\n  token storage, authentication, or the integration controller surface).\n- When the `token_rotation_required` flag is set to `True` on a partner record\n  (visible in Federation > Import Tools > Integration Partners).\n- On a periodic schedule — at minimum once per year or whenever a partner\n  personnel change occurs.\n\n**How to rotate (back-office procedure):**\n\n1. Open **Federation > Import Tools > Integration Partners**.\n2. Filter for partners where **Token Rotation Required** is checked, or where\n   **Last Rotated On** is older than the rotation policy window.\n3. For each partner, open the form and click **Rotate Token** (requires\n   Federation Manager group). Confirm the dialog.\n4. The wizard reveals the new raw token **once** (it cannot be retrieved again).\n   Copy it immediately and deliver it to the partner over a secure channel\n   (not email in plain text).\n5. The `token_rotation_required` flag clears automatically after a successful\n   rotation.\n\n**After a migration from plaintext storage:**\n\nIf `sports_federation_import_tools` was upgraded from a version prior to\n`19.0.1.2.0`, existing plaintext tokens were hashed in place and flagged for\nrotation by the post-migration script. Partners with `Token Rotation Required`\nset to `True` are still functional (their hashed token verifies correctly)\nbut should be rotated and re-issued at the next opportunity.\n\n**Verification:**\n\nAfter rotation, ask the partner to make one authenticated test call and confirm\na `200 OK` response to `/integration/v1/contracts`. A `401` response with\n`access_denied` indicates the token was not delivered correctly.\n\n## Rollback\n\nIf the upgrade must be rolled back:\n\n1. Stop or scale down the Odoo service to prevent new writes.\n2. Restore the PostgreSQL dump from the relevant backup directory.\n3. Restore the matching filestore archive.\n4. Restart the Odoo service.\n5. Re-run the post-upgrade verification checklist against the restored system.\n\nExample restore outline:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose stop odoo\ndropdb -U odoo odoo\ncreatedb -U odoo odoo\npg_restore -U odoo -d odoo backups/<timestamp>/odoo_<timestamp>.dump\ntar -xzf backups/<timestamp>/filestore_odoo_<timestamp>.tar.gz -C odoo-data/filestore\ndocker compose up -d odoo\n```\n\nAdjust database names and paths to match the selected backup directory.\n\n---\n\n## Upgrade Path Notes (per release train)\n\nThis section records DB migrations, new `ir.config_parameter` keys, deprecated\nfield removals, and module install order changes introduced in each release.\nAdd a subsection here for every release train that makes schema or behavioural\nchanges. Assign named officials or a club officiating duty and resolve shortages.\n7. Open match-day control, record results, and approve official results.\n8. Recompute and publish standings.\n9. This is deliberately\nseparate from the competition engine's `federation.stage.progression` model,\nwhich belongs to tournament-level progression workflows and uses a different\nrelation contract.\n\nBefore generating a structure, the graph is validated for cycles. Root stages\ncan then be prepared; dependent stages wait for incoming progression results.\nApproved fixture results can populate dependent stages, and frozen standings\nare stored as immutable snapshots.\n\nStage-graph access rules are loaded from `security/ir.model.access.csv`. The\nstructure form extension identifies the stage tab by its `stage_ids` field so\nthe view remains safe when translated page labels change.\n## Supported format generation\n\nThe format studio now estimates fixture and round counts before generation. It supports single and double leagues, seeded knockout and placement brackets, match series, pool-to-knockout configuration, and championship/relegation splits. Dynamic Swiss, ladder, and double-elimination formats are deliberately not advertised as automatic because they require round-by-round or reset-final semantics outside the immutable fixture graph.\n", "content_length": 1428, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_format/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "7c527aeced8da21ff2fd2701dc53c9ce8e9d1586b33b663b7efda898a87f43dc", "size_bytes": 1428}
+--+{"content": "# Sports Federation Format\n\nThe format addon manages versioned competition structures, their stages, and\nFormat Studio stage graphs.\n\n## Stage graph models\n\nFormat Studio uses `federation.structure.stage.progression` for edges between\nstages in one `federation.competition.structure`. This is deliberately\nseparate from the competition engine's `federation.stage.progression` model,\nwhich belongs to tournament-level progression workflows and uses a different\nrelation contract.\n\nBefore generating a structure, the graph is validated for cycles. Root stages\ncan then be prepared; dependent stages wait for incoming progression results.\nApproved fixture results can populate dependent stages, and frozen standings\nare stored as immutable snapshots.\n\nStage-graph access rules are loaded from `security/ir.model.access.csv`. The\nstructure form extension identifies the stage tab by its `stage_ids` field so\nthe view remains safe when translated page labels change.\n## Supported format generation\n\nThe format studio now estimates fixture and round counts before generation. It supports single and double leagues, seeded knockout and placement brackets, match series, pool-to-knockout configuration, championship/relegation splits, Swiss rounds, ladder formats, and power-of-two double elimination. Swiss round counts are configurable on the structure, while double elimination uses the dynamic pairing service to account for its winner, loser, and reset-final routes. These estimates are planning guidance; format-specific generation workflows remain responsible for validating the final fixture graph.\n", "content_length": 1599, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_format/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "a77ea3a8e64ed4bd839025fe8e3e21961d32e160ec3c607bd480eaa5b7eb539d", "size_bytes": 1599}

+-+ {"content": "# Competition Workflow Ownership\n\nThe ownership chain is the supported competition-planning architecture. No\nproduction data migration is required solely for this ownership clarification.\n\n## Capability ownership\n\n- Competition Core owns edition lifecycle and role assignments.\n- Registration owns entries and versioned finalized participant sets.\n- Format Studio owns stage topology, logical fixtures, standings snapshots, and progression.\n- Calendar owns physical match days, courts, and availability slots.\n- Scheduling owns fixture-to-slot assignments and fairness proposals.\n- Schedule Approval owns independent review and immutable publications.\n- Result Control owns the complete result lifecycle.\n- Match-Day Operations owns live execution and incidents.\n\n## Domain event contract\n\nEvents are past-tense facts. Producers emit only after a successful state change. Consumers must be idempotent and may not mutate the producer aggregate. Event payloads contain stable record IDs, version/revision, actor, and reason where applicable.\n\nRequired events: participant_set_finalized, structure_frozen, stage_standings_frozen, stage_progression_applied, matchday_capacity_ready, schedule_submitted, schedule_approved, schedule_published, matchday_opened, result_approved, result_contested, result_corrected, matchday_closed.\n", "content_length": 1325, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "docs/competition_engine_ownership.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "3352ecae7e79ab9a7fa5079eca2e62c212b65a59136effde4e6945b21563894c", "size_bytes": 1325}

+-- {"content": "# Sports Federation Governance\n\nFormal override-request workflow with decisions and audit trails. Provides a\nstructured way for federation officials to request, review, and implement\nexceptions to standard processes.\n\n## Purpose\n\nSome situations require bending the rules — late registrations, replayed matches,\nexceptional eligibility grants. This module ensures those exceptions are\n**requested, decided, logged, and auditable** rather than happening informally.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Core entities |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Player references |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournament references |\n| `mail` | Chatter |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.override.request`\n\nA formal request to override a standard process.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Request title |\n| `request_type` | Selection | Type of override |\n| `target_model` / `target_res_id` | Char / Integer | Linked record |\n| `requested_by_id` | Many2one | Requester (user) |\n| `requested_on` | Datetime | Request timestamp |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / submitted / approved / rejected / implemented / closed |\n| `reason` | Text | Justification |\n| `implementation_note` | Text | How it was applied |\n| `decision_ids` | One2many | Review decisions |\n| `audit_note_ids` | One2many | Audit trail entries |\n| `outcome_ids` | One2many | Post-decision outcome log |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → submitted → approved / rejected → implemented → closed, with submitted requests withdrawable back to draft before a decision is recorded.\n\n### `federation.override.decision`\n\nA review decision on an override request.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | The request |\n| `decision` | Selection | approve / reject / request_info |\n| `decided_by_id` | Many2one | Decision maker |\n| `decided_on` | Datetime | Decision timestamp |\n| `note` | Text | Reasoning |\n\n### `federation.audit.note`\n\nFree-form audit notes attached to an override request.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | The request |\n| `note` | Text | Audit remark |\n| `author_id` | Many2one | Author |\n| `created_on` | Datetime | Timestamp |\n\n### `federation.override.outcome`\n\nOutcome tracking row attached to an override request after implementation or\nfollow-up review.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | Source override request |\n| `outcome` | Selection | implemented / effective / partial / ineffective / reversed |\n| `outcome_on` | Datetime | When the outcome was recorded |\n| `recorded_by_id` | Many2one | Operator recording the outcome |\n| `request_type` | Selection | Snapshot of the originating request type |\n| `target_model` / `target_res_id` | Char / Integer | Snapshot of the overridden record |\n| `request_state` | Selection | Request state at the time of logging |\n| `note` | Text | Outcome commentary |\n\n## Security Groups\n\n| Group | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| Governance Officer | Can review and decide on override requests |\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Formal request lifecycle** — Every exception starts as a draft request,\n   can be withdrawn back to draft while still submitted, and otherwise follows\n   a structured approval flow.\n2. **Multi-decision support** — Multiple governance officers can weigh in on a\n   single request.\n3. **Audit trail** — All decisions and notes are timestamped and attributed.\n4. **Generic target** — Requests can link to any record type via model/res_id.\n5. **Outcome evidence** — implemented requests now create outcome-log rows so\n   governance review can extend beyond the approval moment.\n", "content_length": 3754, +-  {"content": "# Sports Federation Club Roles and Portal\n\nVersion: 19.0.4.1.0\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nRole-oriented self-service portal for club representatives, officials, and tournament operators.\n\n## Primary user journeys\n\n### Club representative\n\n- manage club teams and players\n- submit season and tournament registrations\n- prepare and activate rosters\n- complete match sheets and readiness tasks\n- nominate officials\n- review result actions and deadlines\n\n### Official\n\n- view assignments\n- confirm or decline within the authorized scope\n- access relevant match information\n\n### Tournament operator\n\n- use the tournament operations board\n- monitor courts, matches, readiness, and action queues\n- execute scoped result and operational actions\n\n## Trust boundary\n\nAll privileged portal writes must use a model-owned method and the shared `federation.portal.privilege` boundary. Controllers validate input and resolve scope but do not perform raw elevated business writes. See `adr/0001-portal-trust-boundaries.md`.\n\nEvery new privileged route requires:\n\n1. positive in-scope coverage\n2. negative out-of-scope coverage\n3. direct-ID or guessed-record coverage\n4. model/helper ownership assertions when elevation is used\n5. CSRF enforcement for state-changing browser or JSON-RPC routes\n\n## Portal UX direction\n\nThe landing page should remain task-first. Common tasks are teams, registrations, upcoming matches, and action items. Specialist tools should be progressively disclosed instead of presented as an undifferentiated module catalogue.\n\n## Operations board\n\nThe board loads through scoped JSON-RPC, supports polling and structured failures, and exposes only matches and actions available to the current user. Server-side checks remain authoritative.\n\n## Tests\n\nThe module includes HTTP smoke, ownership, access-denied, team, player, roster, registration, officiating, result, accessibility, mobile, operations-board, and end-to-end portal workflow tests.\n\n## Consolidated documentation\n\n`PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_COVERAGE.md`, `PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_TEST_MATRIX.md`, and `ROADMAP_RC.md` are deleted. Their durable rules are consolidated here and in ADR-0001; the test files are the authoritative live coverage map.\n\n## competition portal\n\nThe active competition portal is edition-based. Participation comes from\ncompetition entries and finalized participant sets. Match-day schedule data is\nrendered only from each match day's current live publication. Draft schedules,\nreview evidence and superseded publications are intentionally unavailable.\n\nPrimary routes:\n\n- `/my/competitions`\n- `/my/competition-entries`\n- `/my/match-days`\n- `/sports/match-days/<id>/operations`\n\nLegacy tournament workspace routes are redirect-only and render no V1 data.\nThe backend tournament-registration action is loaded before the menus that use\nit, so a fresh module install and an upgrade both build the registration menu\nwithout relying on stale database metadata.\n\n\n## Accessible error recovery and focus management\n\nPortal forms move keyboard focus to server-rendered error summaries, connect\ninvalid controls to that summary with `aria-describedby`, and announce the\nsummary through an assertive live region. Bootstrap confirmation dialogs move\nfocus into the dialog and restore it to the invoking control when closed.\nKeyboard focus uses a visible outline that does not depend on color-only status\ncues. The focused accessibility suite covers these contracts together with\nmobile table and action wrapping.\n", "content_length": 3540, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_portal/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "3ea4f6e8c7c0686f04a9a5a78e3b76b66861847771f9655441258519bd4016a5", "size_bytes": 3540}

+-+-{"content": "Sports Federation Standings\n===========================\n\nComputes and stores league-style standings tables for tournament stages and\ngroups. Aggregates match results into a ranked table with points, wins,\nlosses, goal differences, and configurable tie-break ordering.\n\nPurpose\n-------\n\nProvides a snapshot of competition standings that can be published, audited,\nand used by downstream modules such as the public site, reporting, and\nqualification logic. Standings are linked to rule sets to ensure consistent\nscoring and tie resolution.\n\nDependencies\n------------\n\n- ``sports_federation_tournament``: Tournaments, stages, groups, and matches.\n- ``sports_federation_rules``: Rule sets for scoring and tie-breaks.\n- ``mail``: Chatter integration.\n\nModels\n------\n\n``federation.standing``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA standings table for a specific scope such as a tournament, stage, or group.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Standings title.\n- ``tournament_id`` (Many2one): Tournament.\n- ``stage_id`` (Many2one): Optional stage scope.\n- ``group_id`` (Many2one): Optional group scope.\n- ``competition_id`` (Many2one): Competition context.\n- ``rule_set_id`` (Many2one): Scoring and tie-break rules.\n- ``state`` (Selection): ``draft``, ``computed``, or ``frozen``.\n- ``line_ids`` (One2many): Ranked team entries.\n- ``line_count`` (Integer): Stat-button counter.\n- ``computed_on`` (Datetime): When the table was last computed.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Additional notes.\n\nState machine:\n\n- ``draft -> computed -> frozen``.\n\n``federation.standing.line``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nOne row per participant in the standings table.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``standing_id`` (Many2one): Parent standings.\n- ``participant_id`` (Many2one): The team.\n- ``rank`` (Integer): Position in the standings table (1 = first).\n- ``played`` (Integer): Total matches played.\n- ``won`` / ``drawn`` / ``lost`` (Integer): Results breakdown.\n- ``score_for`` / ``score_against`` (Integer): Goals/points scored and conceded.\n- ``score_diff`` (Integer, computed): ``score_for - score_against``.\n- ``points`` (Integer): Total points per rule set.\n- ``note`` (Char): Short free-text remark for this line.\n- ``tiebreak_notes`` (Text, readonly): Auto-generated explanation of the tie-break criterion used to order this participant.\n\n``federation.standing.recompute.job``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nAsynchronous recompute queue record used for background standings updates.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``standing_id`` (Many2one): Target standing to recompute.\n- ``idempotency_key`` (Char): Replay-safe key for deduplicating repeated queue requests.\n- ``correlation_id`` (Char): Trace identifier propagated through queue processing.\n- ``state`` (Selection): ``pending``, ``running``, ``done``, or ``failed``.\n- ``attempt_count`` / ``max_attempts`` (Integer): Retry control metadata.\n- ``requested_on`` / ``started_on`` / ``completed_on`` (Datetime): Lifecycle timestamps.\n- ``next_retry_on`` (Datetime): Retry schedule for failed jobs.\n- ``last_error`` (Text): Last failure reason captured for operators.\n\nKey Behaviours\n--------------\n\n- **Rule-set driven scoring**: points are calculated using the attached rule\n   set and its configured win, draw, and loss values.\n- **Tie-break resolution**: when teams have equal points, tie-break rules from\n   the rule set are applied in sequence order.\n- **Snapshot model**: each standings record is a point-in-time computation,\n   allowing historical comparison.\n- **Official-result filtering**: when ``sports_federation_result_control`` is\n   installed, only matches with ``include_in_official_standings = True`` are\n   counted.\n- **Freeze behavior**: frozen standings reject recomputation unless\n   ``force_recompute`` is provided in context.\n- **Auto-advance hook**: freezing a standing can trigger pending\n   ``federation.stage.progression`` rules with ``auto_advance = True``.\n- **Publication is separate**: public visibility is handled by\n   ``sports_federation_public_site`` through ``website_published``, not by a\n   dedicated published standings state.\n- **Optional queued recompute**: standings can be recomputed asynchronously via\n   ``federation.standing.recompute.job`` and the\n   ``action_queue_recompute`` button.\n- **Idempotent queue requests**: repeated queue requests with the same\n   ``idempotency_key`` replay the original job instead of creating duplicates.\n- **Queue visibility**: pending and failed queue counters are surfaced directly\n   on the standing form, with a dedicated queue action and menu entry.\n\n## Migration note (v19.0.1.2.0)\n\n- Adds ``federation.standing.recompute.job`` for asynchronous, idempotent\n   standings recompute processing.\n- Adds queue cron ``Standings: Process Recompute Queue``.\n\n## Recompute job recovery\n\nStanding recompute jobs use bounded exponential retry. Exhausted jobs move to `Needs operator action`, preserve the correlation ID and error evidence, and can be explicitly returned to the queue by a manager. The queue cron also recovers jobs left in `running` after a worker interruption.\n", "content_length": 5027, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_standings/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "fac9e6593f4665d79b936eb12082894d8ee14db0fedb13c468f646ae81dda197", "size_bytes": 5027}

Patterns**\n- **Module split**: `sports_federation_base` (master data), `sports_federation_tournament` (tournaments, matches, participants), `sports_federation_format / sports_federation_scheduling` (service/wizards), plus domain modules (`people`, `rules`, `officiating`, `rosters`, `result_control`, `public_site`, `reporting`, `finance_bridge`, `venues`, `discipline`, `standings`, ...).\n- **Model naming**: Domain models use the `federation.` prefix (e.g. `federation.player`, `federation.match`).\n- **Common patterns**: `ir.sequence` for identifiers, `state` selection fields for workflows, wizards for batch operations (under `wizards/`), `controllers/` for portal/website endpoints, and `security/` for groups/record rules/ACLs.\n\n**Key Files & Where To Look**\n- **High-level sports_federation_scheduling` (no persistent models if not required).\n- **Add a controller / portal flow**: use `controllers/` and add templates under `views/` or `templates/`; respect portal record rules (see `sports_federation_portal`).\n- **Security**: always add or update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and any `security/*.xml` groups/rules for new models or new endpoints.\n- **Manifest hygiene**: update `__manifest__.py` `depends`, `data`, and `version` fields when introducing DB changes or new data files.\n\n**Testing & Local Run**\n- **Where tests live**: `odoo/<module>/tests/` when present (some modules include unit/functional tests).\n- **Run module tests**: use the Odoo test runner for module-level tests (e.g. `odoo-bin -d <db> -i <module> --test-enable`) or your established local development workflow.\n- **Release sanity**: include at least one focused test for new business logic (especially schedule generation, result pipeline, and state transitions).\n\n**PR Checklist (required before merge)**\n- **Tests**: Add/adjust tests covering the new behaviour.\n- **Security**: Update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and add group/record-rule XML if necessary.\n- **Manifest**: Add new data files to `__manifest__.py` `data` list and ensure `depends` are correct.\n-- **Docs**: Update or add a short README in the module and, if behaviour changes, update the relevant `odoo/_workflows` file.\n- **Small, focused commits**: Prefer atomic commits (one logical change per commit) and descriptive commit messages.\n\n**How Copilot Should Help (recommended prompts & behaviour)**\n- **Primary rule**: Prefer conservative, minimal changes that keep module boundaries intact. Avoid touching unrelated modules unless absolutely required and explain why.\n- **When asked to implement a model change**: return a plan and a single patch that includes: the `models/<file>.py` change, `models/__init__.py` export, `security/ir.model.access.csv` entry, `views/*.xml` (if UI), `__manifest__.py` update, and a new test under `tests/` that exercises the main logic.\n- **When asked to add a wizard or generator**: create a transient model in `wizards/`, a wizard view, and a small deterministic example in tests that demonstrates expected output (e.g. round-robin schedule for 4 participants).\n- **When asked about business rules or workflows**: consult and reference the Workflow docs in `odoo/_workflows` and the `TECHNICAL_NOTE.md` to ensure behaviour matches the documented flows.\n\n**Example prompts you can give Copilot in this repo**\n- **Add a model**: \"Add a new persistent model `federation.referee` with fields `name`, `certification_level`, `active`; add ACLs, a basic tree/form view, and unit tests. Show me the patch with files changed.\"\n- **Create a wizard**: \"Create a `round_robin_wizard` that generates matches for a stage; include wizard model, view, manifest update, and a unit test verifying match count for 4 teams.\"\n- **Fix workflow behaviour**: \"Investigate why standings recompute includes contested results; propose a minimal fix and tests to prevent contested results from being counted.\"\n\n**Notes & Expectations**\n- **Authoritative sources**: the `_workflows` documents and `TECHNICAL_NOTE.md` are the source of truth for business behaviour—use them before changing workflows.\n- **Keep modules decoupled**: the architecture intentionally separates `base`, `tournament`, and the `competition_engine` service; prefer adding features in the appropriate module.\n- **Ask clarifying questions**: if a requested feature impacts tournament rules, scheduling, or publication flows, ask which workflow (`_workflows/*.md`) should govern the behaviour.\n\n**Documentation Maintenance (required)**\n\n- **Always update docs**: For any code, data model, view, workflow, or behaviour change, update the relevant documentation files in this repository as part of the same change set (or in a linked follow-up PR). Format freezes a structure. Calendar prepares physical capacity. Scheduling submits a complete schedule. Approval publishes an immutable snapshot. Match-day operations execute only a published snapshot.\n\n## Migration policy\n\nThe legacy monolithic engine has been removed from the addon set. New and existing operational flows use the ownership split. Databases upgraded from a release that installed the legacy addon require the normal reviewed upgrade/migration procedure before production rollout; do not silently reinterpret existing production records.\n\n\n## Schedule handoff operator handoff\n\nThe operator path is fully exposed in the backend: Schedule Planner submits a\nvalidated revision, Schedule Review Queue provides independent request-changes\nor approval decisions, Publication exposes approved schedules and immutable\npublication history, and Match-Day Operations consumes only the current live\npublication. Submission creates its pending review atomically when the approval\naddon is installed; there is no operator-visible intermediate state that\nrequires a separate \"start review\" action.\n\n## Phases 5.1.1 to 5.3: publication and live operations\n\nSchedule review decisions are command-only: ACLs are read-only and the review\nmodel rejects direct decision-field writes. Live publications are scoped and\nversioned per match day. Publication replacement uses a dedicated wizard,\nrequires a replacement reason, locks the match day during version allocation,\nand rejects stale confirmations.\n\nMatch-Day Control exposes readiness, the exact live publication, published\nmatches, court state, incidents, immutable sessions and operational deviations.\nOpening a day freezes the publication digest in a session. Live moves, delays,\npostponements and cancellations update only operational match fields; the\napproved publication and `published_slot_id` remain immutable. Every deviation\nrecords actor, reason, old/new slot, session and publication, and emits an audit\nevent.\n", "content_length": 2809, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "COMPETITION_ENGINE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "2c6a2ef0be5e1aece6060a09b33b5da37b58fc1a0bca7e3604aa9cde951df0b0", "size_bytes": 2809}

Integration keys can be copied from `ci/integrations.env.example` or provided by your shell environment.\n\n## Focused test commands\n\nRun targeted suites for the main maintained flows:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite portal_public_ops\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite finance_reporting\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite rosters_readiness_guard\n```\n\nRun an individual module when you only need a narrow slice:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_result_control\n```\n\nList the named suites from the runner itself:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --list-suites\n```\n\n## Pre-push checks\n\nBefore release qualification, commit or intentionally discard all tracked\nchanges and remove generated runtime configuration. The RC preflight enforces\nthat the candidate can be reproduced from its commit:\n\n```bash\nscripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh preflight\n```\n\nRun the normal development checks afterward:\n\n```bash\nblack --check sports_federation_base sports_federation_tournament sports_federation_standings sports_federation_venues sports_federation_portal sports_federation_public_site ci\nflake8 sports_federation_base sports_federation_tournament sports_federation_standings sports_federation_venues sports_federation_portal sports_federation_public_site ci\nbash -n ci/run_tests.sh\nbash -n ci/apply_env_to_ir_config.sh\nbash -n ci/restore_backup_drill.sh\npython3 ci/check_doc_freshness.py\npython3 ci/check_markdown_links.py\npython3 ci/check_module_owners.py\npython3 ci/check_openapi_contracts.py\npython3 ci/check_release_train.py\npython3 ci/check_explain_snapshots.py\npython3 ci/check_ci_hygiene.py\npython3 ci/check_workflow_state_contracts.py\npython3 ci/check_module_dependency_drift.py\nbash ci/prune_ci_logs.sh 30\n```\n\n## CI/CD Pipeline\n\n### Named test suites\n\nThe CI runner groups modules into named suites for focused feedback. Use the\nsuite that covers the area you changed:\n\n| Suite | Modules covered |\n|---|---|\n| `competition_core` | Base, tournament, scheduling, results, standings critical path |\n| `portal_public_ops` | Portal ownership, public routes, compliance, standings, venue-facing flows |\n| `finance_reporting` | Finance bridge and reporting coverage |\n| `rosters_readiness_guard` | Participant readiness regression and discovery gate |\n| `release_surfaces` | Broader portal/public, match-day, compliance, notification release verification |\n| `people_rosters_rules` | People, rosters, rules, and officiating modules |\n| `ops_and_notifications` | Discipline, governance, notifications, import_tools, demo modules |\n\n```bash\n# Run a named suite\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n\n# Run a single module (fastest for narrow changes)\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_standings\n\n# Run everything (use before merging)\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh\n\n# List suites\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --list-suites\n```\n\n### Reading CI output\n\nThe runner prints a results block at the end:\n\n```\n════════════════════════════════\n  RESULTS\n════════════════════════════════\n  Exit code:     0\n  Tests run:     62\n  Tests passed:  62\n  Tests failed:  0\n  Test errors:   0\n════════════════════════════════\n```\n\nA non-zero exit code means failure. Find the cause:\n\n```bash\n# Show failing test names and tracebacks\ndocker logs <container> 2>&1 | grep -A 20 \"FAIL\\|ERROR\\|Traceback\"\n```\n\nThe container name is printed by `docker compose ps` or appears in the runner\noutput as `sf_ci-ci-odoo-run-<hash>`.\n\n### CI gate stages\n\n1. **Module install** — all declared modules install without error.\n2. **Test run** — `TransactionCase` and `HttpCase` tests execute.\n3. **Query-count checks** — `assertQueryCount` assertions verify no N+1\n   regressions were introduced.\n4. **EXPLAIN snapshots** — `ci/check_explain_snapshots.py` compares query\n   plans against stored baselines.\n5. **Doc freshness checks** — `ci/check_doc_freshness.py`, `check_markdown_links.py`,\n   `check_module_owners.py`, `check_openapi_contracts.py` verify documentation\n   and contracts are up to date.\n6. **Workflow contract checks** — `ci/check_workflow_state_contracts.py` verifies\n   that documented lifecycle states and required workflow actions stay aligned\n   with model declarations.\n\n### Workflow contract map upkeep\n\n- Keep `_workflows/contracts/workflow_state_contracts.json` aligned with each\n  canonical workflow markdown and model state source.\n- If CI reports undocumented states, either add the state to the matching\n  workflow markdown and contract entry or remove/rename the code state.\n- If CI reports missing actions, add the action method in code with the\n  expected guardrails or update the contract when the workflow changed by design.\n\n### Iterating on a failing test\n\n```bash\n# 1. Make your code change\n# 2. Run only the affected module\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_<name>\n# 3. If it passes, run the full suite before pushing\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite <suite>\n```\n\nKeep the `--keep` flag to leave the Docker stack running between iterations\n(avoids paying the container startup cost each run):\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_standings --keep\n# ... fix code ...\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_standings --keep\n```\n\nUse `--keep-on-failure` for automatic cleanup on success and retained\ncontainers/database/filestore/configuration on failure. For fast UI work use\n`--frontend-module`; for cross-module safety use\n`--affected-from origin/main --include-dependents`. Workspace contracts can be\ncombined with:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_competition_contracts\n```\n\n### Pre-push checks\n\nBefore pushing, run the static checks locally to avoid a CI round-trip:\n\n```bash\nblack --check sports_federation_base sports_federation_tournament \\\n      sports_federation_standings sports_federation_venues \\\n      sports_federation_portal sports_federation_public_site ci\nflake8 sports_federation_base sports_federation_tournament \\\n       sports_federation_standings sports_federation_venues \\\n       sports_federation_portal sports_federation_public_site ci\nbash -n ci/run_tests.sh\npython3 ci/check_doc_freshness.py\npython3 ci/check_markdown_links.py\npython3 ci/check_module_owners.py\npython3 ci/check_openapi_contracts.py\npython3 ci/check_release_train.py\npython3 ci/check_explain_snapshots.py\npython3 ci/check_module_dependency_drift.py\npython3 ci/check_migration_review.py\npython3 ci/check_constraint_index_contracts.py\n```\n\n## Documentation expectations\n\n- Update the relevant module README for behavior or schema changes.\n- Update the matching workflow under `_workflows/` when business behavior changes.\n- Keep `TECHNICAL_NOTE.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `INTEGRATION_CONTRACTS.md`, and `STATE_AND_OWNERSHIP_MATRIX.md` aligned when the change affects their scope.\n- Update `MODULE_OWNERS.yaml` whenever a new addon is introduced or primary module ownership changes.\n- Update `DATA_RETENTION_POLICY.md` when a change modifies cleanup scope or retention windows for logs, staged deliveries, or generated report files.\n- Update the relevant record under `adr/` when a change revises portal trust boundaries, reporting SQL-view policy, or public route ownership.\n\n## Module implementation checklist\n\nWhen adding an addon or persistent model, keep the change complete and\ninstallable:\n\n- Declare direct dependencies and every XML/CSV file in `__manifest__.py`.\n- Export model, wizard, and controller packages from their `__init__.py` files.\n- Add ACLs and record rules for every new model; check company and portal scope.\n- Add a module README, focused regression test, and workflow update when the\n  change introduces a business state or user journey.\n- For a new module, use the standard layout: `models/`, `security/`, `views/`,\n  optional `data/`, `wizards/`, `controllers/`, and `tests/`. Do not create\n  empty directories.\n\n## Migration review checklist\n\nFor model, view, controller, security, or ownership changes, record the\naffected modules and release train, then verify:\n\n- schema, backfill, index, view, route, and ACL implications are understood;\n- `python3 ci/check_migration_review.py --base-ref origin/main` passes;\n- the migration dry-run command and result are recorded in\n  `RELEASE_RUNBOOK.md`;\n- rollback triggers, backup requirements, and any SQL reversal are recorded in\n  the same runbook;\n- the affected module tests and the relevant full suite pass.\n\n## Architecture summary\n\nThe dependency direction is `base → tournament → competition_core → registration → format → calendar → scheduling`, followed\nby domain modules such as people, rules, rosters, officiating, results,\nstandings, compliance, discipline, governance, venues, and finance. Portal,\npublic-site, notification, reporting, and import modules are integration or\nsurface layers. -+ {"content": "# Integration Contracts\n\nLast updated: 2026-08-20\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nThis document defines the stable partner-facing contracts currently supported by\nthe federation platform and the policy used to version, evolve, and deprecate\nthem.\n\nMachine-readable partner route definitions live in `openapi/integration_v1.yaml`.\nKeep the OpenAPI file, this document, and the route implementations aligned in\nthe same change set whenever a managed integration contract changes.\n\n## Contract Principles\n\n- Every external export or feed must expose an explicit contract identifier.\n- Version changes must be additive within a version whenever possible.\n- Breaking schema changes require a new contract version rather than silent\n  mutation of an existing response.\n- Deprecated routes or payloads remain available for at least one supported\n  release cycle after the replacement contract is published, unless security or\n  legal requirements force a faster removal.\n- Contract changes must be reflected in code, tests where applicable, this\n  document, and the roadmap or release notes in the same change set.\n\n## Authentication Strategy\n\nPublic tournament contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"`\n- intended for website visitors, public calendars, and read-only partner\n  consumption\n\nOperator-authenticated reporting exports:\n\n- `auth=\"user\"`\n- require an authenticated backend session\n- intended for federation operators using backend actions and reporting screens\n\nManaged partner contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"` routes protected by partner credentials\n- require `X-Federation-Partner-Code` and `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- enforce per-partner contract subscriptions before a payload is served or a\n  delivery is accepted\n- intended for explicit machine-to-machine integrations without sharing backend\n  user sessions\n\nImport contracts:\n\n- executed either through backend import wizards or through managed partner\n  delivery staging before entering the same wizard flow\n- guarded by dry-run preview, governance-job approval, and checksum matching for\n  live imports\n\n## Public Contracts\n\n## Tournament Feed\n\n- Canonical route: `/api/v1/tournaments/<slug>/feed`\n- Compatibility routes:\n  - `/api/v1/tournaments/<id>/feed`\n  - `/api/v1/competitions/<id>/feed`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_feed`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: v1`\n- Payload anchor:\n  - top-level `api_version = \"v1\"`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - top-level keys in the v1 payload are stable\n  - additive nested fields are allowed in v1 when they do not alter existing\n    semantics\n\n## Tournament Schedule Calendar\n\n- Canonical route: `/tournaments/<slug>/schedule.ics`\n- Compatibility route: `/tournament/<id>/schedule.ics`\n- Response type: `text/calendar`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_schedule_ics`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: ics_v1`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - calendar structure stays compatible with standard ICS consumers\n  - field enrichment should be additive inside event descriptions, not a change\n    to the ICS envelope\n\n## Authenticated CSV Contracts\n\nAll authenticated CSV exports expose these headers:\n\n- `X-Federation-Contract`\n- `X-Federation-Contract-Version`\n\n## Standings Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/standings/<tournament_id>`\n- Contract: `standings_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n- Notes:\n  - intended for downstream standings review and board-pack style extracts\n\n## Participation Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/participation/<season_id>`\n- Contract: `participation_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Summary Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance`\n- Contract: `finance_summary_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Event Handoff Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance/events`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Versioning anchor:\n  - detailed finance-event handoff rows expose a schema version column and the\n    matching response header contract version\n- Required handoff fields include:\n  - event identity and state\n  - handoff state\n  - fee type and amount\n  - invoice, external, accounting-batch, and reconciliation references\n  - source traceability\n  - exported, reconciled, and closed timestamps\n\n## Managed Partner Contracts\n\n## Contract Manifest\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/contracts`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- Payload includes:\n  - contract code, version, direction, transport, and route hint\n  - deprecation stage and replacement contract\n  - `available` flag for database-specific operational availability\n  - partner subscription state and last-used timestamp\n\n## Partner Finance Event Handoff\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`\n- Response type: `text/csv`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Optional query parameters:\n  - `limit` to request one bounded page of rows; defaults to `200` and caps at `500`\n  - `cursor` to resume after the last row from the previous page\n- Invalid `limit` or `cursor` values return `400` with the standard `data_validation` payload.\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: finance_event_v1`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: <schema version>`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code: <partner code>`\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Mode: cursor_page` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Count: <row count>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Has-More: true|false` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Page-Limit: <effective limit>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Next-Cursor: <timestamp>|<id>` when another page is available\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n\n## Inbound Delivery Staging\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/inbound/<contract_code>/deliveries`\n- Method: `POST`\n- Request type: JSON object\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n  - optional `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key` to safely reuse the same staged delivery for matching retries\n- Request fields:\n  - `filename`\n  - `payload_base64`\n  - optional `notes`\n  - optional `source_reference`\n- Response header on every successful delivery request:\n  - `X-Federation-Delivery-Outcome: created|checksum_reuse|idempotency_replay`\n- Response headers when an idempotency key is supplied:\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key: <normalized key>`\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotent-Replay: true|false`\n- Response fields:\n  - `delivery_outcome` with `created`, `checksum_reuse`, or `idempotency_replay`\n  - delivery identity and current state\n  - partner and contract codes\n  - echoed `idempotency_key` when present\n  - payload checksum\n  - contract route hint\n- Duplicate handling:\n  - the same partner, contract, and payload checksum reuse the active staged\n    delivery while it remains in preview or approval flow and report\n    `delivery_outcome = checksum_reuse`\n  - the same partner, contract, and idempotency key replay the original delivery\n    across all states, report `delivery_outcome = idempotency_replay`, and\n    still return `400` if the key is reused for a different payload\n\n## Import Contracts\n\nReusable import templates are versioned backend contracts and live under\n`federation.import.template`.\n\nCurrent template codes:\n\n- `clubs_csv`\n- `players_csv`\n- `seasons_csv`\n- `teams_csv`\n- `tournament_participants_csv`\n\nCurrent template version:\n\n- `csv_v1`\n\nManaged inbound delivery policy:\n\n1. A subscribed partner posts a base64 payload to the inbound delivery route for\n  the relevant contract.\n2. The system stages a `federation.integration.delivery` record, deduplicates\n  active resubmissions by checksum, and can also bind an explicit idempotency\n  key to the request for safer client retries.\n3. Operators open the staged delivery in the matching import wizard for preview.\n4. Approval and live execution continue through the standard governance-job\n  workflow already used for manual rollover imports.\n\nLive import policy:\n\n1. Run a dry-run preview for the uploaded CSV.\n2. Request approval, which creates a governance job tied to the file checksum,\n   target model, template, and preview results.\n3. Approve the governance job.\n4. Execute the live import only if the CSV checksum and selected template still\n   match the approved job.\n\nVerification policy:\n\n- governance jobs store preview totals, execution totals, and before/after\n  target-model record counts\n- live imports that partially succeed remain visible as\n  `completed_with_errors`\n- staged partner deliveries mirror preview, approval, completion, and failure\n  states so operators can reconcile inbound handoffs without leaving the app\n\n## Versioning Policy\n\n- Public JSON versions are encoded in both the path and the payload.\n- CSV and ICS contracts use stable routes plus explicit response headers.\n- Import templates use a version field on the template and a matching schema\n  snapshot on the governance job.\n- Breaking changes require a new contract identifier or version rather than a\n  silent replacement.\n\nEndpoint compatibility policy (v1):\n\n- `/integration/v1/contracts`: additive response changes only; remove fields\n  only in a new API version.\n- `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`: keep CSV column order and header\n  semantics stable for `finance_event_v1` until a new contract code/version is\n  published.\n- `/integration/v1/inbound/{contract_code}/deliveries`: keep\n  `delivery_outcome` semantics (`created`, `checksum_reuse`,\n  `idempotency_replay`) stable within v1.\n- JSON error envelopes for all managed integration endpoints must preserve the\n  typed shape `{error, error_code, correlation_id}` across minor releases.\n\nPartner onboarding references:\n\n- Golden request/response examples: `openapi/examples/INTEGRATION_GOLDEN_EXAMPLES.md`.\n- CI contract guardrails: `ci/check_openapi_contracts.py`.\n\n## Deprecation Policy\n\nThe working list of compatibility aliases, owners, review dates, and target\nsunset dates is maintained here and must be updated in the same change set as\nany contract-facing deprecation decision.\n\n| Surface | Canonical replacement | Target exit |\n|---|---|---|\n| `/tournaments`, `/tournaments/<slug>`, numeric tournament page routes | `/competitions`, `/competitions/<edition-slug>` | 2026-10-01 |\n| Numeric public tournament page routes | Edition routes under `/competitions/<edition-slug>` | 2026-10-01 |\n| Numeric or competition-named v1 tournament feeds | `/api/v1/tournaments/<slug>/feed` | 2026-10-01 |\n| Player import `name` column fallback | Explicit `first_name`, `last_name` columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Team import name fallbacks | `club_code` and explicit team naming columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Participant import tournament/team name fallbacks | `tournament_code` and `team_code` | 2026-10-15 |\n\nRemove a compatibility surface only after its replacement is documented,\ncovered by tests, and announced in the owning module README. If a target date\npasses without a removal decision, extend it here with the reason.\n\n- Slug-based public routes are canonical.\n- Numeric public routes remain compatibility shims and should not be used for\n  new integrations.\n- Legacy competition-named public feed routes remain compatibility aliases for\n  the tournament feed and are considered deprecated in favor of the canonical\n  tournament path.\n- Older CSV shapes should remain available for one supported release cycle once\n  a replacement contract is published.\n- Removals must be announced by updating this file, relevant READMEs, and the\n  roadmap in the same release window.\n\n## Integration configuration\n\nCI and local development use environment variables for SMTP, OAuth, partner\ntokens, webhooks, and object storage. Copy `ci/integrations.env.example` to\n`ci/.env`; never commit credentials. The CI helper writes non-empty values to\nOdoo system parameters with the `integration.` prefix, including:\n\n- `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_USE_TLS`,\n  `EMAIL_FROM`;\n- `SENDGRID_API_KEY`, `MAILGUN_API_KEY`;\n- `OAUTH_GOOGLE_*`, `OAUTH_GITHUB_*`;\n- `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`;\n- `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `S3_BUCKET`, `S3_REGION`;\n- `ALLOWED_HOSTS`.\n\nRead global parameters through `ir.config_parameter` and do not log secret\nvalues. Upload malware scanning, when enabled, uses\n`sports_federation.attachment_scan.command` and\n`sports_federation.attachment_scan.timeout_seconds`; exit code `0` means clean,\n`10` means infected, and any other non-zero code means verification failed.\n\n## Notification matrix\n\nThe notification dispatcher is non-blocking and records delivery outcomes in\n`federation.notification.log`. Business actions trigger the following current\nnotifications:\n\n| Event | Recipient or audience | Channel |\n|---|---|---|\n| Season registration confirmed or returned | Submitting representative or club contact | Email |\n| Tournament published | Participant club and team contacts | Email |\n| Participant confirmed | Team and club contacts | Email |\n| Result submitted | Result validators | Activity |\n| Result approved or contested | Team/club contacts; managers for contests | Email |\n| Standing frozen | Participant club contacts | Email |\n| Finance event confirmed | Partner or club/player/referee contact | Email |\n| Referee assigned | Referee | Email |\n| Overdue referee confirmation or officiating shortage | Federation managers | Activity |\n\nDelivery failures must not roll back the business transaction. If a data transformation is later required, it\nmust be introduced in a new reviewed migration with an explicit backfill and\nrollback plan; reinstalling the removed addon is not an approved rollback.\n\n## Backups\n\nThe upgrade script performs backups by default. It stores:\n\n- `modules.txt` with the exact install/upgrade module list\n- `<db>_<timestamp>.dump` as a PostgreSQL custom-format dump\n- `filestore_<db>_<timestamp>.tar.gz` when a filestore exists under\n  `./odoo-data/filestore/<db>`\n\nDo not use `--skip-backup` for production releases.\n\nRun the periodic restore drill against one of these backup directories before\nor during each release train using the restore checklist in this runbook:\n\n```bash\nbash addons/ci/restore_backup_drill.sh --backup-dir 2026-04-15_191410 --target-db odoo_restore_drill --dry-run\n```\n\n## Production Upgrade\n\nRun the upgrade and let the script restart the live Odoo service afterward so\nPython changes are loaded by the running web container:\n\n```bash\n./scripts/upgrade_sports_federation.sh --db odoo\n```\n\nFor a non-interactive upgrade that excludes demo data, use `--yes`. To include\nthe demo addon non-interactively, add `--install-demo`.\n\nThe script installs modules that are missing or uninstalled, upgrades modules\nthat are already installed, and restarts the Odoo service. It runs:\n\n- `odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d <db> -i <install_module_csv> -u <upgrade_module_csv> --stop-after-init`\n- `docker compose restart odoo`\n\nThe demo addon is excluded by default. Interactive runs ask whether\n`sports_federation_demo` should be installed. Use `--install-demo` when that\nchoice is intentional and the upgrade is non-interactive.\n\n## Post-Upgrade Verification\n\nVerify these operator checkpoints immediately after the upgrade:\n\n1. Open Federation > Reporting > Operator Checklist and confirm there are no\n   unexpected blocked queues.\n2. Open Federation > Reporting > Report Schedules and confirm there are no new\n   `Last Run Failed` schedules.\n3. Open Federation > Import Tools > Inbound Deliveries and confirm there are no\n   unexpected `failed` or `processed_with_errors` deliveries.\n4. Trigger one scheduled report manually from Federation > Reporting > Report\n   Schedules if the release touched reporting code.\n\n## Integration Partner Token Rotation\n\nAfter any release that modifies integration partner credentials, or on a\nscheduled rotation cycle, rotate partner tokens using the following procedure:\n\n**When to rotate:**\n- After upgrading `sports_federation_import_tools` (any release that changed\n  token storage, authentication, or the integration controller surface).\n- When the `token_rotation_required` flag is set to `True` on a partner record\n  (visible in Federation > Import Tools > Integration Partners).\n- On a periodic schedule — at minimum once per year or whenever a partner\n  personnel change occurs.\n\n**How to rotate (back-office procedure):**\n\n1. Open **Federation > Import Tools > Integration Partners**.\n2. Filter for partners where **Token Rotation Required** is checked, or where\n   **Last Rotated On** is older than the rotation policy window.\n3. For each partner, open the form and click **Rotate Token** (requires\n   Federation Manager group). Confirm the dialog.\n4. The wizard reveals the new raw token **once** (it cannot be retrieved again).\n   Copy it immediately and deliver it to the partner over a secure channel\n   (not email in plain text).\n5. The `token_rotation_required` flag clears automatically after a successful\n   rotation.\n\n**After a migration from plaintext storage:**\n\nIf `sports_federation_import_tools` was upgraded from a version prior to\n`19.0.1.2.0`, existing plaintext tokens were hashed in place and flagged for\nrotation by the post-migration script. Partners with `Token Rotation Required`\nset to `True` are still functional (their hashed token verifies correctly)\nbut should be rotated and re-issued at the next opportunity.\n\n**Verification:**\n\nAfter rotation, ask the partner to make one authenticated test call and confirm\na `200 OK` response to `/integration/v1/contracts`. A `401` response with\n`access_denied` indicates the token was not delivered correctly.\n\n## Rollback\n\nIf the upgrade must be rolled back:\n\n1. Stop or scale down the Odoo service to prevent new writes.\n2. Restore the PostgreSQL dump from the relevant backup directory.\n3. Restore the matching filestore archive.\n4. Restart the Odoo service.\n5. +- {"content": "# Competition Engine\n\nThis implementation provides role-owned capabilities and explicit handovers for competition planning and operations.\n\n## Addons\n\n1. `sports_federation_competition_core`: identity, roles, lifecycle and events.\n2. `sports_federation_registration`: application queue and finalized participant sets.\n3. `sports_federation_format`: versioned logical structures and fixtures.\n4. `sports_federation_calendar`: physical match days, round allocations and capacity.\n5. `sports_federation_scheduling`: one-way fixture-to-slot assignments, pure validation and deterministic proposals.\n6. `sports_federation_schedule_approval`: independent review and immutable publication snapshots.\n7. `sports_federation_matchday`: live operational control and incidents.\n\n## Required handovers\n\nRegistration finalizes a participant set. Format freezes a structure. Calendar prepares physical capacity. Scheduling submits a complete schedule. Approval publishes an immutable snapshot. Match-day operations execute only a published snapshot.\n\n## Migration policy\n\nThe legacy monolithic engine has been removed from the addon set. New and existing operational flows use the ownership split. Databases upgraded from a release that installed the legacy addon require the normal reviewed upgrade/migration procedure before production rollout; do not silently reinterpret existing production records.\n\n\n## Schedule handoff operator handoff\n\nThe operator path is fully exposed in the backend: Schedule Planner submits a\nvalidated revision, Schedule Review Queue provides independent request-changes\nor approval decisions, Publication exposes approved schedules and immutable\npublication history, and Match-Day Operations consumes only the current live\npublication. Submission creates its pending review atomically when the approval\naddon is installed; there is no operator-visible intermediate state that\nrequires a separate \"start review\" action.\n\n## Phases 5.1.1 to 5.3: publication and live operations\n\nSchedule review decisions are command-only: ACLs are read-only and the review\nmodel rejects direct decision-field writes. Live publications are scoped and\nversioned per match day. Publication replacement uses a dedicated wizard,\nrequires a replacement reason, locks the match day during version allocation,\nand rejects stale confirmations.\n\nMatch-Day Control exposes readiness, the exact live publication, published\nmatches, court state, incidents, immutable sessions and operational deviations.\nOpening a day freezes the publication digest in a session. Live moves, delays,\npostponements and cancellations update only operational match fields; the\napproved publication and `published_slot_id` remain immutable. Every deviation\nrecords actor, reason, old/new slot, session and publication, and emits an audit\nevent.\n", "content_length": 2809, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "COMPETITION_ENGINE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "2c6a2ef0be5e1aece6060a09b33b5da37b58fc1a0bca7e3604aa9cde951df0b0", "size_bytes": 2809}

+  {"content": "# Contributing\n\nThis repository expects small, test-backed changes with matching documentation updates.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.10 or newer for local linting\n- Docker with Compose current for the containerized Odoo test runner\n- Git Bash, WSL, or another POSIX shell for the `ci/*.sh` scripts on Windows\n\n## Local setup\n\n```bash\ncp ci/.env.example ci/.env\npython -m pip install --upgrade pip\npython -m pip install -r requirements.txt\n```\n\nKeep `ci/.env` local-only. Integration keys can be copied from `ci/integrations.env.example` or provided by your shell environment.\n\n## Focused test commands\n\nRun targeted suites for the main maintained flows:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite portal_public_ops\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite finance_reporting\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite rosters_readiness_guard\n```\n\nRun an individual module when you only need a narrow slice:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_result_control\n```\n\nList the named suites from the runner itself:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --list-suites\n```\n\n## Pre-push checks\n\nBefore release qualification, commit or intentionally discard all tracked\nchanges and remove generated runtime configuration. Release review must verify the configured cron XML IDs, active defaults, date anchors, retention constants, attachment cleanup, and preservation of unresolved workflow records. A date update without those checks is not sufficient.\n\n## Scope\n\nThe current automated retention policy covers these repository-owned surfaces:\n\n- `federation.notification.log` records created by `sports_federation_notifications`\n- `federation.integration.delivery` records and their staged payload attachments\n  in `sports_federation_import_tools`\n- `federation.report.schedule.generated_file` attachments created by\n  `sports_federation_reporting`\n\nNon-terminal workflow records are intentionally excluded from automated purge.\nIf a delivery is still waiting for preview, approval, or live processing, it is\nretained until an operator resolves it.\n\n## Retention Windows\n\n| Surface | State / Condition | Retention Window | Cleanup Anchor | Cleanup Result |\n|---------|-------------------|------------------|----------------|----------------|\n| Notification logs | `pending` | 30 days | `create_date` | Delete old log row |\n| Notification logs | `sent` | 90 days | `create_date` | Delete old log row |\n| Notification logs | `failed` | 180 days | `create_date` | Delete old log row |\n| Inbound deliveries | `cancelled` | 90 days | `received_on` | Delete delivery and staged payload attachment |\n| Inbound deliveries | `processed` | 180 days | `processed_on` | Delete delivery and staged payload attachment |\n| Inbound deliveries | `processed_with_errors` | 180 days | `processed_on` | Delete delivery and staged payload attachment |\n| Inbound deliveries | `failed` | 365 days | `received_on` | Delete delivery and staged payload attachment |\n| Generated report files | Last successful export snapshot | 60 days | `last_run_on` | Clear stored file payload and filename, keep schedule |\n\n## Automation\n\nThe cleanup routines run through daily scheduled actions that ship with the\naffected addons:\n\n- `sports_federation_notifications.ir_cron_notification_log_retention`\n- `sports_federation_import_tools.ir_cron_federation_integration_delivery_retention`\n- `sports_federation_reporting.ir_cron_federation_report_schedule_retention`\n\nThese jobs are active by default and call the corresponding model cleanup\nhelpers during normal Odoo cron execution.\n\n## Operator Notes\n\n- Delivery retention only applies to terminal states, so unresolved inbound\n  partner handoffs remain visible in the operator checklist.\n- Report schedule retention clears the stored export artifact but preserves the\n  schedule definition, run metadata, and next execution date.\n- If audit, legal, or incident-response requirements require a longer window,\n  update the model retention constants and this document in the same branch.\n\n## Change Management\n\nWhen retention windows or cleanup scope change:\n\n1. Update this document in the same branch as the code change.\n2. Update the affected module README files and release/runbook guidance.\n3. Re-run `python3 ci/check_doc_freshness.py` and `python3 ci/check_markdown_links.py`.\n4. Re-run the affected module test suites to confirm the cleanup behavior still\n   matches the documented policy.\n\n## Execution evidence\n\nEvery automated retention run appends a `federation.retention.evidence` record with its policy code, timestamps, outcome, and affected-record counts. Evidence is read-only to federation managers and is retained independently from the records cleaned by the policy.\n\n\n## Recovery visibility\n\nFederation managers use **Administration → Retention and Recovery** to verify policy freshness and outcomes.
