Tournament Publication Setup\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_public_site`\n\nBefore publishing, ensure the tournament has:\n\n1. a completed setup with matches and public-facing text\n2. approved results if the results page should be visible\n3. computed standings if the standings page should be visible\n\nThen configure the public-site fields on the tournament:\n\n- `website_published`\n- `public_slug`\n- `public_description`\n- `public_featured`\n- `public_editorial_summary`\n- `public_pinned_announcement`\n- `show_public_results`\n- `show_public_standings`\n\nThe first transition from unpublished to published sends the tournament\npublication notification to participating club and team contacts.\n\nThe tournament Website tab now also surfaces the next unmet prerequisite\ndirectly on the form: whether the tournament itself is still unpublished,\nwhether standings do not exist yet, or whether standings exist but are not yet\npublished or visible.\n\n### 2. Standings And Results Visibility\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Modules**: `sports_federation_standings`, `sports_federation_result_control`\n\n1. Publish the standings record itself with `website_published = True`.\n2. Optionally set `public_title` for the public standings page.\n3. Remember the public results page only shows approved results.\n4. Use the standings form and the tournament Website tab together for the final\n  handoff: standings pages explain whether approved results are still pending,\n  while the tournament Website tab explains whether the public blocker is the\n  standings record or the tournament visibility toggles.\n4. Public participant lists exclude withdrawn tournament participants.\n\n### 3. Editorial Publication Workflow\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator or communications staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_public_site`\n\nEditorial items can be anchored to a season, tournament, or team and use the\nstate machine below:\n\n`draft` → `scheduled` → `published` → `archived`\n\nOperator actions:\n\n1. **Schedule** — allowed only from `draft`, and only when `publish_start` is set.\n2. **Publish Now** — allowed from `draft` or `scheduled`.\n3. **Archive** — allowed from `scheduled` or `published`.\n4. **Reset to Draft** — allowed from `scheduled` or `archived`.\n\nStatusbar behavior:\n\n- The form statusbar shows the active publication pipeline:\n  `draft`, `scheduled`, `published`.\n- `archived` is still a real record state, but operators reach it and leave it\n  through explicit actions and search filters rather than as a visible statusbar\n  stop.\n\nVisibility guards:\n\n- Editorial items must be `active`.\n- `draft` and `archived` items are never public.\n- `scheduled` and `published` items are only public inside the\n  `publish_start` / `publish_end` window.\n\n### 4. Public Pages Go Live\n\n**Actor**: System (automatic)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_public_site`\n\nCanonical public surfaces include:\n\n| URL | Content |\n|-----|---------|\n| `/competitions` | Main tournament hub with featured, live, recent, and archived sections |\n| `/competitions/<edition-slug>` | Canonical competition edition overview page |\n| `/competitions/<edition-slug>/teams` | Published participant list excluding withdrawn entries |\n| `/competitions/<edition-slug>/standings` | Public standings page when enabled |\n| `/competitions/<edition-slug>/results` | Approved public results when enabled |\n| `/competitions/<edition-slug>/schedule` | Upcoming fixtures |\n| `/competitions/<edition-slug>/bracket` | Public bracket view when bracket data exists |\n| `/competitions/<edition-slug>/divisions/<division-slug>/schedule.ics` | Tournament schedule calendar export |\n| `/api/v1/competitions/<edition-slug>` | Stable v1 JSON feed |\n| `/seasons/<slug>` | Season landing page with editorial and tournament aggregation |\n| `/teams/<slug>` | Public team profile page |\n| `/teams/<slug>/schedule` | Team-centric grouped upcoming schedule |\n| `/teams/<slug>/results` | Team-centric recent approved results |\n| `/teams/<slug>/schedule.ics` | Team schedule calendar export |\n| `/api/v1/teams/<slug>/feed` | Stable v1 team follow feed |\n\nOlder `/competitions` and numeric routes remain as compatibility paths, but the\nauthoritative public URLs are the slug-based `/competitions/...` routes.\nCompatibility routes only redirect while the tournament still matches the\nrelevant publication guard; unpublished tournaments fail closed instead of\nresolving through direct slug or numeric paths. ++ {"content": "# Workflow: Roster Management\n\nEnd-to-end lifecycle for managing team rosters — from pre-season draft through\nactive season use, match-day locking, post-season closure, and controlled\nreopening when closure needs to be undone.\n\n## Overview\n\nA **team roster** (`federation.team.roster`) is the official squad declaration\nfor a team in a given season and competition. Clubs assemble their rosters, get\nthem activated by federation staff, and use them as the source pool for\nmatch-day squad sheets. Roster changes after activation require explicit admin\nsteps; match-day locks prevent post-match tampering.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_rosters` | Roster, roster line, match sheet, match sheet line, participation audit |\n| `sports_federation_base` | Team, season, club, season registration |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Player records and player licenses |\n| `sports_federation_rules` | Squad-size and eligibility rule sets |\n| `sports_federation_discipline` | Suspension checks during eligibility validation |\n| `sports_federation_portal` | Club representative self-service roster editing |\n\n## Models\n\n| Model | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| `federation.team.roster` | Master roster for a team/season/competition |\n| `federation.team.roster.line` | Individual player slot within a roster |\n| `federation.match.sheet` | Match-day squad declaration for one team |\n| `federation.match.sheet.line` | Individual player/staff entry on a match sheet |\n| `federation.participation.audit` | Immutable audit log of roster and sheet events |\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Roster Creation\n\n**Actor**: Club administrator or federation staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rosters`\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Rosters → Team Rosters** and click **New**.\n2. Select the **team**, **season**, and optionally the **competition** and **rule set**.\n3. Odoo auto-generates a name (`{Team} – {Competition} – {Season} Roster`);\n   leave blank to trigger auto-generation, or supply a custom name.\n4. Set minimum/maximum squad sizes if a rule set is not attached.\n5. Add **roster lines** — one per player. Each line stores:\n   - player reference\n   - optional captain/vice-captain flag\n   - linked player license (auto-scoped to the roster's team and season)\n6. Portal users editing a roster only see licenses that match the roster's team and\n   season; any attempt to supply out-of-scope IDs is rejected server-side.\n\nRoster status starts at **`draft`**.\n\n### 2. Eligibility & Readiness Check\n\n**Actor**: Federation staff or automated validation\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rosters`\n\n1. The system computes `ready_for_activation` (stored Boolean) whenever roster\n   lines, players, or licenses change.\n2. `readiness_feedback` (stored Text) lists blocking reasons, e.g.:\n   - Player has no active license for this season.\n   - Squad size is below the required minimum.\n   - Player is currently serving a suspension.\n3. All checks must pass before the roster can be activated.\n\n### 3. Roster Activation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rosters`\n\n1. Once readiness is confirmed, change status: **`draft` → `active`**.\n2. An active roster is visible to club representatives in the portal and available\n   as a source for match sheets.\n3. A `federation.participation.audit` entry is created for the activation event.\n\n### 4. Player Additions and Changes Post-Activation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rosters`\n\n1. Minor changes (e.g. adding a new player mid-season) require temporarily setting\n   the roster back to `draft`, making changes, re-running the readiness check, and\n   re-activating.\n2. The re-activation creates a new audit log entry recording the responsible user\n   and timestamp.\n\n### 5. Match Sheet Creation\n\n**Actor**: Club administrator / team manager\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rosters`\n\n1. For each fixture, create a **match sheet** (`federation.match.sheet`) linked to\n   the match, the team, and the source roster.\n2. Set the **side** (home / away / other).\n3. Add **match sheet lines** — typically by selecting from the active roster lines.\n   Mark starters vs. substitutes and assign jersey numbers.\n4. Add coach and manager names if required.\n5. Computed `ready_for_submission` reflects the same license/discipline/squad-size\n   checks as the parent roster. `readiness_feedback` lists any blockers.\n\nMatch sheet states: `draft` → `submitted` → `approved` → `locked`.\n\n### 6. Match Sheet Submission and Approval\n\n**Actor**: Club administrator → Federation staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rosters`\n\n1. Club submits the sheet (`draft` → `submitted`).\n2. Federation staff reviews the lineup and **approves** it (`submitted` → `approved`).\n3. If corrections are needed, staff resets to `draft` for the club to amend.\n4. Once approved, the listed players are locked in; only substitution-timing fields\n   remain editable until the sheet reaches `locked`.\n\n### 7. Match-Day Lock\n\n**Actor**: System (automated after match completion) or federation staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rosters`\n\n1. After the match concludes (match state reaches `done`), the match sheet is\n   locked: status → **`locked`**, `locked_on` timestamp and `locked_by_id` are\n   recorded.\n2. `match_day_locked` (computed on the roster) reflects whether any linked sheet\n   is locked, surfacing a read-only message in the roster form.\n3. No further lineup changes are possible once locked; a new protest/appeal must\n   be filed through the **Discipline** module.\n\n### 8. Roster Closure\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator (end of season)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rosters`\n\n1. When the season closes, change status: **`active` → `closed`**.\n2. Closed rosters are removed from new match-sheet preparation flows.\n3. If closure was premature, use **Reopen** to restore\n   **`closed` → `active`**.\n4. Reopen keeps safeguards in place: the roster must still pass readiness\n   checks, and reopen is blocked if another active roster already exists in the\n   same team/season/competition scope.\n5. Audit trail remains fully queryable for historical analysis.\n\n## State Diagrams\n\n```\nRoster:      draft ↔ active → closed → active\n\nMatch Sheet: draft → submitted → approved → locked\n                  ↑← reset (from submitted to draft)\n```\n\n## Portal Access\n\n- Club representatives with an active `federation.club.representative` record can\n  view and edit **draft** roster lines for their club's teams.\n- Only licenses scoped to the roster's team and season are shown in the portal;\n  server-side validation rejects any attempt to select out-of-scope records.\n- **Active** or **closed** rosters keep lineup edits read-only in the portal.\n- Authorized representatives can still use portal roster actions to close an\n   active roster or reopen a closed roster when federation policy allows it.\n\n## Audit Trail\n\nEvery significant roster event (creation, activation, reset, line additions,\nmatch sheet approval, lock) records a `federation.participation.audit` entry\nwith actor, timestamp, and event type. Season Creation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_base`\n\n1. Open the **Seasons** screen from the backend setup area.\n2. Create a new season with name, code, and date range (e.g. \"2025-2026\").\n3. Set the season state to **open**.\n\nThe season record becomes the scoping key for all registrations, tournaments,\nrosters, and licenses throughout the year.\n\n### 2. Club Registration Opening\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_base`\n\n1. Open the **Season Registrations** screen from the backend setup area.\n2. Create registration records (one per team) or let clubs self-register via the portal.\n3. Each registration links a team and its club to an open season.\n\nRegistration states: `draft` → `submitted` → `confirmed` / `cancelled`.\n\n### 3. Portal Self-Service (Optional)\n\n**Actor**: Club representative (portal user)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_portal`\n\n1. Club representative logs into the portal.\n2. Navigates to the federation registration section.\n3. Submits their club's season registration request.\n4. Adds supporting notes when needed.\n5. Registration is created in `submitted` state for federation review.\n\n### 4. Registration Review & Approval\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_base`\n\n1. Review submitted registrations from the backend review screen.\n2. Verify club ownership, season status, and any federation prerequisites.\n3. **Confirm** the registration or **reject** it back to `draft` with a rejection reason.\n4. Confirmed teams are eligible to enrol players and proceed into competition operations.\n5. The season and registration forms now surface that same order of operations\n  inline: draft seasons point operators toward registrations, open seasons warn\n  when registrations are still missing or pending, and confirmed registrations\n  expose a direct **Open Team Rosters** handoff for the next operational step.\n\nThere is no persistent `rejected` season-registration state in the current model. Rejection is represented by the record returning to `draft` while keeping `rejection_reason` for follow-up.\n\n### 5. Team Enrolment\n\n**Actor**: Club administrator or federation staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_base`\n\n1. Under each confirmed club registration, create or confirm teams for the season.\n2. Teams inherit the club's season registration scope.\n3. Teams become available for tournament participation and roster creation.\n4. When roster preparation is the next task, use **Open Team Rosters** from the\n  confirmed registration. The action opens the roster list with the current\n  team, season, competition, and rule-set context prefilled.\n\n### 6. Player Registration & Licensing\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_people`\n\nPlayer licenses are the formal proof of a player's eligibility to compete in a\ngiven season. Each license is scoped to one player, one season, and one club.\n\n#### License Creation\n\n1. Create or locate the player record (`federation.player`) with club affiliation.\n2. Navigate to the player's **Licenses** tab and click **New**, or go to\n   **Federation → People → Player Licenses** and create from there.\n3. Fill in:\n   - **Season** (must be open)\n   - **Club** (must match the player's current club)\n   - **Issue date** and **Expiry date** (expiry must be after issue date)\n   - **Category**: `senior` | `youth` | `junior` | `cadet`\n   - Optional eligibility notes\n4. Compliance Document Collection\n\n**Actor**: Club representative or federation staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_compliance`\n\n1. Federation defines document requirements per entity type (club, player, etc.).\n2. Clubs upload required documents (insurance, safety certificates, etc.).\n3. Federation staff reviews submissions: `submitted` → `approved` / `rejected`.\n4. Compliance checks are run to flag missing or expired documents.\n\n### 8. Fee Recording\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_finance_bridge`\n\n1. Upon registration confirmation, a finance event is created for the registration fee.\n2. Finance event follows: `draft` → `confirmed` → `settled` / `cancelled`.\n\n### 9. Notifications\n\n**Actor**: System (automated)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_notifications`\n\n- Registration confirmation and rejection emails are logged and sent to the submitting club representative.\n- Reminders for incomplete or stale draft registrations (cron job).\n- Missing-document notices triggered by compliance checks.\n\n## State Diagram\n\n```\nSeason: draft → open → closed\n\nRegistration: draft → submitted → confirmed\n                                 → cancelled\n                                 ↘ draft (via rejection)\n\nLicense: draft → active → expired\n                        → cancelled\n```\n\n## Key Decision Points\n\n| Question | Outcome |\n|----------|---------|\n| Are all compliance documents submitted? | Block approval until compliant |\n| Is the registration fee paid? | Registration can proceed but fee remains tracked |\n| Has the club been sanctioned? | Governance override may be needed |\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [Tournament Lifecycle](WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md) — tournaments open to registered clubs\n- [Compliance Management](WORKFLOW_COMPLIANCE_MANAGEMENT.md) — document collection detail\n- [Financial Tracking](WORKFLOW_FINANCIAL_TRACKING.md) — fee handling detail\n", "content_length": 7572, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_SEASON_REGISTRATION.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "c18b121a00f574762fd52745741e6b13459c9a931a5747b5d1f55749a363b7ce", "size_bytes": 7612}
++-{"content": "# Workflow: Standings Lifecycle\n\nAutomatic and manual standing recomputation, freeze points, website\npublication, and the impact of official-result changes on standings tables.\n\n## Overview\n\nStandings are derived from results that still have\n`include_in_official_standings = True`. They recompute automatically when a\nresult becomes official, can be recomputed manually at any time, and are\nfrozen when the authoritative ranking for a stage must be locked. Public\nvisibility is separate from the standings state itself and is controlled\nthrough `website_published`.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings model, recompute engine |\n| `sports_federation_result_control` | Result approval triggering recompute |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournament, stage, match records |\n| `sports_federation_governance` | Override requests for disputed standings |\n| `sports_federation_public_site` | Publication (`website_published`) |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Notification on standings publication |\n\n## Models\n\n| Model | Key Fields |\n|-------|-----------|\n| `federation.standings` | `tournament_id`, `stage_id`, `group_id`, `state`, `computed_on`, `website_published`, `public_title` |\n| `federation.standings.line` | `team_id`, `position`, `points`, `played`, `won`, `drawn`, `lost`, `goals_for`, `goals_against`, `goal_diff` |\n\n## Standing States\n\n```\ndraft → computed → frozen\n```\n\n| State | Meaning |\n|-------|---------|\n| `draft` | Standings record exists but has not been computed |\n| `computed` | Standings are up to date with the currently official results |\n| `frozen` | Standings are locked; no further recompute will change them |\n\n`website_published = True` controls whether the standing is visible on the\npublic site. It does not create a separate standings workflow state.\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Automatic Recompute Trigger\n\n**Actor**: System (triggered by result approval)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control` → `sports_federation_standings`\n\nWhen a match result is approved (`result_state = approved`):\n\n1. `include_in_official_standings` is set to `True` on the match record.\n2. The result approval method calls\n   `federation.standings._trigger_recompute(tournament_id, stage_id, group_id)`.\n3. Any `federation.standings` record linked to the same tournament / stage /\n   group that is in `draft` or `computed` state is queued for recompute.\n4. The standings table is rebuilt from scratch from all approved results\n   in that scope.\n5. After recompute, the standings transition to `computed`.\n\n**Frozen standings are not recomputed**. If a result is approved after the\nstandings have been frozen, a warning appears on the match form but the\nstandings are not changed.\n\n### 2. Manual Recompute\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings`\n\nWhen results are corrected or the automatic trigger did not fire (e.g. an edge\ncase during bulk import):\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Standings** and open the relevant standings record.\n2. Click **Recompute** (only available in `draft` or `computed` states, never on\n   `frozen` or `published`).\n3. The standings engine rebuilds all lines from approved results.\n4. State transitions to `computed`.\n\n### 3. Freeze Decision\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator (Federation Manager group)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings`\n\nStandings are frozen at a natural boundary — end of group stage, end of regular\nseason, or after the last knockout round of a stage:\n\n1. Open the standings record in `computed` state.\n2. Click **Freeze**.\n3. State transitions: `computed → frozen`.\n4. Frozen standings will not be touched by any subsequent result approval in\n   that scope.\n\n**Who can freeze**: only users in the `group_federation_manager` security group\ncan freeze standings.\n\n**When to freeze**: freeze only after all matches in the stage are `done` and\nall results are `approved`. Freezing with unapproved results creates an\nincomplete official table.\n\n### 4. Publication Approval\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings` → `sports_federation_public_site`\n\nBefore standings appear on the public website, a publication approval step\nprovides a human review checkpoint:\n\n1. With standings in `computed` or `frozen` state, publish the record from the\n   Website tab.\n2. `website_published` is set to `True`.\n3. The standings page at `/tournaments/<slug>/standings` now reflects the\n   table.\n\nIf `sports_federation_notifications` is installed, a notification is dispatched\nto club contacts when standings for their tournament are published.\n\n**Unpublishing**: set `website_published = False` to pull the standings from\nthe public site without changing the `state`. This is useful when a dispute or\nlate correction requires re-review.\n\n### 5. Contested Result Impact on Standings\n\n**Actor**: Club representative or federation official → Governance officer\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control` + `sports_federation_governance`\n\nWhen a result is contested after standings have been computed:\n\n1. `result_state` moves to `contested` and\n   `include_in_official_standings` becomes `False`.\n2. Any standings in `draft` or `computed` scope are recomputed automatically\n   and drop the result.\n3. If the standing is `frozen`, federation staff must decide whether to leave\n   the frozen table in place during review or deliberately unfreeze or\n   force-recompute it after governance review.\n4. If the standing is public (`website_published = True`) and the table should\n   be withdrawn during review, unpublish it separately. Publication is not a\n   standings state.\n5. A governance override request may document the review, but it does not keep\n   a contested result official.\n\n## Contested Results and the Frozen Table\n\n| Standing status | Operator action |\n|----------------|-----------------|\n| `draft` / `computed` | Automatic recompute removes the contested result |\n| `frozen` | Federation manager decides whether to unfreeze or force-recompute after review |\n| `website_published = True` | Unpublish separately if the public table should be hidden during review |\n\n## Summary of Access Control\n\n| Action | Required Group |\n|--------|---------------|\n| Manual recompute | `group_federation_manager` |\n| Freeze standings | `group_federation_manager` |\n| Publish / unpublish | `group_federation_manager` |\n| View standings | `group_federation_user` (backend), public (website) |\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md](WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md) — Result approval that triggers automatic recompute.\n- [WORKFLOW_APPEAL_DISPUTE.md](WORKFLOW_APPEAL_DISPUTE.md) — Appeal and dispute process for contested results.\n- [WORKFLOW_PUBLIC_PUBLICATION.md](WORKFLOW_PUBLIC_PUBLICATION.md) — Broader public-site publication workflow.\n", "content_length": 6858, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_STANDINGS_LIFECYCLE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "86e83a191263b79c6c7853d709420122651e9df47981ed344187fff6581ca353", "size_bytes": 6880}
++-{"content": "# Workflow: Tournament Lifecycle\n\nFull lifecycle of a tournament — from competition definition and participant\nenrolment through schedule generation, match execution, and final completion.\n\n## Overview\n\nA **competition** is a recurring series (e.g. \"National League Division 1\").\nWithin each season, competitions host one or more **tournaments** which are\nstructured into stages, groups, and matches. This workflow covers the entire\njourney from initial setup to final completion.\n\nCanonical readiness chain (registration to publication):\n\n1. Confirm season registration.\n2. Confirm tournament participant.\n3. Prepare active ready roster and match-day sheets.\n4. Publish schedule and run live operations.\n5. Approve results.\n6. Recompute/review standings.\n7. Publish tournament and standings surfaces.\n\nBlocking vs warning-only model:\n\n- Blocking: the step cannot proceed (for example, deadline-backed roster blockers\n   or unresolved publication validation blockers).\n- Warning-only: the step can proceed, but requires operator follow-up and may\n   require manager override logging depending on the surface.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Seasons, clubs, teams |\n| `sports_federation_rules` | Rule sets governing scoring, tie-breaks, eligibility |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Competition, tournament, stage, group, participant, match models |\n| `sports_federation_competition_core`, `sports_federation_registration` | Competition identity, lifecycle, registration, and participant finalization |\n| `sports_federation_format` | Versioned logical structures and stage graphs |\n| `sports_federation_calendar` | Physical match days, capacity, slots, and timelines |\n| `sports_federation_scheduling` | Deterministic fixture assignment and schedule validation |\n| `sports_federation_schedule_approval` | Schedule review and immutable publication snapshots |\n| `sports_federation_matchday` | Live operations after schedule publication |\n| `sports_federation_venues` | Venue and playing-area assignment |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings computation at each stage |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Participant-confirmation and publication notifications |\n| `sports_federation_public_site` | Public publication of tournament pages |\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Competition Setup\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rules`, `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Define a **rule set** with scoring values (win/draw/loss points), tie-break\n   criteria, squad-size limits, and eligibility rules.\n2. Create a **competition** (e.g. \"National League Division 1\").\n3. Link the competition to the active season and the rule set.\n4. Set competition state to `active`.\n\n### 2. Tournament Creation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Under the competition, create a **tournament** (e.g. \"NL Div 1 — Season 2025\").\n2. Set tournament type: `league`, `cup`, `friendly`, or `playoff`.\n3. Assign date range, rule set (inherited from competition or overridden).\n4. Set maximum participants if applicable.\n5. If the competition is spread over multiple event days, plan the shared\n   schedule blocks directly on the stage rounds. Each round can carry a\n   calendar date and a venue, while the matches inside that round keep their\n   own kickoff times.\n6. Tournament starts in `draft` state.\n\n### 3. Venue Assignment\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_venues`\n\n1. Create or select venues with address, capacity, and playing areas.\n2. Link venues to the tournament via the `venues` Many2many field.\n3. Individual matches can later reference specific venues and playing areas.\n\n### 4. Participant Enrolment\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator (or via import)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`, `sports_federation_import_tools`\n\n1. Add **participants** to the tournament — each links a team to the tournament.\n    - If the flow starts from portal registration requests, an administrator first\n       confirms the `federation.competition.entry` record. That creates or links\n       a `federation.tournament.participant` record in state `registered`.\n    - That participant must still be moved to state `confirmed` before schedule\n       generation can use it.\n2. Optionally assign participants to specific stages and groups.\n3. Set seeding ranks for bracket placement.\n4. Participant states: `registered` → `confirmed` → `withdrawn` / `eliminated`.\n5. Participant confirmation can happen before the team has an active roster, but\n   only until one week before its first scheduled match, or one week before\n   tournament start if no match has been scheduled yet. Once that deadline is\n   reached, participant confirmation is blocked until the team has an active\n   ready roster. When both a competition-specific roster and a season-wide\n   roster are available, the competition-specific roster is used for readiness\n   checks.\n6. The participant form now surfaces the current roster deadline feedback inline\n   and exposes **Open Team Roster** when operators need to resolve the blocker\n   in the rosters flow before confirmation can continue.\n7. Confirming a participant sends an email to the team and club contacts.\n8. Move tournament to `open` state once enrolment is complete.\n\nBulk enrolment is available via the **Import Tournament Participants** wizard.\n\n### 5. Stage & Group Structure\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Create **stages** within the tournament (e.g. \"Group Phase\", \"Quarter-Finals\").\n2. Set stage type: `group`, `knockout`, `playoff`, or `other`.\n3. Order stages by sequence.\n4. Within each stage, create **groups** (e.g. \"Group A\", \"Pool 1\").\n5. Assign participants to groups.\n6. Create or review the stage rounds that should exist for each phase. Example:\n   rounds 1-4 for the round-robin stage, then knockout rounds on the final stage.\n\n### 6. Schedule Generation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Modules**: `sports_federation_format`, `sports_federation_calendar`,\n`sports_federation_scheduling`, `sports_federation_schedule_approval`, and\n`sports_federation_matchday`\n\nThe path is an explicit sequence of handovers:\n\n- Freeze the logical structure and stage graph in `sports_federation_format`.\n- Prepare physical match days and playable capacity in\n   `sports_federation_calendar`.\n- Generate or assign fixtures and validate the complete draft in\n   `sports_federation_scheduling`.\n- Submit the draft for review and publish an immutable snapshot through\n   `sports_federation_schedule_approval`.\n- Start live operations only from the published snapshot through\n   `sports_federation_matchday`.\n\n1. Move the competition into the state that permits scheduling.\n2. Registration finalizes and locks the confirmed participant set.\n3. Format freezes the structure and stage graph for the competition edition.\n   Round-robin and knockout generation remain deterministic and scoped to the\n   frozen structure.\n4. Calendar creates match days and `federation.schedule.slot` capacity for the\n   required venues and courts. Slot lifecycle and court timelines are owned by\n   `sports_federation_calendar`.\n5. Scheduling assigns fixtures to available slots, applies fairness and rest\n   validation, and returns a complete draft schedule. Blocking conflicts must be\n   resolved before review; warnings remain visible and auditable.\n6. Schedule approval reviews the draft and publishes an immutable schedule\n   snapshot. Federation managers may approve configured warning-only overrides,\n   with the reason retained in the audit trail.\n7. Match-day operations open and close only published schedules. Referee\n   readiness, venue readiness, result follow-up, and incidents are handled by\n   their owning modules without changing the approved snapshot.\n\n**Round Robin**: The format service generates a complete deterministic pairing\nset where every team plays every other team once or twice according to policy.\n\n**Knockout**: The format service creates a seeded single-elimination bracket,\nincluding byes and future-round wiring for non-power-of-two participant counts.\n\n### 7. Match Execution\n\n**Actor**: Federation staff, referees\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Matches are scheduled with date/time, venue, home/away teams.\n2. Match states progress: `draft` → `scheduled` → `in_progress` → `done`.\n3. Scores are entered on the match form (home_score, away_score).\n4. Match-day details are handled by the [Match Day Operations](WORKFLOW_MATCH_DAY_OPERATIONS.md)\n   workflow.\n\n### 8. Standings Computation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings`\n\n1. Create a **standings** record scoped to the tournament, stage, or group.\n2. Link the rule set for scoring and tie-break rules.\n3. Compute standings: aggregates match results into ranked lines.\n4. States: `draft` → `computed` → `frozen`.\n5. Frozen standings are the publication candidates for the public site.\n\n### 9. Stage Progression\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. After a stage completes, review standings to determine qualifiers.\n2. Qualification rules from the rule set indicate who advances.\n3. Use `federation.stage.progression` rules to formalise advancement: these\n   can be single-group, cross-group (e.g. \"best third-placed teams\"), and\n   include seeding/placement strategies. A progression rule can be executed\n   manually (`action_execute()`) or set to `auto_advance=True`.\n    - When designing a versioned structure in Format Studio, use the\n       structure-scoped `federation.structure.stage.progression` edges instead.\n       These graph edges are separate from the competition engine's tournament\n       progression rules and are validated before the structure is generated.\n   - When a standings record is `frozen`/`computed`, any progression rules for\n     that stage with `auto_advance=True` will be executed automatically — new\n     participants are created in the target stage and (optionally) a new stage\n     schedule can be generated automatically.\n4. Tournament templates (`federation.tournament.template`) let administrators\n   scaffold common stage/group/progression combinations (for recurring\n   tournaments). Use `action_apply()` from the template to create stages and\n   progression rules for a tournament in a single step.\n5. Generate the next stage's schedule using competition engine wizards.\n6. Typical workflow: freeze the round-robin standing, auto-advance the top-ranked\n   teams into the knockout stage through a `federation.stage.progression` rule,\n   then schedule those knockout matches onto the planned knockout rounds.\n\n### 10. Tournament Completion\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. After the final stage, review and approve all remaining results.\n2. Compute and publish final standings.\n3. Set tournament state to `closed`.\n4. Competition can be closed at end of season.\n\n### 11. Public Publication\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_public_site`\n\n1. Set `website_published = True` on the tournament.\n2. Configure public slug, description, and toggle results/standings visibility.\n   The tournament Website tab now states whether publication is blocked because\n   the tournament is still unpublished, standings do not exist yet, or standings\n   remain hidden, and it links back to the standings action when relevant.\n3. Publish standings records. Standings forms also explain whether approved\n   results are still pending or whether website publication is the next valid\n   step.\n4. Participant club and team contacts receive a tournament-publication email the first time the tournament is published.\n5. Public pages become available at `/tournaments/<slug>` and the related\n   canonical `/competitions/...` route family.\n\n## State Diagram\n\n```\nCompetition: draft → active → closed\n\nTournament: draft → open → in_progress → closed\n                                       → cancelled\n\nMatch: draft → scheduled → in_progress → done\n                                        → cancelled\n\nStandings: draft → computed → frozen\n\nParticipant: registered → confirmed → withdrawn\n                                    → eliminated\n```\n\n## Key Decision Points\n\n| Question | Outcome |\n|----------|---------|\n| League or Cup format? | Determines round-robin vs. knockout wizard |\n| How many stages? | Single-stage league or multi-stage tournament with progression |\n| Power-of-two bracket? | Knockout wizard handles byes for odd counts |\n| When to publish? | Standings should be computed and verified before publication |\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [Match Day Operations](WORKFLOW_MATCH_DAY_OPERATIONS.md) — detailed match-day process\n- [Result Pipeline](WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md) — score verification and approval\n- [Season Registration](WORKFLOW_SEASON_REGISTRATION.md) — prerequisite club/team registration\n", "content_length": 13020, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "7006557805831eab890948323e37d682c5927710a716dc892c72b811761ea024", "size_bytes": 13078}
+++{"content": "# Workflow: Standings Lifecycle\n\nAutomatic and manual standing recomputation, freeze points, website\npublication, and the impact of official-result changes on standings tables.\n\n## Overview\n\nStandings are derived from results that still have\n`include_in_official_standings = True`. They recompute automatically when a\nresult becomes official, can be recomputed manually at any time, and are\nfrozen when the authoritative ranking for a stage must be locked. Public\nvisibility is separate from the standings state itself and is controlled\nthrough `website_published`.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings model, recompute engine |\n| `sports_federation_result_control` | Result approval triggering recompute |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournament, stage, match records |\n| `sports_federation_governance` | Override requests for disputed standings |\n| `sports_federation_public_site` | Publication (`website_published`) |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Notification on standings publication |\n\n## Models\n\n| Model | Key Fields |\n|-------|-----------|\n| `federation.standings` | `tournament_id`, `stage_id`, `group_id`, `state`, `computed_on`, `website_published`, `public_title` |\n| `federation.standings.line` | `team_id`, `position`, `points`, `played`, `won`, `drawn`, `lost`, `goals_for`, `goals_against`, `goal_diff` |\n\n## Standing States\n\n```\ndraft → computed → frozen\n```\n\n| State | Meaning |\n|-------|---------|\n| `draft` | Standings record exists but has not been computed |\n| `computed` | Standings are up to date with the currently official results |\n| `frozen` | Standings are locked; no further recompute will change them |\n\n`website_published = True` controls whether the standing is visible on the\npublic site. It does not create a separate standings workflow state.\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Automatic Recompute Trigger\n\n**Actor**: System (triggered by result approval)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control` → `sports_federation_standings`\n\nWhen a match result is approved (`result_state = approved`):\n\n1. `include_in_official_standings` is set to `True` on the match record.\n2. The result approval method calls\n   `federation.standings._trigger_recompute(tournament_id, stage_id, group_id)`.\n3. Any `federation.standings` record linked to the same tournament / stage /\n   group that is in `draft` or `computed` state is queued for recompute.\n4. The standings table is rebuilt from scratch from all approved results\n   in that scope.\n5. After recompute, the standings transition to `computed`.\n\n**Frozen standings are not recomputed**. If a result is approved after the\nstandings have been frozen, a warning appears on the match form but the\nstandings are not changed.\n\n### 2. Manual Recompute\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings`\n\nWhen results are corrected or the automatic trigger did not fire (e.g. an edge\ncase during bulk import):\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Standings** and open the relevant standings record.\n2. Click **Recompute** (only available in `draft` or `computed` states, never on\n   `frozen` or `published`).\n3. The standings engine rebuilds all lines from approved results.\n4. State transitions to `computed`.\n\n### 3. Freeze Decision\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator (Federation Manager group)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings`\n\nStandings are frozen at a natural boundary — end of group stage, end of regular\nseason, or after the last knockout round of a stage:\n\n1. Open the standings record in `computed` state.\n2. Click **Freeze**.\n3. State transitions: `computed → frozen`.\n4. Frozen standings will not be touched by any subsequent result approval in\n   that scope.\n\n**Who can freeze**: only users in the `group_federation_manager` security group\ncan freeze standings.\n\n**When to freeze**: freeze only after all matches in the stage are `done` and\nall results are `approved`. Freezing with unapproved results creates an\nincomplete official table.\n\n### 4. Publication Approval\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings` → `sports_federation_public_site`\n\nBefore standings appear on the public website, a publication approval step\nprovides a human review checkpoint:\n\n1. With standings in `computed` or `frozen` state, publish the record from the\n   Website tab.\n2. `website_published` is set to `True`.\n3. The standings page at `/competitions/<edition-slug>/standings` now reflects the\n   table.\n\nIf `sports_federation_notifications` is installed, a notification is dispatched\nto club contacts when standings for their tournament are published.\n\n**Unpublishing**: set `website_published = False` to pull the standings from\nthe public site without changing the `state`. This is useful when a dispute or\nlate correction requires re-review.\n\n### 5. Contested Result Impact on Standings\n\n**Actor**: Club representative or federation official → Governance officer\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control` + `sports_federation_governance`\n\nWhen a result is contested after standings have been computed:\n\n1. `result_state` moves to `contested` and\n   `include_in_official_standings` becomes `False`.\n2. Any standings in `draft` or `computed` scope are recomputed automatically\n   and drop the result.\n3. If the standing is `frozen`, federation staff must decide whether to leave\n   the frozen table in place during review or deliberately unfreeze or\n   force-recompute it after governance review.\n4. If the standing is public (`website_published = True`) and the table should\n   be withdrawn during review, unpublish it separately. Publication is not a\n   standings state.\n5. A governance override request may document the review, but it does not keep\n   a contested result official.\n\n## Contested Results and the Frozen Table\n\n| Standing status | Operator action |\n|----------------|-----------------|\n| `draft` / `computed` | Automatic recompute removes the contested result |\n| `frozen` | Federation manager decides whether to unfreeze or force-recompute after review |\n| `website_published = True` | Unpublish separately if the public table should be hidden during review |\n\n## Summary of Access Control\n\n| Action | Required Group |\n|--------|---------------|\n| Manual recompute | `group_federation_manager` |\n| Freeze standings | `group_federation_manager` |\n| Publish / unpublish | `group_federation_manager` |\n| View standings | `group_federation_user` (backend), public (website) |\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md](WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md) — Result approval that triggers automatic recompute.\n- [WORKFLOW_APPEAL_DISPUTE.md](WORKFLOW_APPEAL_DISPUTE.md) — Appeal and dispute process for contested results.\n- [WORKFLOW_PUBLIC_PUBLICATION.md](WORKFLOW_PUBLIC_PUBLICATION.md) — Broader public-site publication workflow.\n", "content_length": 6867, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_STANDINGS_LIFECYCLE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "5f4f4090720ce7beaeb793767efd8dae49614b26c3b90434ad07c34f150aa2f3", "size_bytes": 6889}
+++{"content": "# Workflow: Tournament Lifecycle\n\nFull lifecycle of a tournament — from competition definition and participant\nenrolment through schedule generation, match execution, and final completion.\n\n## Overview\n\nA **competition** is a recurring series (e.g. \"National League Division 1\").\nWithin each season, competitions host one or more **tournaments** which are\nstructured into stages, groups, and matches. This workflow covers the entire\njourney from initial setup to final completion.\n\nCanonical readiness chain (registration to publication):\n\n1. Confirm season registration.\n2. Confirm tournament participant.\n3. Prepare active ready roster and match-day sheets.\n4. Publish schedule and run live operations.\n5. Approve results.\n6. Recompute/review standings.\n7. Publish tournament and standings surfaces.\n\nBlocking vs warning-only model:\n\n- Blocking: the step cannot proceed (for example, deadline-backed roster blockers\n   or unresolved publication validation blockers).\n- Warning-only: the step can proceed, but requires operator follow-up and may\n   require manager override logging depending on the surface.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Seasons, clubs, teams |\n| `sports_federation_rules` | Rule sets governing scoring, tie-breaks, eligibility |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Competition, tournament, stage, group, participant, match models |\n| `sports_federation_competition_core`, `sports_federation_registration` | Competition identity, lifecycle, registration, and participant finalization |\n| `sports_federation_format` | Versioned logical structures and stage graphs |\n| `sports_federation_calendar` | Physical match days, capacity, slots, and timelines |\n| `sports_federation_scheduling` | Deterministic fixture assignment and schedule validation |\n| `sports_federation_schedule_approval` | Schedule review and immutable publication snapshots |\n| `sports_federation_matchday` | Live operations after schedule publication |\n| `sports_federation_venues` | Venue and playing-area assignment |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings computation at each stage |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Participant-confirmation and publication notifications |\n| `sports_federation_public_site` | Public publication of tournament pages |\n\n## Verified UI navigation\n\nUse [`docs/COMPETITION_UI_WORKFLOW.md`](../docs/COMPETITION_UI_WORKFLOW.md). The main journey is under **Federation → Competition Workflow**; addon names below describe ownership, not menu labels.\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Competition Setup\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rules`, `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Define a **rule set** with scoring values (win/draw/loss points), tie-break\n   criteria, squad-size limits, and eligibility rules.\n2. Create a **competition** (e.g. \"National League Division 1\").\n3. Link the competition to the active season and the rule set.\n4. Set competition state to `active`.\n\n### 2. Tournament Creation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Under the competition, create a **tournament** (e.g. \"NL Div 1 — Season 2025\").\n2. Set tournament type: `league`, `cup`, `friendly`, or `playoff`.\n3. Assign date range, rule set (inherited from competition or overridden).\n4. Set maximum participants if applicable.\n5. If the competition is spread over multiple event days, plan the shared\n   schedule blocks directly on the stage rounds. Each round can carry a\n   calendar date and a venue, while the matches inside that round keep their\n   own kickoff times.\n6. Tournament starts in `draft` state.\n\n### 3. Venue Assignment\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_venues`\n\n1. Create or select venues with address, capacity, and playing areas.\n2. Link venues to the tournament via the `venues` Many2many field.\n3. Individual matches can later reference specific venues and playing areas.\n\n### 4. Participant Enrolment\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator (or via import)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`, `sports_federation_import_tools`\n\n1. Add **participants** to the tournament — each links a team to the tournament.\n    - If the flow starts from portal registration requests, an administrator first\n       confirms the `federation.competition.entry` record. That creates or links\n       a `federation.tournament.participant` record in state `registered`.\n    - That participant must still be moved to state `confirmed` before schedule\n       generation can use it.\n2. Optionally assign participants to specific stages and groups.\n3. Set seeding ranks for bracket placement.\n4. Participant states: `registered` → `confirmed` → `withdrawn` / `eliminated`.\n5. Participant confirmation can happen before the team has an active roster, but\n   only until one week before its first scheduled match, or one week before\n   tournament start if no match has been scheduled yet. Once that deadline is\n   reached, participant confirmation is blocked until the team has an active\n   ready roster. When both a competition-specific roster and a season-wide\n   roster are available, the competition-specific roster is used for readiness\n   checks.\n6. The participant form now surfaces the current roster deadline feedback inline\n   and exposes **Open Team Roster** when operators need to resolve the blocker\n   in the rosters flow before confirmation can continue.\n7. Confirming a participant sends an email to the team and club contacts.\n8. Move tournament to `open` state once enrolment is complete.\n\nBulk enrolment is available via the **Import Tournament Participants** wizard.\n\n### 5. Stage & Group Structure\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Create **stages** within the tournament (e.g. \"Group Phase\", \"Quarter-Finals\").\n2. Set stage type: `group`, `knockout`, `playoff`, or `other`.\n3. Order stages by sequence.\n4. Within each stage, create **groups** (e.g. \"Group A\", \"Pool 1\").\n5. Assign participants to groups.\n6. Create or review the stage rounds that should exist for each phase. Example:\n   rounds 1-4 for the round-robin stage, then knockout rounds on the final stage.\n\n### 6. Schedule Generation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Modules**: `sports_federation_format`, `sports_federation_calendar`,\n`sports_federation_scheduling`, `sports_federation_schedule_approval`, and\n`sports_federation_matchday`\n\nThe path is an explicit sequence of handovers:\n\n- Freeze the logical structure and stage graph in `sports_federation_format`.\n- Prepare physical match days and playable capacity in\n   `sports_federation_calendar`.\n- Generate or assign fixtures and validate the complete draft in\n   `sports_federation_scheduling`.\n- Submit the draft for review and publish an immutable snapshot through\n   `sports_federation_schedule_approval`.\n- Start live operations only from the published snapshot through\n   `sports_federation_matchday`.\n\n1. Move the competition into the state that permits scheduling.\n2. Registration finalizes and locks the confirmed participant set.\n3. Format freezes the structure and stage graph for the competition edition.\n   Round-robin and knockout generation remain deterministic and scoped to the\n   frozen structure.\n4. ++ {"content": "# ADR-0001: Portal Trust Boundaries\n\nLast updated: 2026-08-20\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nPortal club representatives and officials must create or update federation records without receiving broad backend ACLs. Controller-only checks are insufficient because direct model calls, guessed identifiers, or future routes could otherwise widen access.\n\n## Decision\n\nPortal writes use explicit, model-owned privilege boundaries:\n\n- Controllers resolve the request user and the candidate record, reject malformed input, and invoke a model-owned portal method.\n- Ownership and scope are enforced again in the model or shared privilege service.\n- Elevated reads and writes go through `federation.portal.privilege`, including helpers such as `elevate()`, `portal_search()`, `portal_create()`, `portal_write()`, and `portal_call()` where applicable.\n- The privilege boundary preserves the request user for audit attribution while keeping elevation narrow and explicit.\n- Controllers must not perform business writes through raw `sudo()`.\n- Positive in-scope, negative out-of-scope, direct-ID, and elevated-helper tests are mandatory for every privileged portal write surface.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Privilege escalation remains centralized and reviewable.\n- Controller and ORM boundaries fail closed independently.\n- Cross-club and team-scoped access can be regression-tested consistently.\n- New portal features must reuse the privilege service or add a reviewed model-owned equivalent.\n- Raw elevated controller writes are treated as security defects.\n", "content_length": 1629, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0001-portal-trust-boundaries.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "2c05056fbddc6d0400083a690deca702e9800c026de6e87185e537ebea6576fe", "size_bytes": 1629}
++ {"content": "# ADR-0002: Reporting SQL Views\n\nLast updated: 2026-04-18\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nFederation reporting combines finance, standings, compliance, notification, planning, and workflow data across multiple addons. Rebuilding those joins in controllers or repeated ORM loops would duplicate logic and create unpredictable performance.\n\n## Decision\n\nOperational and planning projections remain read-only analytical models backed by PostgreSQL views when their data is naturally cross-module or aggregation-heavy.\n\n- SQL-backed report models use `_auto = False`.\n- View definitions are recreated deterministically from `init()` or the repository's approved view helper.\n- Controllers and exports consume report models instead of embedding substantial SQL or cross-module aggregation logic.\n- Report models are read-only and must not masquerade as writable business records.\n- Heavy reports retain query budgets, representative fixtures, and performance watchpoints.\n- SQL view changes are upgrade-sensitive and require migration review evidence.\n- A normal stored Odoo model is preferred when the data has its own lifecycle or must be edited.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Cross-module reporting logic remains centralized.\n- Export and operator surfaces share the same projection semantics.\n- View dependencies and upgrade order require explicit review.\n- Maintainers must preserve query plans, migration safety, and read-only behavior.\n", "content_length": 1514, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0002-reporting-sql-views.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "ef36c1653fd664b1b66d727fab316472e1dd05aad0b7e71a28d0f01cd5a889ad", "size_bytes": 1514}

---{"content": "# Sports Federation Format\n\nThe format addon manages versioned competition structures, their stages, and\nFormat Studio stage graphs.\n\n## Stage graph models\n\nFormat Studio uses `federation.structure.stage.progression` for edges between\nstages in one `federation.competition.structure`. This is deliberately\nseparate from the competition engine's `federation.stage.progression` model,\nwhich belongs to tournament-level progression workflows and uses a different\nrelation contract.\n\nBefore generating a structure, the graph is validated for cycles. Root stages\ncan then be prepared; dependent stages wait for incoming progression results.\nApproved fixture results can populate dependent stages, and frozen standings\nare stored as immutable snapshots.\n\nStage-graph access rules are loaded from `security/ir.model.access.csv`. The\nstructure form extension identifies the stage tab by its `stage_ids` field so\nthe view remains safe when translated page labels change.\n## Supported format generation\n\nThe format studio now estimates fixture and round counts before generation. It supports single and double leagues, seeded knockout and placement brackets, match series, pool-to-knockout configuration, and championship/relegation splits. Dynamic Swiss, ladder, and double-elimination formats are deliberately not advertised as automatic because they require round-by-round or reset-final semantics outside the immutable fixture graph.\n", "content_length": 1428, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_format/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "7c527aeced8da21ff2fd2701dc53c9ce8e9d1586b33b663b7efda898a87f43dc", "size_bytes": 1428}

Swiss round counts are configurable on the structure, while double elimination uses the dynamic pairing service to account for its winner, loser, and reset-final routes. -- {"content": "# Sports Federation Governance\n\nFormal override-request workflow with decisions and audit trails. Provides a\nstructured way for federation officials to request, review, and implement\nexceptions to standard processes.\n\n## Purpose\n\nSome situations require bending the rules — late registrations, replayed matches,\nexceptional eligibility grants. This module ensures those exceptions are\n**requested, decided, logged, and auditable** rather than happening informally.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Core entities |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Player references |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournament references |\n| `mail` | Chatter |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.override.request`\n\nA formal request to override a standard process.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Request title |\n| `request_type` | Selection | Type of override |\n| `target_model` / `target_res_id` | Char / Integer | Linked record |\n| `requested_by_id` | Many2one | Requester (user) |\n| `requested_on` | Datetime | Request timestamp |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / submitted / approved / rejected / implemented / closed |\n| `reason` | Text | Justification |\n| `implementation_note` | Text | How it was applied |\n| `decision_ids` | One2many | Review decisions |\n| `audit_note_ids` | One2many | Audit trail entries |\n| `outcome_ids` | One2many | Post-decision outcome log |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → submitted → approved / rejected → implemented → closed, with submitted requests withdrawable back to draft before a decision is recorded.\n\n### `federation.override.decision`\n\nA review decision on an override request.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | The request |\n| `decision` | Selection | approve / reject / request_info |\n| `decided_by_id` | Many2one | Decision maker |\n| `decided_on` | Datetime | Decision timestamp |\n| `note` | Text | Reasoning |\n\n### `federation.audit.note`\n\nFree-form audit notes attached to an override request.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | The request |\n| `note` | Text | Audit remark |\n| `author_id` | Many2one | Author |\n| `created_on` | Datetime | Timestamp |\n\n### `federation.override.outcome`\n\nOutcome tracking row attached to an override request after implementation or\nfollow-up review.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | Source override request |\n| `outcome` | Selection | implemented / effective / partial / ineffective / reversed |\n| `outcome_on` | Datetime | When the outcome was recorded |\n| `recorded_by_id` | Many2one | Operator recording the outcome |\n| `request_type` | Selection | Snapshot of the originating request type |\n| `target_model` / `target_res_id` | Char / Integer | Snapshot of the overridden record |\n| `request_state` | Selection | Request state at the time of logging |\n| `note` | Text | Outcome commentary |\n\n## Security Groups\n\n| Group | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| Governance Officer | Can review and decide on override requests |\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Formal request lifecycle** — Every exception starts as a draft request,\n   can be withdrawn back to draft while still submitted, and otherwise follows\n   a structured approval flow.\n2. **Multi-decision support** — Multiple governance officers can weigh in on a\n   single request.\n3. **Audit trail** — All decisions and notes are timestamped and attributed.\n4. **Generic target** — Requests can link to any A menu can be hidden if the current user lacks the required role or record access.\n\n## Actual backend menu map\n\n```text\nFederation\n├── Setup\n│   ├── Core Records\n│   │   ├── Clubs\n│   │   └── Teams\n│   ├── Seasons\n│   ├── Season Registrations\n│   └── Competition Setup\n│       ├── Competition Templates\n│       ├── Season Competitions\n│       └── Rules & Policies\n├── Competition Workflow\n│   ├── Create Competition\n│   ├── Competition Overview\n│   ├── Registration Desk\n│   ├── Format Studio\n│   ├── Format Templates\n│   ├── Calendar Planner\n│   ├── Schedule Planner\n│   ├── Schedule Review Queue\n│   ├── Match-Day Control\n│   └── Technical Records\n├── Planning\n│   ├── Operational Action Queue\n│   └── Advanced Records\n│       ├── Divisions & Tournaments\n│       ├── Matches\n│       └── Tournament Structure\n├── Match Day\n│   ├── Match Sheets\n│   ├── Venues\n│   ├── Officiating\n│   └── Discipline\n├── Publication\n│   ├── Standings\n│   ├── Approved Schedules\n│   └── Schedule Publications\n└── Administration\n    ├── Reporting\n    │   └── Operational Health\n    ├── Retention and Recovery\n    ├── Retention Evidence\n    └── Operational Job Health\n```\n\nThere is no backend menu named **Competitions**, **Registrations**, **Scheduling**, **Schedule Approval**, **Results**, or **Competition Engine**. Those are concepts or addon names, not current navigation labels.\n\n## Actual club portal links\n\n```text\nMy Account\n├── Overview                 /my/competitions\n├── Action items             /my/action-items\n├── My teams                 /my/teams\n├── Season registrations     /my/season-registrations\n├── Match day                /my/match-day\n├── Officials                /my/referee-duties\n└── Results                  /my/results\n```\n\n## Complete workflow and recovery\n\n### 1. Prepare reusable setup\n\nUse:\n\n```text\nFederation > Setup > Seasons\nFederation > Setup > Competition Setup > Competition Templates\nFederation > Setup > Competition Setup > Rules & Policies > Rule Sets & Policies\nFederation > Setup > Core Records > Clubs\nFederation > Setup > Core Records > Teams\n```\n\nCreate the season, reusable competition definition, rule set, clubs, and teams. Points, tie-break, eligibility, and qualification components are below **Rules & Policies > Advanced Components**.\n\n**Recovery:** Edit unused records. Archive records that already have history. Do not delete referenced seasons, competitions, clubs, teams, or rule sets merely to restart a workflow.\n\n### 2. Create the season competition\n\nPreferred menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Create Competition\n```\n\nThe wizard selects the setup template, competition template, season, dates, optional rule set, registration dates, divisions, and responsibilities. It creates the season competition, divisions, registration windows, and role assignments, then opens the season competition.\n\nInspect the records through:\n\n```text\nFederation > Setup > Competition Setup > Season Competitions\nFederation > Planning > Advanced Records > Divisions & Tournaments\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Competition Overview\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Correct newly created records before clubs submit. There is no generic **Undo Competition Wizard** button. If downstream entries, fixtures, schedules, results, or publications exist, preserve the original records and create controlled replacements.\n\n### 3. Open registration and accept entries\n\nBackend:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Registration Desk\n```\n\nClub portal:\n\n```text\nMy Account > Season registrations\n```\n\nUse **Open Registration** on a draft registration window. Clubs prepare and submit entries. Managers review them in the Registration Desk.\n\n**Recovery:** Use **Close Registration** to stop submissions. A submitted entry can be withdrawn by the club or returned by the manager with a reason. A returned entry can be corrected and resubmitted. Rejection remains historical evidence.\n\n### 4. Finalize participants\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Registration Desk\n```\n\nClose the registration window and press **Finalize Participants**. The finalized participant set feeds the format structure.\n\n**Recovery:** Correct entries before finalization. If a finalized set is wrong and nothing depends on it, create a corrected set through the registration workflow. If fixtures or schedules exist, create a successor structure or schedule revision instead of mutating published history.\n\n### 5. Configure and generate the format\n\nMenus:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Templates\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio\n```\n\n**Format Templates** is manager-only. In **Format Studio**, select the season competition, division, finalized participant set, and format settings. Use **Check Feasibility**, then **Generate Fixtures**. For multi-stage structures use **Validate Stage Graph**. Once accepted, use **Freeze Structure**.\n\n**Recovery:** Before freeze, correct and regenerate. Once operational matches or frozen stage snapshots exist, create a new structure version. The current UI has no generic structure-unfreeze command.\n\n### 6. Prepare and progress stages\n\nThere is no standalone **Stage Progression** menu. Stage controls are on the structure opened from:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio\n```\n\nAvailable stage actions are **Prepare**, **Start**, and **Freeze & Progress**.\n\n**Recovery:** Correct a stage before starting it. Before progression, correct and recompute standings. Frozen snapshot lines are immutable; after progression use a corrected successor structure rather than editing evidence.\n\n### 7. Plan calendar capacity\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Calendar Planner\n```\n\nCreate match days, slot windows, and capacity, then use **Mark Capacity Ready**. Venue setup and constraints are under:\n\n```text\nFederation > Match Day > Venues\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Edit draft calendar records. If a schedule already uses the calendar, make the deliberate calendar correction and refresh the working schedule. Stale assignments are flagged, not silently deleted.\n\n### 8. Build the working schedule\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner\n```\n\nUse **Refresh Calendar Fixtures**. Assign dates, times, venues, and courts manually, or use **Auto-schedule**, **Preview**, and **Apply Auto-schedule**. Review fairness warnings.\n\n**Recovery:** Draft and change-requested schedules remain editable. A preview does not change the schedule until applied. Refresh fixtures, move assignments, or regenerate while mutable.\n\n### 9. Submit and review the schedule\n\nPlanner menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner\n```\n\nUse **Submit for Review**. Approver menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Review Queue\n```\n\nThe review exposes **Withdraw Submission**, **Request Changes**, and **Approve Schedule** according to state and role.\n\n**Recovery:** Withdraw a pending submission to return it to editing. Request changes to return it to the planner. If an approval is mistaken, do not publish; correct it through a new review cycle while preserving separation of duties.\n\n### 10. Publish the schedule\n\nUse **Publish Schedule** on an approved review. The two real publication menus are:\n\n```text\nFederation > Publication > Approved Schedules\nFederation > Publication > Schedule Publications\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Live publications are immutable. Open the published schedule under **Federation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner**, use **Amend Schedule**, enter a reason, and press **Create Amendment**. The replacement follows submit, review, approve, and publish again. The old publication becomes superseded. There is no in-place **Unpublish** button.\n\n### 11. Operate match day\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Match-Day Control\n```\n\nUse **Open Match Day** when ready. During operations use **Update Court**, **Report Incident**, or **Operational Schedule Change**. Finish with **Close Match Day**. Supporting records are under:\n\n```text\nFederation > Match Day > Match Sheets\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Technical Records > Incidents\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Technical Records > Operational Deviations\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Resolve incident and deviation records with **Resolve**. Operational changes are recorded rather than silently altering the approved publication. Correct the planning baseline through a schedule amendment.\n\n### 12. Submit and approve results\n\nBackend menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Planning > Advanced Records > Matches\n```\n\nResult Control extends the match form; there is no separate backend **Results** menu. The form provides **Submit Result**, **Verify Result**, **Approve Result**, **Raise Dispute / Request Exception**, **Correct Result**, and **Reset to Draft**.\n\nClub portal:\n\n```text\nMy Account > Results\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Reset an incorrect in-progress result to draft. Raise a dispute for governed review. Correct contested or approved results through **Correct Result**. Never silently edit an approved score.\n\n### 13. Recompute and freeze standings\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Publication > Standings\n```\n\nUse **Recompute** or **Queue Recompute**, inspect lines and tie-break notes, and then use **Freeze**.\n\n**Recovery:** Recompute while unfrozen. For a frozen standing, use **Unfreeze**, correct the source result or rule, use **Force Recompute**, and freeze again. Failed asynchronous work appears under the nested **Recompute Queue**.\n\n### 14. Monitor exceptions\n\nMenus:\n\n```text\nFederation > Planning > Operational Action Queue\nFederation > Administration > Reporting > Operational Health\nFederation > Administration > Operational Job Health\n```\n\nUse source links to correct business records in their owning workflow. Override this\nwith `RELEASE_BASELINE_EVIDENCE_DIR` when CI provides a dedicated artifact\ndirectory.\n\n### Exit criteria\n\n- One immutable candidate SHA is recorded in every evidence file.\n- Test failures and errors are zero.\n- Static, ownership, workflow, migration, publication, and security contracts pass.\n- Performance budgets pass.\n- Browser lifecycle, finance, and public-site tours pass.\n- Local and GitHub release-candidate validation agree on the same commit.\n- The worktree is clean before qualification starts.\n\n## Release Candidate and Migration Evidence\n\nStatus: **Implemented, pending rehearsal with an approved backup**\n\n### Objective\n\nProve deployment and recovery against a representative pre-refactor database and\nmatching filestore.\n\n### Automation\n\nRun the complete migration rehearsal from a clean candidate checkout:\n\n```bash\nscripts/ci/run_migration_rehearsal.sh \\\n  --backup-dir /path/to/approved-backup \\\n  --rollback-owner \"Release owner\" \\\n  --rollback-trigger \"Invariant comparison or acceptance validation fails\" \\\n  --yes\n```\n\nThe command restores the source backup, captures pre-upgrade invariants, upgrades\nthe restored database, captures post-upgrade invariants, runs role-separated\nacceptance, restores the same backup into an independent rollback database, and\ncompares all evidence. Evidence is written under\n`artifacts/release/migration/` by default.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n- production-like database and filestore restore;\n- pre-upgrade invariant snapshot;\n- reviewed module upgrade;\n- post-upgrade invariant comparison;\n- role-separated operator pilot;\n- backup checksum and restore evidence;\n- rollback drill with named owner and trigger;\n- archived RC logs and machine-readable evidence.\n\n### Exit criteria\n\nThe upgraded copy preserves competition, registration, fixture, schedule,\npublication, match-day, result, standings, portal, public, integration, and\nattachment invariants. Restore and rollback complete from the recorded backup.\n\n## Simplified Competition Journey\n\nStatus: **Implemented**\n\n### Objective\n\nAllow a normal league, tournament day, or cup to be configured, scheduled,\napproved, and published without exposing the underlying Odoo model structure.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n- template-led competition creation;\n- guided Basics, Participants, Format, Calendar, Schedule, Publish journey;\n- user-facing Draft, Ready, Live, Finished presentation states;\n- visible blockers, responsible role, and next action;\n- advanced stage graph, revision, fairness, and shared-day controls separated\n  from the normal path;\n- task-first club portal.\n\n### Reversibility contract\n\n- Setup templates apply editable defaults and can be cancelled.\n- Late fixtures can be added to or removed from calendar allocations.\n- Draft and change-requested schedules refresh from the current calendar plan without deleting assignments.\n- Submitting planners can withdraw pending reviews; approver-requested changes return the same schedule to an editable state.\n- Published evidence stays immutable and corrections use a linked replacement revision.\n\n### Exit criteria\n\nA trained non-developer completes the normal journey without developer mode, direct model navigation, manual progression mapping, or shell access. Every pre-publication handoff has an explicit return path; post-publication changes use traceable replacement revisions.\n\n## Operational Job Reliability\n\nStatus: **Implemented**\n\n### Objective\n\nGeneralize the proven standings recompute reliability pattern without moving\ndomain execution out of its owning addon.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n- bounded retry and backoff;\n- stale-running recovery;\n- dead-letter/operator-action state;\n- correlation IDs and sanitized error evidence;\n- idempotent manual retry;\n- operator visibility for notification, report, integration, retention, and\n  snapshot jobs;\n- shared infrastructure only after two proven consumers exist.\n\n### Implementation\n\nThe shared `federation.operation.job` queue records source ownership, attempts,\nretry timing, correlation IDs, stale-worker recovery, terminal operator action,\nand manual retry. It complements module tests\nby proving that one federation storyline can be followed across ownership\nboundaries without hidden setup or direct database edits.\n\n## Automated gate\n\nRun the complete release-focus verification:\n\n```bash\npython3 ci/check_release_focus_contract.py\nscripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh focus\n```\n\nThe focus lane runs the lifecycle, finance, and public browser tours together\nwith the schedule-amendment, approval immutability, officiating, governance,\nportal-security, compliance, and pilot-readiness tests.\n\n## Pilot storyline\n\n1. Create a season and competition edition.\n2. Open registration and finalize the participant set.\n3. Freeze the competition structure and generate fixtures.\n4. Prepare match-day capacity and assign every fixture to a slot.\n5. Submit the schedule for independent review and publish the approved revision.\n6. Assign named officials or a club officiating duty and resolve shortages.\n7. Open match-day control, record results, and approve official results.\n8. Recompute and publish standings.\n9. Confirm the public competition, schedule, format, and standings pages.\n10. Confirm finance-event creation, settlement, export readiness, and traceability.\n11. Amend one published schedule through a replacement revision and verify that\n    the original publication and audit evidence remain immutable.\n12. Verify that an unrelated portal user cannot read or mutate another club's\n    registration, roster, officiating, result, or compliance records.\n\n## Acceptance evidence\n\nRecord the release-candidate commit, database name, commands, start/end time,\nall automated results, and any manual observations in the release runbook. A\nrelease candidate is not accepted while any focus-lane test is skipped, flaky,\nor dependent on manual data repair.\n\n## Role-separated acceptance gate\n\nRun the operator-role contract before the browser pilot:\n\n```bash\nscripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh focus\n```\n\nThe pilot must use distinct registration, format, calendar, schedule-planning, schedule-approval, and match-day operators.
