Those are concepts or addon names, not current navigation labels.\n\n## Actual club portal links\n\n```text\nMy Account\n├── Overview                 /my/competitions\n├── Action items             /my/action-items\n├── My teams                 /my/teams\n├── Season registrations     /my/season-registrations\n├── Match day                /my/match-day\n├── Officials                /my/referee-duties\n└── Results                  /my/results\n```\n\n## Complete workflow and recovery\n\n### 1. Prepare reusable setup\n\nUse:\n\n```text\nFederation > Setup > Seasons\nFederation > Setup > Competition Setup > Competition Templates\nFederation > Setup > Competition Setup > Rules & Policies > Rule Sets & Policies\nFederation > Setup > Core Records > Clubs\nFederation > Setup > Core Records > Teams\n```\n\nCreate the season, reusable competition definition, rule set, clubs, and teams. Points, tie-break, eligibility, and qualification components are below **Rules & Policies > Advanced Components**.\n\n**Recovery:** Edit unused records. Archive records that already have history. Do not delete referenced seasons, competitions, clubs, teams, or rule sets merely to restart a workflow.\n\n### 2. Create the season competition\n\nPreferred menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Create Competition\n```\n\nThe wizard selects the setup template, competition template, season, dates, optional rule set, registration dates, divisions, and responsibilities. It creates the season competition, divisions, registration windows, and role assignments, then opens the season competition.\n\nInspect the records through:\n\n```text\nFederation > Setup > Competition Setup > Season Competitions\nFederation > Planning > Advanced Records > Divisions & Tournaments\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Competition Overview\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Correct newly created records before clubs submit. There is no generic **Undo Competition Wizard** button. If downstream entries, fixtures, schedules, results, or publications exist, preserve the original records and create controlled replacements.\n\n### 3. Open registration and accept entries\n\nBackend:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Registration Desk\n```\n\nClub portal:\n\n```text\nMy Account > Season registrations\n```\n\nUse **Open Registration** on a draft registration window. Clubs prepare and submit entries. Managers review them in the Registration Desk.\n\n**Recovery:** Use **Close Registration** to stop submissions. A submitted entry can be withdrawn by the club or returned by the manager with a reason. A returned entry can be corrected and resubmitted. Rejection remains historical evidence.\n\n### 4. Finalize participants\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Registration Desk\n```\n\nClose the registration window and press **Finalize Participants**. The finalized participant set feeds the format structure.\n\n**Recovery:** Correct entries before finalization. If a finalized set is wrong and nothing depends on it, create a corrected set through the registration workflow. If fixtures or schedules exist, create a successor structure or schedule revision instead of mutating published history.\n\n### 5. Configure and generate the format\n\nMenus:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Templates\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio\n```\n\n**Format Templates** is manager-only. In **Format Studio**, select the season competition, division, finalized participant set, and format settings. Use **Check Feasibility**, then **Generate Fixtures**. For multi-stage structures use **Validate Stage Graph**. Once accepted, use **Freeze Structure**.\n\n**Recovery:** Before freeze, correct and regenerate. Once operational matches or frozen stage snapshots exist, create a new structure version. The current UI has no generic structure-unfreeze command.\n\n### 6. Prepare and progress stages\n\nThere is no standalone **Stage Progression** menu. Stage controls are on the structure opened from:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio\n```\n\nAvailable stage actions are **Prepare**, **Start**, and **Freeze & Progress**.\n\n**Recovery:** Correct a stage before starting it. Before progression, correct and recompute standings. Frozen snapshot lines are immutable; after progression use a corrected successor structure rather than editing evidence.\n\n### 7. Plan calendar capacity\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Calendar Planner\n```\n\nCreate match days, slot windows, and capacity, then use **Mark Capacity Ready**. Venue setup and constraints are under:\n\n```text\nFederation > Match Day > Venues\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Edit draft calendar records. If a schedule already uses the calendar, make the deliberate calendar correction and refresh the working schedule. Stale assignments are flagged, not silently deleted.\n\n### 8. Build the working schedule\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner\n```\n\nUse **Refresh Calendar Fixtures**. Assign dates, times, venues, and courts manually, or use **Auto-schedule**, **Preview**, and **Apply Auto-schedule**. Review fairness warnings.\n\n**Recovery:** Draft and change-requested schedules remain editable. A preview does not change the schedule until applied. Refresh fixtures, move assignments, or regenerate while mutable.\n\n### 9. Submit and review the schedule\n\nPlanner menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner\n```\n\nUse **Submit for Review**. Approver menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Review Queue\n```\n\nThe review exposes **Withdraw Submission**, **Request Changes**, and **Approve Schedule** according to state and role.\n\n**Recovery:** Withdraw a pending submission to return it to editing. Request changes to return it to the planner. If an approval is mistaken, do not publish; correct it through a new review cycle while preserving separation of duties.\n\n### 10. Publish the schedule\n\nUse **Publish Schedule** on an approved review. The two real publication menus are:\n\n```text\nFederation > Publication > Approved Schedules\nFederation > Publication > Schedule Publications\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Live publications are immutable. Open the published schedule under **Federation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner**, use **Amend Schedule**, enter a reason, and press **Create Amendment**. The replacement follows submit, review, approve, and publish again. The old publication becomes superseded. There is no in-place **Unpublish** button.\n\n### 11. Operate match day\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Match-Day Control\n```\n\nUse **Open Match Day** when ready. During operations use **Update Court**, **Report Incident**, or **Operational Schedule Change**. Finish with **Close Match Day**. Supporting records are under:\n\n```text\nFederation > Match Day > Match Sheets\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Technical Records > Incidents\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Technical Records > Operational Deviations\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Resolve incident and deviation records with **Resolve**. Operational changes are recorded rather than silently altering the approved publication. Correct the planning baseline through a schedule amendment.\n\n### 12. Submit and approve results\n\nBackend menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Planning > Advanced Records > Matches\n```\n\nResult Control extends the match form; there is no separate backend **Results** menu. The form provides **Submit Result**, **Verify Result**, **Approve Result**, **Raise Dispute / Request Exception**, **Correct Result**, and **Reset to Draft**.\n\nClub portal:\n\n```text\nMy Account > Results\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Reset an incorrect in-progress result to draft. Raise a dispute for governed review. Correct contested or approved results through **Correct Result**. Never silently edit an approved score.\n\n### 13. Recompute and freeze standings\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Publication > Standings\n```\n\nUse **Recompute** or **Queue Recompute**, inspect lines and tie-break notes, and then use **Freeze**.\n\n**Recovery:** Recompute while unfrozen. For a frozen standing, use **Unfreeze**, correct the source result or rule, use **Force Recompute**, and freeze again. Failed asynchronous work appears under the nested **Recompute Queue**.\n\n### 14. Monitor exceptions\n\nMenus:\n\n```text\nFederation > Planning > Operational Action Queue\nFederation > Administration > Reporting > Operational Health\nFederation > Administration > Operational Job Health\n```\n\nUse source links to correct business records in their owning workflow. Retry only retryable jobs.\n\n## Required terminology in operator documentation\n\n- Use **Federation > Competition Workflow**, not “Competition Engine”.\n- Use **Registration Desk**, not “Registration Windows” as a menu.\n- Use **Schedule Planner**, not “Scheduling > Schedules”.\n- Use **Schedule Review Queue**, not “Schedule Approval > Reviews”.\n- Use **Publication > Schedule Publications**, not “Schedule Approval > Publications”.\n- Use **Planning > Advanced Records > Matches**, not “Results > Match Results”.\n- Use **Publication > Standings**, not “Standings > Standings”.\n- Use **Format Studio** for stage progression; there is no standalone progression menu.\n", "content_length": 10699, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "untracked", "path": "docs/COMPETITION_UI_WORKFLOW.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "cd08e472281fa27aa4999aa4f0206a44e569cde6e1abcb981f0b34229033f40a", "size_bytes": 11089}

Evidence is written under\n`artifacts/release/migration/` by default.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n- production-like database and filestore restore;\n- pre-upgrade invariant snapshot;\n- reviewed module upgrade;\n- post-upgrade invariant comparison;\n- role-separated operator pilot;\n- backup checksum and restore evidence;\n- rollback drill with named owner and trigger;\n- archived RC logs and machine-readable evidence.\n\n### Exit criteria\n\nThe upgraded copy preserves competition, registration, fixture, schedule,\npublication, match-day, result, standings, portal, public, integration, and\nattachment invariants. Restore and rollback complete from the recorded backup.\n\n## Simplified Competition Journey\n\nStatus: **Implemented**\n\n### Objective\n\nAllow a normal league, tournament day, or cup to be configured, scheduled,\napproved, and published without exposing the underlying Odoo model structure.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n- template-led competition creation;\n- guided Basics, Participants, Format, Calendar, Schedule, Publish journey;\n- user-facing Draft, Ready, Live, Finished presentation states;\n- visible blockers, responsible role, and next action;\n- advanced stage graph, revision, fairness, and shared-day controls separated\n  from the normal path;\n- task-first club portal.\n\n### Reversibility contract\n\n- Setup templates apply editable defaults and can be cancelled.\n- Late fixtures can be added to or removed from calendar allocations.\n- Draft and change-requested schedules refresh from the current calendar plan without deleting assignments.\n- Submitting planners can withdraw pending reviews; approver-requested changes return the same schedule to an editable state.\n- Published evidence stays immutable and corrections use a linked replacement revision.\n\n### Exit criteria\n\nA trained non-developer completes the normal journey without developer mode, direct model navigation, manual progression mapping, or shell access. Prepare reusable setup\n\nUse:\n\n```text\nFederation > Setup > Seasons\nFederation > Setup > Competition Setup > Competition Templates\nFederation > Setup > Competition Setup > Rules & Policies > Rule Sets & Policies\nFederation > Setup > Core Records > Clubs\nFederation > Setup > Core Records > Teams\n```\n\nCreate the season, reusable competition definition, rule set, clubs, and teams. Points, tie-break, eligibility, and qualification components are below **Rules & Policies > Advanced Components**.\n\n**Recovery:** Edit unused records. Archive records that already have history. Do not delete referenced seasons, competitions, clubs, teams, or rule sets merely to restart a workflow.\n\n### 2. Create the season competition\n\nPreferred menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Create Competition\n```\n\nThe wizard selects the setup template, competition template, season, dates, optional rule set, registration dates, divisions, and responsibilities. It creates the season competition, divisions, registration windows, and role assignments, then opens the season competition.\n\nInspect the records through:\n\n```text\nFederation > Setup > Competition Setup > Season Competitions\nFederation > Planning > Advanced Records > Divisions & Tournaments\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Competition Overview\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Correct newly created records before clubs submit. There is no generic **Undo Competition Wizard** button. If downstream entries, fixtures, schedules, results, or publications exist, preserve the original records and create controlled replacements.\n\n### 3. Open registration and accept entries\n\nBackend:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Registration Desk\n```\n\nClub portal:\n\n```text\nMy Account > Season registrations\n```\n\nUse **Open Registration** on a draft registration window. Clubs prepare and submit entries. Managers review them in the Registration Desk.\n\n**Recovery:** Use **Close Registration** to stop submissions. A submitted entry can be withdrawn by the club or returned by the manager with a reason. A returned entry can be corrected and resubmitted. Rejection remains historical evidence.\n\n### 4. Finalize participants\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Registration Desk\n```\n\nClose the registration window and press **Finalize Participants**. The finalized participant set feeds the format structure.\n\n**Recovery:** Correct entries before finalization. If a finalized set is wrong and nothing depends on it, create a corrected set through the registration workflow. If fixtures or schedules exist, create a successor structure or schedule revision instead of mutating published history.\n\n### 5. Configure and generate the format\n\nMenus:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Templates\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio\n```\n\n**Format Templates** is manager-only. In **Format Studio**, select the season competition, division, finalized participant set, and format settings. Use **Check Feasibility**, then **Generate Fixtures**. For multi-stage structures use **Validate Stage Graph**. Once accepted, use **Freeze Structure**.\n\n**Recovery:** Before freeze, correct and regenerate. Once operational matches or frozen stage snapshots exist, create a new structure version. The current UI has no generic structure-unfreeze command.\n\n### 6. Prepare and progress stages\n\nThere is no standalone **Stage Progression** menu. Stage controls are on the structure opened from:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio\n```\n\nAvailable stage actions are **Prepare**, **Start**, and **Freeze & Progress**.\n\n**Recovery:** Correct a stage before starting it. Before progression, correct and recompute standings. Frozen snapshot lines are immutable; after progression use a corrected successor structure rather than editing evidence.\n\n### 7. Plan calendar capacity\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Calendar Planner\n```\n\nCreate match days, slot windows, and capacity, then use **Mark Capacity Ready**. Venue setup and constraints are under:\n\n```text\nFederation > Match Day > Venues\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Edit draft calendar records. If a schedule already uses the calendar, make the deliberate calendar correction and refresh the working schedule. Stale assignments are flagged, not silently deleted.\n\n### 8. Build the working schedule\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner\n```\n\nUse **Refresh Calendar Fixtures**. Assign dates, times, venues, and courts manually, or use **Auto-schedule**, **Preview**, and **Apply Auto-schedule**. Review fairness warnings.\n\n**Recovery:** Draft and change-requested schedules remain editable. A preview does not change the schedule until applied. Refresh fixtures, move assignments, or regenerate while mutable.\n\n### 9. Submit and review the schedule\n\nPlanner menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner\n```\n\nUse **Submit for Review**. Approver menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Review Queue\n```\n\nThe review exposes **Withdraw Submission**, **Request Changes**, and **Approve Schedule** according to state and role.\n\n**Recovery:** Withdraw a pending submission to return it to editing. Request changes to return it to the planner. If an approval is mistaken, do not publish; correct it through a new review cycle while preserving separation of duties.\n\n### 10. Publish the schedule\n\nUse **Publish Schedule** on an approved review. The two real publication menus are:\n\n```text\nFederation > Publication > Approved Schedules\nFederation > Publication > Schedule Publications\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Live publications are immutable. Open the published schedule under **Federation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner**, use **Amend Schedule**, enter a reason, and press **Create Amendment**. The replacement follows submit, review, approve, and publish again. The old publication becomes superseded. There is no in-place **Unpublish** button.\n\n### 11. Operate match day\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Match-Day Control\n```\n\nUse **Open Match Day** when ready. During operations use **Update Court**, **Report Incident**, or **Operational Schedule Change**. Finish with **Close Match Day**. Supporting records are under:\n\n```text\nFederation > Match Day > Match Sheets\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Technical Records > Incidents\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Technical Records > Operational Deviations\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Resolve incident and deviation records with **Resolve**. Operational changes are recorded rather than silently altering the approved publication. Correct the planning baseline through a schedule amendment.\n\n### 12. Submit and approve results\n\nBackend menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Planning > Advanced Records > Matches\n```\n\nResult Control extends the match form; there is no separate backend **Results** menu. The form provides **Submit Result**, **Verify Result**, **Approve Result**, **Raise Dispute / Request Exception**, **Correct Result**, and **Reset to Draft**.\n\nClub portal:\n\n```text\nMy Account > Results\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Reset an incorrect in-progress result to draft. Raise a dispute for governed review. Correct contested or approved results through **Correct Result**. Never silently edit an approved score.\n\n### 13. Recompute and freeze standings\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Publication > Standings\n```\n\nUse **Recompute** or **Queue Recompute**, inspect lines and tie-break notes, and then use **Freeze**.\n\n**Recovery:** Recompute while unfrozen. For a frozen standing, use **Unfreeze**, correct the source result or rule, use **Force Recompute**, and freeze again. Failed asynchronous work appears under the nested **Recompute Queue**.\n\n### 14. Monitor exceptions\n\nMenus:\n\n```text\nFederation > Planning > Operational Action Queue\nFederation > Administration > Reporting > Operational Health\nFederation > Administration > Operational Job Health\n```\n\nUse source links to correct business records in their owning workflow. Retry only retryable jobs.\n\n## Required terminology in operator documentation\n\n- Use **Federation > Competition Workflow**, not “Competition Engine”.\n- Use **Registration Desk**, not “Registration Windows” as a menu.\n- Use **Schedule Planner**, not “Scheduling > Schedules”.\n- Use **Schedule Review Queue**, not “Schedule Approval > Reviews”.\n- Use **Publication > Schedule Publications**, not “Schedule Approval > Publications”.\n- Use **Planning > Advanced Records > Matches**, not “Results > Match Results”.\n- Use **Publication > Standings**, not “Standings > Standings”.\n- Use **Format Studio** for stage progression; there is no standalone progression menu.\n", "content_length": 10699, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "docs/COMPETITION_UI_WORKFLOW.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "cd08e472281fa27aa4999aa4f0206a44e569cde6e1abcb981f0b34229033f40a", "size_bytes": 11089}

+--{"content": "# sports_federation_demo\n\nDeterministic demo-data pack for the Sports Federation Odoo addons.\n\nPurpose\n- Seed a development or showcase database with realistic federation records.\n- Provide a repeatable baseline for onboarding, manual QA, and guided product demos.\n\nWhat it loads\n- Clubs, teams, players, seasons, registrations, tournaments, participants, and matches.\n- Supporting records used by rosters, standings, compliance, discipline, and notifications.\n\nHow to use\n1. Install the module with demo data enabled in Odoo.\n2. Open core workflows from tournament setup through match completion.\n3. Reset by recreating the database when you need a fresh deterministic dataset.\n\nScope and constraints\n- This module is for non-production environments.\n- Demo records prioritize workflow coverage over real-world data volume.\n- The seeded Spring Cup intentionally omits category and gender restrictions\n  because its participant fixture demonstrates senior, youth, and women's\n  teams in one navigable competition.\n- Data is versioned with the addon and intended to stay reproducible across installs.\n\nValidation checklist\n- Module installs without additional manual data steps.\n- Tournament, roster, and standings flows are navigable from seeded records.\n- Portal/public pages can render at least one realistic competition storyline.\n\n## Release-pilot qualification\n\nThe integrated P0-P3 release path is documented in\n`docs/RELEASE_PILOT_SCENARIO.md`. Run\n`scripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh focus` before promoting a release candidate.\n\n## Accessible operator training walkthrough\n\nUse the deterministic demo database with a federation manager who also has the\ncompetition administrator, registration manager, competition designer, calendar\nplanner, schedule planner, schedule approver, and match-day manager roles.\n\nComplete the normal path without a mouse:\n\n1. Open **Competition Overview** and move through controls with `Tab` and\n   `Shift+Tab`. The focused control must always have a visible outline.\n2. Continue through **Registration**, **Format**, **Calendar**, **Schedule**, and\n   **Review**, activating links and buttons with `Enter` or `Space`.\n3. Submit an incomplete portal form. Focus must move to the error summary, and\n   invalid controls must reference that summary through `aria-describedby`.\n4. Open and close a confirmation modal. Focus must enter the modal and return to\n   the control that opened it.\n5. Repeat the club portal's competition, roster, officiating, and result tasks at\n   a 390 CSS-pixel viewport. No primary action may require horizontal page\n   scrolling.\n6. Confirm that every state is expressed as readable text. Color and icons may\n   reinforce the state but must not be the only status signal.\n\nThe `keyboard_competition_setup` browser tour qualifies the canonical backend\njourney mechanically. Portal template accessibility and mobile tests qualify\nlabels, error semantics, status text, responsive tables, and action wrapping.\n", "content_length": 2969, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_demo/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "c135482f0b4d180a6b56d126cc1cb96d95e7e81cce8c339291b086ff9f5e09da", "size_bytes": 2969}

Many2one | Resolved season scope for planning and reporting |\n| `partner_id` | Many2one | Related partner |\n| `club_id` / `player_id` / `referee_id` | Many2one | Federation entity |\n| `invoice_ref` / `external_ref` | Char | External references |\n| `handoff_state` | Selection | pending_export / exported / reconciled / closed |\n| `accounting_batch_ref` / `reconciliation_ref` | Char | Accounting handoff references |\n| `notes` | Text | Details |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → confirmed → settled / cancelled.\n- **Handoff state machine**: pending_export → exported → reconciled → closed.\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Source traceability** — Every finance event links back to its originating record\n   (registration, sanction, assignment) via model/res_id.\n2. **Fee catalogue** — Standardised fee types with default amounts.\n3. **Accounting-ready** — `invoice_ref` and `external_ref` keep the bridge ready\n   for future accounting integration while the current lightweight workflow ends\n   in `settled`.\n4. **Idempotent automation** — source-driven helpers reuse or reactivate matching\n  draft finance events instead of duplicating them on workflow re-entry.\n5. **Multi-entity** — Covers intelligence support** — finance events infer a season scope from\n  their source record whenever possible so reporting and budget views can roll\n  up actuals without duplicate data entry.\n8. **Operator-safe batch invoicing** — list-view \"Create Invoices\" now reports\n  per-event failures instead of silently skipping exceptions, so reconciliation\n  issues are visible immediately.\n\n### `federation.season.budget`\n\nPlanning baseline per season and fee type.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `season_id` / `fee_type_id` | Many2one | Budget scope |\n| `budget_amount` | Monetary | Planned amount |\n| `actual_amount` | Monetary | Confirmed and settled actuals for the same scope |\n| `actual_event_count` | Integer | Count of matching actual finance events |\n| `variance_amount` / `variance_pct` | Monetary / Float | Planned vs actual variance |\n| `notes` | Text | Budget commentary |\n\nThe backend exposes season budgets under Federation > Finance and provides a\nstat button that opens the scoped finance events behind the variance figures.\n\n## Accounting Handoff Contract\n\nThe finance bridge now supports an explicit accounting handoff workflow:\n\n- `action_mark_exported()` marks confirmed or settled events as exported\n- `action_mark_reconciled()` requires settlement and an exported handoff state\n- version, handoff state, accounting batch reference,\n  reconciliation reference, source traceability, and execution timestamps\n\n## Season Registration Finance Hooks\n\nThe finance bridge now Uncheck `Dry Run` in the wizard to create real records.\n- Wizard UI names: \"Import Clubs\", \"Import Teams\", \"Import Players\", \"Import Tournament Participants\" (available in the module menu).\n\nHow to use manually:\n- Go to the corresponding import wizard in the Odoo backend (see UI names above).\n- Upload the CSV file and click \"Parse & Import\".\n- Inspect the result message for errors and counts.\n\nThese CSVs include a few rows that intentionally demonstrate common cases:\n- duplicate rows (teams.csv) — to see duplicate detection\n- missing required fields (clubs.csv, teams.csv) — to see validation errors\n- invalid date (players.csv) — to see date parsing error\n- missing references (players.csv, tournament_participants.csv) — to see not-found errors\n\nIf you want, I can also add a small script to auto-load these files into the wizards for automated tests or provide sample `base64` encodings used by unit tests.\n", "content_length": 1688, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_import_tools/demo_csvs/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "98db34c8c1524357c8a0c112072310de04326216fbeda0d10edd9046d7c71dfb", "size_bytes": 1704}

-  {"content": "# Sports Federation Club Roles and Portal\n\nVersion: 19.0.4.1.0\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nRole-oriented self-service portal for club representatives, officials, and tournament operators.\n\n## Primary user journeys\n\n### Club representative\n\n- manage club teams and players\n- submit season and tournament registrations\n- prepare and activate rosters\n- complete match sheets and readiness tasks\n- nominate officials\n- review result actions and deadlines\n\n### Official\n\n- view assignments\n- confirm or decline within the authorized scope\n- access relevant match information\n\n### Tournament operator\n\n- use the tournament operations board\n- monitor courts, matches, readiness, and action queues\n- execute scoped result and operational actions\n\n## Trust boundary\n\nAll privileged portal writes must use a model-owned method and the shared `federation.portal.privilege` boundary. Controllers validate input and resolve scope but do not perform raw elevated business writes. See `adr/0001-portal-trust-boundaries.md`.\n\nEvery new privileged route requires:\n\n1. positive in-scope coverage\n2. negative out-of-scope coverage\n3. direct-ID or guessed-record coverage\n4. model/helper ownership assertions when elevation is used\n5. CSRF enforcement for state-changing browser or JSON-RPC routes\n\n## Portal UX direction\n\nThe landing page should remain task-first. Common tasks are teams, registrations, upcoming matches, and action items. Specialist tools should be progressively disclosed instead of presented as an undifferentiated module catalogue.\n\n## Operations board\n\nThe board loads through scoped JSON-RPC, supports polling and structured failures, and exposes only matches and actions available to the current user. Server-side checks remain authoritative.\n\n## Tests\n\nThe module includes HTTP smoke, ownership, access-denied, team, player, roster, registration, officiating, result, accessibility, mobile, operations-board, and end-to-end portal workflow tests.\n\n## Consolidated documentation\n\n`PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_COVERAGE.md`, `PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_TEST_MATRIX.md`, and `ROADMAP_RC.md` are deleted. Their durable rules are consolidated here and in ADR-0001; the test files are the authoritative live coverage map.\n\n## competition portal\n\nThe active competition portal is edition-based. Participation comes from\ncompetition entries and finalized participant sets. Match-day schedule data is\nrendered only from each match day's current live publication. Draft schedules,\nreview evidence and superseded publications are intentionally unavailable.\n\nPrimary routes:\n\n- `/my/competitions`\n- `/my/competition-entries`\n- `/my/match-days`\n- `/sports/match-days/<id>/operations`\n\nLegacy tournament workspace routes are redirect-only and render no V1 data.\nThe backend tournament-registration action is loaded before the menus that use\nit, so a fresh module install and an upgrade both build the registration menu\nwithout relying on stale database metadata.\n\n\n## Accessible error recovery and focus management\n\nPortal forms move keyboard focus to server-rendered error summaries, connect\ninvalid controls to that summary with `aria-describedby`, and announce the\nsummary through an assertive live region. Bootstrap confirmation dialogs move\nfocus into the dialog and restore it to the invoking control when closed.\nKeyboard focus uses a visible outline that does not depend on color-only status\ncues. The focused accessibility suite covers these contracts together with\nmobile table and action wrapping.\n", "content_length": 3540, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_portal/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "3ea4f6e8c7c0686f04a9a5a78e3b76b66861847771f9655441258519bd4016a5", "size_bytes": 3540}

Controllers validate input and resolve scope but do not perform raw elevated business writes. See `adr/0001-portal-trust-boundaries.md`.\n\nEvery new privileged route requires:\n\n1. positive in-scope coverage\n2. negative out-of-scope coverage\n3. direct-ID or guessed-record coverage\n4. model/helper ownership assertions when elevation is used\n5. CSRF enforcement for state-changing browser or JSON-RPC routes\n\n## Portal UX direction\n\nThe landing page should remain task-first. Common tasks are teams, registrations, upcoming matches, and action items. Specialist tools should be progressively disclosed instead of presented as an undifferentiated module catalogue.\n\n## Operations board\n\nThe board loads through scoped JSON-RPC, supports polling and structured failures, and exposes only matches and actions available to the current user. Server-side checks remain authoritative.\n\n## Tests\n\nThe module includes HTTP smoke, ownership, access-denied, team, player, roster, registration, officiating, result, accessibility, mobile, operations-board, and end-to-end portal workflow tests.\n\n## Consolidated documentation\n\n`PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_COVERAGE.md`, `PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_TEST_MATRIX.md`, and `ROADMAP_RC.md` are deleted. Their durable rules are consolidated here and in ADR-0001; the test files are the authoritative live coverage map.\n\n## competition portal\n\nThe active competition portal is edition-based. Participation comes from\ncompetition entries and finalized participant sets. Match-day schedule data is\nrendered only from each match day's current live publication. Draft schedules,\nreview evidence and superseded publications are intentionally unavailable.\n\nPrimary routes:\n\n- `/my/competitions`\n- `/my/competition-entries`\n- `/my/match-days`\n- `/sports/match-days/<id>/operations`\n\nLegacy tournament workspace routes are redirect-only and render no V1 data.\nThe backend tournament-registration action is loaded before the menus that use\nit, so a fresh module install and an upgrade both build the registration menu\nwithout relying on stale database metadata.\n\n\n## Accessible error recovery and focus management\n\nPortal forms move keyboard focus to server-rendered error summaries, connect\ninvalid controls to that summary with `aria-describedby`, and announce the\nsummary through an assertive live region. Bootstrap confirmation dialogs move\nfocus into the dialog and restore it to the invoking control when closed.\nKeyboard focus uses a visible outline that does not depend on color-only status\ncues. The focused accessibility suite covers these contracts together with\nmobile table and action wrapping.\n", "content_length": 3540, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_portal/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "3ea4f6e8c7c0686f04a9a5a78e3b76b66861847771f9655441258519bd4016a5", "size_bytes": 3540}

-+-{"content": "Sports Federation Standings\n===========================\n\nComputes and stores league-style standings tables for tournament stages and\ngroups. Aggregates match results into a ranked table with points, wins,\nlosses, goal differences, and configurable tie-break ordering.\n\nPurpose\n-------\n\nProvides a snapshot of competition standings that can be published, audited,\nand used by downstream modules such as the public site, reporting, and\nqualification logic. Standings are linked to rule sets to ensure consistent\nscoring and tie resolution.\n\nDependencies\n------------\n\n- ``sports_federation_tournament``: Tournaments, stages, groups, and matches.\n- ``sports_federation_rules``: Rule sets for scoring and tie-breaks.\n- ``mail``: Chatter integration.\n\nModels\n------\n\n``federation.standing``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA standings table for a specific scope such as a tournament, stage, or group.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Standings title.\n- ``tournament_id`` (Many2one): Tournament.\n- ``stage_id`` (Many2one): Optional stage scope.\n- ``group_id`` (Many2one): Optional group scope.\n- ``competition_id`` (Many2one): Competition context.\n- ``rule_set_id`` (Many2one): Scoring and tie-break rules.\n- ``state`` (Selection): ``draft``, ``computed``, or ``frozen``.\n- ``line_ids`` (One2many): Ranked team entries.\n- ``line_count`` (Integer): Stat-button counter.\n- ``computed_on`` (Datetime): When the table was last computed.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Additional notes.\n\nState machine:\n\n- ``draft -> computed -> frozen``.\n\n``federation.standing.line``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nOne row per participant in the standings table.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``standing_id`` (Many2one): Parent standings.\n- ``participant_id`` (Many2one): The team.\n- ``rank`` (Integer): Position in the standings table (1 = first).\n- ``played`` (Integer): Total matches played.\n- ``won`` / ``drawn`` / ``lost`` (Integer): Results breakdown.\n- ``score_for`` / ``score_against`` (Integer): Goals/points scored and conceded.\n- ``score_diff`` (Integer, computed): ``score_for - score_against``.\n- ``points`` (Integer): Total points per rule set.\n- ``note`` (Char): Short free-text remark for this line.\n- ``tiebreak_notes`` (Text, readonly): Auto-generated explanation of the tie-break criterion used to order this participant.\n\n``federation.standing.recompute.job``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nAsynchronous recompute queue record used for background standings updates.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``standing_id`` (Many2one): Target standing to recompute.\n- ``idempotency_key`` (Char): Replay-safe key for deduplicating repeated queue requests.\n- ``correlation_id`` (Char): Trace identifier propagated through queue processing.\n- ``state`` (Selection): ``pending``, ``running``, ``done``, or ``failed``.\n- ``attempt_count`` / ``max_attempts`` (Integer): Retry control metadata.\n- ``requested_on`` / ``started_on`` / ``completed_on`` (Datetime): Lifecycle timestamps.\n- ``next_retry_on`` (Datetime): Retry schedule for failed jobs.\n- ``last_error`` (Text): Last failure reason captured for operators.\n\nKey Behaviours\n--------------\n\n- **Rule-set driven scoring**: points are calculated using the attached rule\n   set and its configured win, draw, and loss values.\n- **Tie-break resolution**: when teams have equal points, tie-break rules from\n   the rule set are applied in sequence order.\n- **Snapshot model**: each standings record is a point-in-time computation,\n   allowing historical comparison.\n- **Official-result filtering**: when ``sports_federation_result_control`` is\n   installed, only matches with ``include_in_official_standings = True`` are\n   counted.\n- **Freeze behavior**: frozen standings reject recomputation unless\n   ``force_recompute`` is provided in context.\n- **Auto-advance hook**: freezing a standing can trigger pending\n   ``federation.stage.progression`` rules with ``auto_advance = True``.\n- **Publication is separate**: public visibility is handled by\n   ``sports_federation_public_site`` through ``website_published``, not by a\n   dedicated published standings state.\n- **Optional queued recompute**: standings can be recomputed asynchronously via\n   ``federation.standing.recompute.job`` and the\n   ``action_queue_recompute`` button.\n- **Idempotent queue requests**: repeated queue requests with the same\n   ``idempotency_key`` replay the original job instead of creating duplicates.\n- **Queue visibility**: pending and failed queue counters are surfaced directly\n   on the standing form, with a dedicated queue action and menu entry.\n\n## Migration note (v19.0.1.2.0)\n\n- Adds ``federation.standing.recompute.job`` for asynchronous, idempotent\n   standings recompute processing.\n- Adds queue cron ``Standings: Process Recompute Queue``.\n\n## Recompute job recovery\n\nStanding recompute jobs use bounded exponential retry. Exhausted jobs move to `Needs operator action`, preserve the correlation ID and error evidence, and can be explicitly returned to the queue by a manager. The queue cron also recovers jobs left in `running` after a worker interruption.\n", "content_length": 5027, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_standings/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "fac9e6593f4665d79b936eb12082894d8ee14db0fedb13c468f646ae81dda197", "size_bytes": 5027}

``score_for - score_against``.\n- ``points`` (Integer): Total points per rule set.\n- ``note`` (Char): Short free-text remark for this line.\n- ``tiebreak_notes`` (Text, readonly): Auto-generated explanation of the tie-break criterion used to order this participant.\n\n``federation.standing.recompute.job``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nAsynchronous recompute queue record used for background standings updates.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``standing_id`` (Many2one): Target standing to recompute.\n- ``idempotency_key`` (Char): Replay-safe key for deduplicating repeated queue requests.\n- ``correlation_id`` (Char): Trace identifier propagated through queue processing.\n- ``state`` (Selection): ``pending``, ``running``, ``done``, or ``failed``.\n- ``attempt_count`` / ``max_attempts`` (Integer): Retry control metadata.\n- ``requested_on`` / ``started_on`` / ``completed_on`` (Datetime): Lifecycle timestamps.\n- ``next_retry_on`` (Datetime): Retry schedule for failed jobs.\n- ``last_error`` (Text): Last failure reason captured for operators.\n\nKey Behaviours\n--------------\n\n- **Rule-set driven scoring**: points are calculated using the attached rule\n   set and its configured win, draw, and loss values.\n- **Tie-break resolution**: when teams have equal points, tie-break rules from\n   the rule set are applied in sequence order.\n- **Snapshot model**: each standings record is a point-in-time computation,\n   allowing historical comparison.\n- **Official-result filtering**: when ``sports_federation_result_control`` is\n   installed, only matches with ``include_in_official_standings = True`` are\n   counted.\n- **Freeze behavior**: frozen standings reject recomputation unless\n   ``force_recompute`` is provided in context.\n- **Auto-advance hook**: freezing a standing can trigger pending\n   ``federation.stage.progression`` rules with ``auto_advance = True``.\n- **Publication is separate**: public visibility is handled by\n   ``sports_federation_public_site`` through ``website_published``, not by a\n   dedicated published standings state.\n- **Optional queued recompute**: standings can be recomputed asynchronously via\n   ``federation.standing.recompute.job`` and the\n   ``action_queue_recompute`` button.\n- **Idempotent queue requests**: repeated queue requests with the same\n   ``idempotency_key`` replay the original job instead of creating duplicates.\n- **Queue visibility**: pending and failed queue counters are surfaced directly\n   on the standing form, with a dedicated queue action and menu entry.\n\n## Migration note (v19.0.1.2.0)\n\n- Adds ``federation.standing.recompute.job`` for asynchronous, idempotent\n   standings recompute processing.\n- Adds queue cron ``Standings: Process Recompute Queue``.\n\n## Recompute job recovery\n\nStanding recompute jobs use bounded exponential retry. Exhausted jobs move to `Needs operator action`, preserve the correlation ID and error evidence, and can be explicitly returned to the queue by a manager. The queue cron also recovers jobs left in `running` after a worker interruption.\n", "content_length": 5171, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_standings/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "940003737303dce07d7d81f5fb376b0d268ff5e20c874edb30722fc3065cc59c", "size_bytes": 5171}

++ {"content": "\"\"\"Tour T-09: Public Site — Tournament Publication and Editorial Scheduling\n\nWalks the public site publication workflow:\n  1. Create a tournament and publish it (website_published = True)\n  2. Create an editorial item in draft\n  3. Schedule the item → 'scheduled'\n  4. Publish the item → 'published'\n  5. Archive the item → 'archived'\n  6. Reset to draft → 'draft'\n  7. STEP 1: Publish tournament\n        self.assertFalse(self.tournament.website_published)\n        self.tournament.website_published = True\n        self.assertTrue(self.tournament.website_published)\n\n        # STEP 2: Create an editorial item in draft\n        item = self.env[\"federation.public.editorial.item\"].create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tour Launch Announcement\",\n                \"summary\": \"The Tour Cup 2026 is now open!\",\n                \"content_type\": \"announcement\",\n                \"publish_start\": \"2026-01-01 09:00:00\",\n                \"season_id\": self.season.id,\n                \"tournament_id\": self.tournament.id,\n            }\n        )\n        self.assertEqual(item.publication_state, \"draft\")\n        self.assertFalse(item.can_access_publicly())\n\n        # STEP 3: Schedule the item\n        item.action_schedule()\n        self.assertEqual(item.publication_state, \"scheduled\")\n\n        # STEP 4: Publish\n        item.action_publish()\n        self.assertEqual(item.publication_state, \"published\")\n        self.assertTrue(item.can_access_publicly())\n\n        # STEP 6: Archive — removed from live feed\n        item.action_archive_item()\n        self.assertEqual(item.publication_state, \"archived\")\n        self.assertFalse(item.can_access_publicly())\n\n        live_after_archive = self.env[\n            \"federation.public.editorial.item\"\n        ].get_live_items(season=self.season)\n        self.assertNotIn(item, live_after_archive)\n\n        # ++ {"content": "# Competition Registration\n\nThe Registration Desk manages team entries for a competition edition and division.\n\n## Team selection\n\nWhen creating or editing a competition entry, the team dropdown is limited to:\n\n- active teams;\n- teams eligible for the selected division's category and gender;\n- teams that are not already entered in the same registration window.\n\nThe available-team list is computed per division and the form applies it as a\nselection domain. The model also validates the same rules on create and write,\nso direct ORM or API requests cannot bypass the desk filter. Changing a window\nclears an existing team selection when it is no longer valid.\n\nEligibility uses the tournament module's existing `search_eligible_teams()` and\n`get_team_eligibility_error()` APIs. No historical registration entries are\nrewritten by this filtering; it only affects new selections and invalid direct\nwrites.\n\n## Regression tests\n\nThe regression coverage is in\n`tests/test_registration_team_selection.py`. Run it with the repository's\nmodule-level Odoo test workflow after installing the registration addon and its\ndeclared dependencies.\n", "content_length": 1135, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_registration/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "c0496e6d758dc7652fceb59fc8f9678fe35c7b4bc86a5389a9b3cbafc5b1ba0f", "size_bytes": 1135}

--+# Competition Operations Quality of Life Roadmap
--+
--+Owner: Federation Competition Operations
--+Last updated: 2026-09-03
--+Review cadence: Every release
--+
--+## Purpose
--+
--+Reduce clicks, ambiguity, recovery time, and support requests without adding a parallel workflow or another dashboard.
--+
--+## Implemented contracts
--+
--+- Operational tasks expose blocker, next step, deadline, responsible club, assignee, urgency bucket, digest status, and direct source navigation.
--+- Retryable operational jobs can be retried from the task; business recovery remains in the owning workflow so reasons and role separation are preserved.
--+- Backend and portal actions use state-based visibility and native Odoo favorites for reusable queue filters.
--+- Registration decisions, reminders, and governed imports provide safe bulk operations; schedule changes remain revision-owned.
--+- Chatter and tracked activities provide the authoritative timeline without copying events into another model.
--+- Club work is grouped into action now, due soon, waiting, and recently completed, with daily digest notifications.
--+- Authenticated cross-module search resolves competitions, tournaments, teams, registration windows, schedules, and matches to typed direct links.
--+- Existing operational queues and the consolidated dashboard remain the action workbench; no duplicate KPI model is introduced.
--+
--+## Exit criteria
--+
--+Users can identify the next action and owner, reach the source in one step, retry failed jobs safely, process supported bulk work, review authoritative history, find records without knowing module boundaries, and work from urgency-based queues.

+-+Menu:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Registration Desk
+-+```
+-+
+-+Close the registration window and press **Finalize Participants**. The finalized participant set feeds the format structure.
+-+
+-+**Recovery:** Correct entries before finalization. If a finalized set is wrong and nothing depends on it, create a corrected set through the registration workflow. If fixtures or schedules exist, create a successor structure or schedule revision instead of mutating published history.
+-+
+-+### 5. Configure and generate the format
+-+
+-+Menus:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Format Templates
+-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio
+-+```
+-+
+-+**Format Templates** is manager-only. In **Format Studio**, select the season competition, division, finalized participant set, and format settings. Use **Check Feasibility**, then **Generate Fixtures**. For multi-stage structures use **Validate Stage Graph**. Once accepted, use **Freeze Structure**.
+-+
+-+**Recovery:** Before freeze, correct and regenerate. Once operational matches or frozen stage snapshots exist, create a new structure version. The current UI has no generic structure-unfreeze command.
+-+
+-+### 6. Prepare and progress stages
+-+
+-+There is no standalone **Stage Progression** menu. Stage controls are on the structure opened from:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio
+-+```
+-+
+-+Available stage actions are **Prepare**, **Start**, and **Freeze & Progress**.
+-+
+-+**Recovery:** Correct a stage before starting it. Before progression, correct and recompute standings. Frozen snapshot lines are immutable; after progression use a corrected successor structure rather than editing evidence.
+-+
+-+### 7. Plan calendar capacity
+-+
+-+Menu:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Calendar Planner
+-+```
+-+
+-+Create match days, slot windows, and capacity, then use **Mark Capacity Ready**. Venue setup and constraints are under:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Match Day > Venues
+-+```
+-+
+-+**Recovery:** Edit draft calendar records. If a schedule already uses the calendar, make the deliberate calendar correction and refresh the working schedule. Stale assignments are flagged, not silently deleted.
+-+
+-+### 8. Build the working schedule
+-+
+-+Menu:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner
+-+```
+-+
+-+Use **Refresh Calendar Fixtures**. Assign dates, times, venues, and courts manually, or use **Auto-schedule**, **Preview**, and **Apply Auto-schedule**. Review fairness warnings.
+-+
+-+**Recovery:** Draft and change-requested schedules remain editable. A preview does not change the schedule until applied. Refresh fixtures, move assignments, or regenerate while mutable.
+-+
+-+### 9. Submit and review the schedule
+-+
+-+Planner menu:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner
+-+```
+-+
+-+Use **Submit for Review**. Approver menu:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Review Queue
+-+```
+-+
+-+The review exposes **Withdraw Submission**, **Request Changes**, and **Approve Schedule** according to state and role.
+-+
+-+**Recovery:** Withdraw a pending submission to return it to editing. Request changes to return it to the planner. If an approval is mistaken, do not publish; correct it through a new review cycle while preserving separation of duties.
+-+
+-+### 10. Publish the schedule
+-+
+-+Use **Publish Schedule** on an approved review. The two real publication menus are:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Publication > Approved Schedules
+-+Federation > Publication > Schedule Publications
+-+```
+-+
+-+**Recovery:** Live publications are immutable. Open the published schedule under **Federation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner**, use **Amend Schedule**, enter a reason, and press **Create Amendment**. The replacement follows submit, review, approve, and publish again. The old publication becomes superseded. There is no in-place **Unpublish** button.
+-+
+-+### 11. Operate match day
+-+
+-+Menu:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Match-Day Control
+-+```
+-+
+-+Use **Open Match Day** when ready. During operations use **Update Court**, **Report Incident**, or **Operational Schedule Change**. Finish with **Close Match Day**. Supporting records are under:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Match Day > Match Sheets
+-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Technical Records > Incidents
+-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Technical Records > Operational Deviations
+-+```
+-+
+-+**Recovery:** Resolve incident and deviation records with **Resolve**. Operational changes are recorded rather than silently altering the approved publication. Correct the planning baseline through a schedule amendment.
+-+
+-+### 12. Submit and approve results
+-+
+-+Backend menu:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Planning > Advanced Records > Matches
+-+```
+-+
+-+Result Control extends the match form; there is no separate backend **Results** menu. The form provides **Submit Result**, **Verify Result**, **Approve Result**, **Raise Dispute / Request Exception**, **Correct Result**, and **Reset to Draft**.
+-+
+-+Club portal:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+My Account > Results
+-+```
+-+
+-+**Recovery:** Reset an incorrect in-progress result to draft. Raise a dispute for governed review. Correct contested or approved results through **Correct Result**. Never silently edit an approved score.
+-+
+-+### 13. Recompute and freeze standings
+-+
+-+Menu:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Publication > Standings
+-+```
+-+
+-+Use **Recompute** or **Queue Recompute**, inspect lines and tie-break notes, and then use **Freeze**.
+-+
+-+**Recovery:** Recompute while unfrozen. For a frozen standing, use **Unfreeze**, correct the source result or rule, use **Force Recompute**, and freeze again. Failed asynchronous work appears under the nested **Recompute Queue**.
+-+
+-+### 14. Monitor exceptions
+-+
+-+Menus:
+-+
+-+```text
+-+Federation > Planning > Operational Action Queue
+-+Federation > Administration > Reporting > Operational Health
+-+Federation > Administration > Operational Job Health
+-+```
+-+
+-+Use source links to correct business records in their owning workflow. Retry only retryable jobs.
+-+

- {"content": "# Competition Engine\n\nThis implementation provides role-owned capabilities and explicit handovers for competition planning and operations.\n\n## Addons\n\n1. `sports_federation_competition_core`: identity, roles, lifecycle and events.\n2. `sports_federation_registration`: application queue and finalized participant sets.\n3. `sports_federation_format`: versioned logical structures and fixtures.\n4. `sports_federation_calendar`: physical match days, round allocations and capacity.\n5. `sports_federation_scheduling`: one-way fixture-to-slot assignments, pure validation and deterministic proposals.\n6. `sports_federation_schedule_approval`: independent review and immutable publication snapshots.\n7. `sports_federation_matchday`: live operational control and incidents.\n\n## Required handovers\n\nRegistration finalizes a participant set. Format freezes a structure. Calendar prepares physical capacity. Scheduling submits a complete schedule. Approval publishes an immutable snapshot. Match-day operations execute only a published snapshot.\n\n## Migration policy\n\nThe legacy monolithic engine has been removed from the addon set. New and existing operational flows use the ownership split. Databases upgraded from a release that installed the legacy addon require the normal reviewed upgrade/migration procedure before production rollout; do not silently reinterpret existing production records.\n\n\n## Schedule handoff operator handoff\n\nThe operator path is fully exposed in the backend: Schedule Planner submits a\nvalidated revision, Schedule Review Queue provides independent request-changes\nor approval decisions, Publication exposes approved schedules and immutable\npublication history, and Match-Day Operations consumes only the current live\npublication. Submission creates its pending review atomically when the approval\naddon is installed; there is no operator-visible intermediate state that\nrequires a separate \"start review\" action.\n\n## Phases 5.1.1 to 5.3: publication and live operations\n\nSchedule review decisions are command-only: ACLs are read-only and the review\nmodel rejects direct decision-field writes. Live publications are scoped and\nversioned per match day. Publication replacement uses a dedicated wizard,\nrequires a replacement reason, locks the match day during version allocation,\nand rejects stale confirmations.\n\nMatch-Day Control exposes readiness, the exact live publication, published\nmatches, court state, incidents, immutable sessions and operational deviations.\nOpening a day freezes the publication digest in a session. Live moves, delays,\npostponements and cancellations update only operational match fields; the\napproved publication and `published_slot_id` remain immutable. Match-day operations execute only a published snapshot.\n\n## Migration policy\n\nThe legacy monolithic engine has been removed from the addon set. New and existing operational flows use the ownership split. Databases upgraded from a release that installed the legacy addon require the normal reviewed upgrade/migration procedure before production rollout; do not silently reinterpret existing production records.\n\n\n## Schedule handoff operator handoff\n\nThe operator path is fully exposed in the backend: Schedule Planner submits a\nvalidated revision, Schedule Review Queue provides independent request-changes\nor approval decisions, Publication exposes approved schedules and immutable\npublication history, and Match-Day Operations consumes only the current live\npublication. For fast UI work use\n`--frontend-module`; for cross-module safety use\n`--affected-from origin/main --include-dependents`. Principles\n\n- Every external export or feed must expose an explicit contract identifier.\n- Version changes must be additive within a version whenever possible.\n- Breaking schema changes require a new contract version rather than silent\n  mutation of an existing response.\n- Deprecated routes or payloads remain available for at least one supported\n  release cycle after the replacement contract is published, unless security or\n  legal requirements force a faster removal.\n- Contract changes must be reflected in code, tests where applicable, this\n  document, and the roadmap or release notes in the same change set.\n\n## Authentication Strategy\n\nPublic tournament contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"`\n- intended for website visitors, public calendars, and read-only partner\n  consumption\n\nOperator-authenticated reporting exports:\n\n- `auth=\"user\"`\n- require an authenticated backend session\n- intended for federation operators using backend actions and reporting screens\n\nManaged partner contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"` routes protected by partner credentials\n- require `X-Federation-Partner-Code` and `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- enforce per-partner contract subscriptions before a payload is served or a\n  delivery is accepted\n- intended for explicit machine-to-machine integrations without sharing backend\n  user sessions\n\nImport contracts:\n\n- executed either through backend import wizards or through managed partner\n  delivery staging before entering the same wizard flow\n- guarded by dry-run preview, governance-job approval, and checksum matching for\n  live imports\n\n## Public Contracts\n\n## Tournament Feed\n\n- Canonical route: `/api/v1/tournaments/<slug>/feed`\n- Compatibility routes:\n  - `/api/v1/tournaments/<id>/feed`\n  - `/api/v1/competitions/<id>/feed`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_feed`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: v1`\n- Payload anchor:\n  - top-level `api_version = \"v1\"`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - top-level keys in the v1 payload are stable\n  - additive nested fields are allowed in v1 when they do not alter existing\n    semantics\n\n## Tournament Schedule Calendar\n\n- Canonical route: `/tournaments/<slug>/schedule.ics`\n- Compatibility route: `/tournament/<id>/schedule.ics`\n- Response type: `text/calendar`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_schedule_ics`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: ics_v1`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - calendar structure stays compatible with standard ICS consumers\n  - field enrichment should be additive inside event descriptions, not a change\n    to the ICS envelope\n\n## Authenticated CSV Contracts\n\nAll authenticated CSV exports expose these headers:\n\n- `X-Federation-Contract`\n- `X-Federation-Contract-Version`\n\n## Standings Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/standings/<tournament_id>`\n- Contract: `standings_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n- Notes:\n  - intended for downstream standings review and board-pack style extracts\n\n## Participation Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/participation/<season_id>`\n- Contract: `participation_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Summary Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance`\n- Contract: `finance_summary_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Event Handoff Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance/events`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Versioning anchor:\n  - detailed finance-event handoff rows expose a schema version column and the\n    matching response header contract version\n- Required handoff fields include:\n  - event identity and state\n  - handoff state\n  - fee type and amount\n  - invoice, external, accounting-batch, and reconciliation references\n  - source traceability\n  - exported, reconciled, and closed timestamps\n\n## Managed Partner Contracts\n\n## Contract Manifest\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/contracts`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- Payload includes:\n  - contract code, version, direction, transport, and route hint\n  - deprecation stage and replacement contract\n  - `available` flag for database-specific operational availability\n  - partner subscription state and last-used timestamp\n\n## Partner Finance Event Handoff\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`\n- Response type: `text/csv`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Optional query parameters:\n  - `limit` to request one bounded page of rows; defaults to `200` and caps at `500`\n  - `cursor` to resume after the last row from the previous page\n- Invalid `limit` or `cursor` values return `400` with the standard `data_validation` payload.\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: finance_event_v1`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: <schema version>`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code: <partner code>`\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Mode: cursor_page` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Count: <row count>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Has-More: true|false` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Page-Limit: <effective limit>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Next-Cursor: <timestamp>|<id>` when another page is available\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n\n## Inbound Delivery Staging\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/inbound/<contract_code>/deliveries`\n- Method: `POST`\n- Request type: JSON object\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n  - optional `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key` to safely reuse the same staged delivery for matching retries\n- Request fields:\n  - `filename`\n  - `payload_base64`\n  - optional `notes`\n  - optional `source_reference`\n- Response header on every successful delivery request:\n  - `X-Federation-Delivery-Outcome: created|checksum_reuse|idempotency_replay`\n- Response headers when an idempotency key is supplied:\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key: <normalized key>`\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotent-Replay: true|false`\n- Response fields:\n  - `delivery_outcome` with `created`, `checksum_reuse`, or `idempotency_replay`\n  - delivery identity and current state\n  - partner and contract codes\n  - echoed `idempotency_key` when present\n  - payload checksum\n  - contract route hint\n- Duplicate handling:\n  - the same partner, contract, and payload checksum reuse the active staged\n    delivery while it remains in preview or approval flow and report\n    `delivery_outcome = checksum_reuse`\n  - the same partner, contract, and idempotency key replay the original delivery\n    across all states, report `delivery_outcome = idempotency_replay`, and\n    still return `400` if the key is reused for a different payload\n\n## Import Contracts\n\nReusable import templates are versioned backend contracts and live under\n`federation.import.template`.\n\nCurrent template codes:\n\n- `clubs_csv`\n- `players_csv`\n- `seasons_csv`\n- `teams_csv`\n- `tournament_participants_csv`\n\nCurrent template version:\n\n- `csv_v1`\n\nManaged inbound delivery policy:\n\n1. A subscribed partner posts a base64 payload to the inbound delivery route for\n  the relevant contract.\n2. The system stages a `federation.integration.delivery` record, deduplicates\n  active resubmissions by checksum, and can also bind an explicit idempotency\n  key to the request for safer client retries.\n3. Operators open the staged delivery in the matching import wizard for preview.\n4. Approval and live execution continue through the standard governance-job\n  workflow already used for manual rollover imports.\n\nLive import policy:\n\n1. Run a dry-run preview for the uploaded CSV.\n2. Request approval, which creates a governance job tied to the file checksum,\n   target model, template, and preview results.\n3. Approve the governance job.\n4. Execute the live import only if the CSV checksum and selected template still\n   match the approved job.\n\nVerification policy:\n\n- governance jobs store preview totals, execution totals, and before/after\n  target-model record counts\n- live imports that partially succeed remain visible as\n  `completed_with_errors`\n- staged partner deliveries mirror preview, approval, completion, and failure\n  states so operators can reconcile inbound handoffs without leaving the app\n\n## Versioning Policy\n\n- Public JSON versions are encoded in both the path and the payload.\n- CSV and ICS contracts use stable routes plus explicit response headers.\n- Import templates use a version field on the template and a matching schema\n  snapshot on the governance job.\n- Breaking changes require a new contract identifier or version rather than a\n  silent replacement.\n\nEndpoint compatibility policy (v1):\n\n- `/integration/v1/contracts`: additive response changes only; remove fields\n  only in a new API version.\n- `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`: keep CSV column order and header\n  semantics stable for `finance_event_v1` until a new contract code/version is\n  published.\n- `/integration/v1/inbound/{contract_code}/deliveries`: keep\n  `delivery_outcome` semantics (`created`, `checksum_reuse`,\n  `idempotency_replay`) stable within v1.\n- JSON error envelopes for all managed integration endpoints must preserve the\n  typed shape `{error, error_code, correlation_id}` across minor releases.\n\nPartner onboarding references:\n\n- Golden request/response examples: `openapi/examples/INTEGRATION_GOLDEN_EXAMPLES.md`.\n- CI contract guardrails: `ci/check_openapi_contracts.py`.\n\n## Deprecation Policy\n\nThe working list of compatibility aliases, owners, review dates, and target\nsunset dates is maintained here and must be updated in the same change set as\nany contract-facing deprecation decision.\n\n| Surface | Canonical replacement | Target exit |\n|---|---|---|\n| `/tournaments`, `/tournaments/<slug>`, numeric tournament page routes | `/competitions`, `/competitions/<edition-slug>` | 2026-10-01 |\n| Numeric public tournament page routes | Edition routes under `/competitions/<edition-slug>` | 2026-10-01 |\n| Numeric or competition-named v1 tournament feeds | `/api/v1/tournaments/<slug>/feed` | 2026-10-01 |\n| Player import `name` column fallback | Explicit `first_name`, `last_name` columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Team import name fallbacks | `club_code` and explicit team naming columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Participant import tournament/team name fallbacks | `tournament_code` and `team_code` | 2026-10-15 |\n\nRemove a compatibility surface only after its replacement is documented,\ncovered by tests, and announced in the owning module README. If a target date\npasses without a removal decision, extend it here with the reason.\n\n- Slug-based public routes are canonical.\n- Numeric public routes remain compatibility shims and should not be used for\n  new integrations.\n- Legacy competition-named public feed routes remain compatibility aliases for\n  the tournament feed and are considered deprecated in favor of the canonical\n  tournament path.\n- Older CSV shapes should remain available for one supported release cycle once\n  a replacement contract is published.\n- Removals must be announced by updating this file, relevant READMEs, and the\n  roadmap in the same release window.\n\n## Integration configuration\n\nCI and local development use environment variables for SMTP, OAuth, partner\ntokens, webhooks, and object storage. Cleanup Result |\n|---------|-------------------|------------------|----------------|----------------|\n| Notification logs | `pending` | 30 days | `create_date` | Delete old log row |\n| Notification logs | `sent` | 90 days | `create_date` | Delete old log row |\n| Notification logs | `failed` | 180 days | `create_date` | Delete old log row |\n| Inbound deliveries | `cancelled` | 90 days | | `processed_with_errors` | 180 days | `processed_on` | Delete delivery and staged payload attachment |\n| Inbound deliveries | `failed` | 365 days | `received_on` | Delete delivery and staged payload attachment |\n| Generated report files | Last successful export snapshot | 60 days | `last_run_on` | Clear stored file payload and filename, keep schedule |\n\n## Automation\n\nThe cleanup routines
