It provides a tournament hub, overview pages, schedule and\nresults pages, standings snapshots, team profile pages, JSON feed access, and\ncalendar export while keeping older competition URLs working.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `website` | Odoo website framework |\n| `sports_federation_portal` | Main tournament website hub and navigation |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournaments, matches, participants |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings data |\n| `sports_federation_venues` | Venue information |\n| `sports_federation_result_control` | Approved result visibility |\n\n## Model extensions\n\n### `federation.tournament`\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `website_published` | Boolean | Enables public visibility |\n| `public_slug` | Char | Legacy public slug retained for tournament feed and redirect compatibility |\n| `public_description` | Html | Long-form website description |\n| `public_featured` | Boolean | Marks the tournament for featured hub sections |\n| `public_editorial_summary` | Text | Short editorial summary for cards and overview layouts |\n| `public_pinned_announcement` | Text | Announcement banner content for the overview page |\n| `public_hero_image` | Binary | Hero image for the public overview page |\n| `show_public_results` | Boolean | Enables the public results page |\n| `show_public_standings` | Boolean | Enables the public standings page |\n\nKey helper methods expose canonical public URLs, published tournament queries,\nteam/result/standings/schedule datasets, JSON feed payloads, and ICS calendar\nexport content.\n\n### `federation.team`\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `public_slug` | Char | Canonical public slug used in `/teams/<slug>` |\n\nTeam helpers provide stable team profile URLs and public tournament links.\nTheir public slug resolver accepts an extra publication domain so controller\nlookups can fail closed before rendering profile, follow, feed, or calendar\nsurfaces.\n\n### `federation.season`\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `website_published` | Boolean | Enables season-wide discovery on the website |\n| `public_slug` | Char | Canonical public slug used in `/seasons/<slug>` |\n| `public_summary` | Text | Short summary used on season discovery pages |\n| `public_description` | Html | Long-form season landing page content |\n\nSeason helpers provide canonical season URLs, featured and recent tournament\nqueries, editorial aggregation for season landing pages, and fail-closed public\nslug resolution for published-season routes.\n\n### `federation.public.editorial.item`\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `publication_state` | Selection | draft / scheduled / published / archived |\n| `content_type` | Selection | highlight / announcement / update |\n| `publish_start` / `publish_end` | Datetime | Optional publication window |\n| `season_id` / `tournament_id` / `team_id` | Many2one | Public anchor for the item |\n| `summary` | Text | Card-friendly editorial summary |\n| `body_html` | Html | Long-form editorial content |\n\nEditorial items let operators schedule season-, tournament-, or team-linked\nhighlights without editing website templates. Scheduling requires a publish\nstart while the item is still in draft; items can publish from draft or\nscheduled, archive from scheduled or published, and reset from scheduled or\narchived back to draft.\n\n### `federation.standing`\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `website_published` | Boolean | Allows standings publication |\n| `public_title` | Char | Public-facing table title |\n\n## Controllers\n\n### `PublicTournamentHubController`\n\nCanonical public routes:\n\n| Route | Auth | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `GET /tournaments` | public | Main public tournament hub with featured, live, recent, and archive sections |\n| `POST /tournaments/api/json` | public | JSON list of published tournaments |\n| `GET /competitions/<edition-slug>` | public | Canonical competition edition overview page |\n| `GET /tournaments/<slug>/teams` | public | Published participant list excluding withdrawn entries |\n| `GET /tournaments/<slug>/standings` | public | Published standings page |\n| `GET /tournaments/<slug>/results` | public | Approved public results |\n| `GET /tournaments/<slug>/schedule` | public | Public schedule grouped for easier browsing |\n| `GET /tournaments/<slug>/bracket` | public | Public bracket sections when bracket data exists |\n| `GET /tournaments/<slug>/schedule.ics` | public | ICS calendar export for the tournament schedule |\n| `GET /api/v1/tournaments/<slug>/feed` | public | Stable v1 JSON tournament feed |\n| `GET /teams/<slug>` | public | Public team profile page |\n| `GET /tournaments/<slug>/register` | user | Website registration form |\n| `POST /tournaments/<slug>/register` | user | Website registration submission via `federation.competition.entry._portal_submit_entry()` |\n\nCompatibility routes remain available for older links, including `/competitions`,\n`/competitions/archive`, numeric `/tournament/<id>` paths, numeric register/feed\npaths, and older coverage aliases. Team profile routes and season follow routes\nresolve through publication-scoped domains before redirects or rendering.\n\n### `PublicFollowController`\n\nCanonical follow and discovery routes:\n\n| Route | Auth | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `GET /seasons` | public | Season discovery page for published seasons |\n| `GET /seasons/<slug>` | public | Canonical season landing page with editorial and tournament sections |\n| `GET /teams/<slug>/schedule` | public | Team-centric grouped upcoming schedule |\n| `GET /teams/<slug>/results` | public | Team-centric recent approved results |\n| `GET /teams/<slug>/schedule.ics` | public | Team schedule calendar export |\n| `GET /api/v1/teams/<slug>/feed` | public | Stable v1 team follow feed |\n\n## Public-site behaviour\n\n1. Tournament-first navigation: the visible website now centers tournaments and nests published coverage under the existing Tournaments area.\n2. Slug-first URLs: tournaments and teams use canonical slug routes, with numeric routes preserved only for backward compatibility.\n3. Editorial control: operators can feature tournaments, add summaries, pin announcements, and assign hero imagery without editing templates.\n4. Better hub discovery: the main hub separates featured, live, recent, and archived tournaments instead of showing one flat list.\n5. Team-aware public pages: standings, results, schedule, and teams pages link through to public team profiles when available.\n6. Sticky section navigation: tournament sub-pages share one consistent local navigation model.\n7. Calendar export: schedules can be consumed as `.ics` for personal or club calendars.\n8. Stable feed contract: the v1 feed includes slug-aware public URLs alongside tournament, standings, schedule, bracket, and result data.\n9. Visibility enforcement: results and standings respect per-tournament publication toggles.\n10. Sanitized website rendering: public descriptions and website content render through standard website field handling.\n11. Backward compatibility: legacy competition routes keep resolving while the visible product language is tournament-first.\n12. Season discovery and editorial planning: published seasons aggregate featured tournaments, recent tournaments, and live editorial items with publication windows.\n13. Automatic menu cleanup: module installs and upgrades normalize stale `/competitions` website menus into the Tournaments submenu and remove leftover duplicates.\n14. Shared privileged-write boundary: website registration POST routes validate HTTP input and then reuse the same tournament registration helper as the portal layer.\n15. + {"content": "# Competition Registration\n\nThe Registration Desk manages team entries for a competition edition and division.\n\n## Team selection\n\nWhen creating or editing a competition entry, the team dropdown is limited to:\n\n- active teams;\n- teams eligible for the selected division's category and gender;\n- teams that are not already entered in the same registration window.\n\nThe available-team list is computed per division and the form applies it as a\nselection domain. The model also validates the same rules on create and write,\nso direct ORM or API requests cannot bypass the desk filter. Changing a window\nclears an existing team selection when it is no longer valid.\n\nEligibility uses the tournament module's existing `search_eligible_teams()` and\n`get_team_eligibility_error()` APIs. +-3. `GET /competitions/<edition-slug>` exposes only a published edition with at least one published division.
+-4. Format, schedule, match-day, standings, results, and bracket links remain inside the canonical `/competitions` namespace.
+-5. `GET /tournaments` redirects once to `/competitions`.
+-6. A legacy tournament detail URL redirects once to the matching edition and preserves the intended division.
+-7. Legacy schedule, standings, results, teams, and bracket URLs redirect once without a loop.
+-8. Unpublished editions, divisions, match days, and schedule publications return 404 or remain absent.
+-9. Versioned feed and calendar contracts retained by policy still return their declared contract version.

-+
-+### 1. Prepare reusable setup
-+
-+Use:
-+
-+```text

-+Federation > Setup > Competition Setup > Competition Templates
-+Federation > Setup > Competition Setup > Rules & Policies > Rule Sets & Policies

-+Federation > Setup > Core Records > Teams
-+```
-+
-+Create the season, reusable competition definition, rule set, clubs, and teams. Points, tie-break, eligibility, and qualification components are below **Rules & Policies > Advanced Components**.
-+
-+**Recovery:** Edit unused records. Archive records that already have history. Do not delete referenced seasons, competitions, clubs, teams, or rule sets merely to restart a workflow.
-+
-+### 2. Create the season competition
-+
-+Preferred menu:
-+
-+```text
-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Create Competition
-+```
-+
-+The wizard selects the setup template, competition template, season, dates, optional rule set, registration dates, divisions, and responsibilities. It creates the season competition, divisions, registration windows, and role assignments, then opens the season competition.
-+
-+Inspect the records through:
-+
-+```text
-+Federation > Setup > Competition Setup > Season Competitions
-+Federation > Planning > Advanced Records > Divisions & Tournaments
-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Competition Overview
-+```
-+
-+**Recovery:** Correct newly created records before clubs submit. There is no generic **Undo Competition Wizard** button. If downstream entries, fixtures, schedules, results, or publications exist, preserve the original records and create controlled replacements.
-+
-+### 3. Open registration and accept entries
-+
-+Backend:
-+
-+```text
-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Registration Desk
-+```
-+
-+Club portal:
-+
-+```text
-+My Account > Season registrations
-+```
-+
-+Use **Open Registration** on a draft registration window. Clubs prepare and submit entries. Managers review them in the Registration Desk.
-+
-+**Recovery:** Use **Close Registration** to stop submissions. A submitted entry can be withdrawn by the club or returned by the manager with a reason. A returned entry can be corrected and resubmitted. Rejection remains historical evidence.
-+
-+### 4. Finalize participants
-+
-+Menu:
-+
-+```text
-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Registration Desk
-+```
-+
-+Close the registration window and press **Finalize Participants**. The finalized participant set feeds the format structure.
-+
-+**Recovery:** Correct entries before finalization. If a finalized set is wrong and nothing depends on it, create a corrected set through the registration workflow. If fixtures or schedules exist, create a successor structure or schedule revision instead of mutating published history.
-+
-+### 5. Configure and generate the format
-+
-+Menus:
-+
-+```text
-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Format Templates
-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio
-+```
-+
-+**Format Templates** is manager-only. In **Format Studio**, select the season competition, division, finalized participant set, and format settings. Use **Check Feasibility**, then **Generate Fixtures**. For multi-stage structures use **Validate Stage Graph**. Once accepted, use **Freeze Structure**.
-+
-+**Recovery:** Before freeze, correct and regenerate. Once operational matches or frozen stage snapshots exist, create a new structure version. The current UI has no generic structure-unfreeze command.
-+
-+### 6. Prepare and progress stages
-+
-+There is no standalone **Stage Progression** menu. Stage controls are on the structure opened from:
-+
-+```text
-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio
-+```
-+
-+Available stage actions are **Prepare**, **Start**, and **Freeze & Progress**.
-+
-+**Recovery:** Correct a stage before starting it. Before progression, correct and recompute standings. Frozen snapshot lines are immutable; after progression use a corrected successor structure rather than editing evidence.
-+
-+### 7. Plan calendar capacity
-+
-+Menu:
-+
-+```text
-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Calendar Planner
-+```
-+

-+

-+Federation > Match Day > Venues
-+```
-+
-+**Recovery:** Edit draft calendar records. If a schedule already uses the calendar, make the deliberate calendar correction and refresh the working schedule. Stale assignments are flagged, not silently deleted.

-+### 8. Build the working schedule
-+
-+Menu:
-+
-+```text
-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner
-+```
-+

-+

-+
-+### 9. Submit and review the schedule
-+

-+
-+```text
-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner
-+```
-+

-+

-+

-+
-+**Recovery:** Withdraw a pending submission to return it to editing. Request changes to return it to the planner. If an approval is mistaken, do not publish; correct it through a new review cycle while preserving separation of duties.
-+
-+### 10. Publish the schedule
-+
-+Use **Publish Schedule** on an approved review. The two real publication menus are:
-+
-+```text
-+Federation > Publication > Approved Schedules
-+Federation > Publication > Schedule Publications
-+```
-+
-+**Recovery:** Live publications are immutable. Open the published schedule under **Federation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner**, use **Amend Schedule**, enter a reason, and press **Create Amendment**. The replacement follows submit, review, approve, and publish again. The old publication becomes superseded. There is no in-place **Unpublish** button.

-+### 11. Operate match day
-+
-+Menu:
-+
-+```text
-+Federation > Competition Workflow > Match-Day Control
-+```
-+

reporting).\n- **Location**: All addons live under the `odoo/` folder as individual modules prefixed with `sports_federation_`.\n-- **Primary docs**: See [odoo/CONTEXT.md](odoo/CONTEXT.md#L1), Patterns**\n- **Module split**: `sports_federation_base` (master data), `sports_federation_tournament` (tournaments, matches, participants), `sports_federation_format / sports_federation_scheduling` (service/wizards), plus domain modules (`people`, `rules`, `officiating`, `rosters`, `result_control`, `public_site`, `reporting`, `finance_bridge`, `venues`, `discipline`, `standings`, ...).\n- **Model naming**: Domain models use the `federation.` prefix (e.g. `federation.player`, `federation.match`).\n- **Common patterns**: `ir.sequence` for identifiers, `state` selection fields for workflows, wizards for batch operations (under `wizards/`), `controllers/` for portal/website endpoints, and `security/` for groups/record rules/ACLs.\n\n**Key Files & Where To Look**\n- **High-level sports_federation_scheduling` (no persistent models if not required).\n- **Add a controller / portal flow**: use `controllers/` and add templates under `views/` or `templates/`; respect portal record rules (see `sports_federation_portal`).\n- **Security**: always add or update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and any `security/*.xml` groups/rules for new models or new endpoints.\n- **Manifest hygiene**: update `__manifest__.py` `depends`, `data`, and `version` fields when introducing DB changes or new data files.\n\n**Testing & Local Run**\n- **Where tests live**: `odoo/<module>/tests/` when present (some modules include unit/functional tests).\n- **Run module tests**: use the Odoo test runner for module-level tests (e.g. `odoo-bin -d <db> -i <module> --test-enable`) or your established local development workflow.\n- **Release sanity**: include at least one focused test for new business logic (especially schedule generation, result pipeline, and state transitions).\n\n**PR Checklist (required before merge)**\n- **Tests**: Add/adjust tests covering the new behaviour.\n- **Security**: Update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and add group/record-rule XML if necessary.\n- **Manifest**: Add new data files to `__manifest__.py` `data` list and ensure `depends` are correct.\n-- **Docs**: Update or add a short README in the module and, if behaviour changes, update the relevant `odoo/_workflows` file.\n- **Small, focused commits**: Prefer atomic commits (one logical change per commit) and descriptive commit messages.\n\n**How Copilot Should Help Show me the patch with files changed.\"\n- **Create a wizard**: \"Create a `round_robin_wizard` that generates matches for a stage; include wizard model, view, manifest update, and a unit test verifying match count for 4 teams.\"\n- **Fix workflow behaviour**: \"Investigate why standings recompute includes contested results; propose a minimal fix and tests to prevent contested results from being counted.\"\n\n**Notes & Expectations**\n- **Authoritative sources**: the `_workflows` documents and `TECHNICAL_NOTE.md` are the source of truth for business behaviour—use them before changing workflows.\n- **Keep modules decoupled**: the architecture intentionally separates `base`, `tournament`, and the `competition_engine` service; prefer adding features in the appropriate module.\n- **Ask clarifying questions**: if a requested feature impacts tournament rules, scheduling, or publication flows, ask which workflow (`_workflows/*.md`) should govern the behaviour.\n\n**Documentation Maintenance (required)**\n\n- **Always update docs**: For any code, data model, view, workflow, or behaviour change, update the relevant documentation files in this repository as part of the same change set (or in a linked follow-up PR). Format freezes a structure. Calendar prepares physical capacity. Scheduling submits a complete schedule. Approval publishes an immutable snapshot. Match-day operations execute only a published snapshot.\n\n## Migration policy\n\nThe legacy monolithic engine has been removed from the addon set. New and existing operational flows use the ownership split. Databases upgraded from a release that installed the legacy addon require the normal reviewed upgrade/migration procedure before production rollout; do not silently reinterpret existing production records.\n\n\n## Schedule handoff operator handoff\n\nThe operator path is fully exposed in the backend: Schedule Planner submits a\nvalidated revision, Schedule Review Queue provides independent request-changes\nor approval decisions, Publication exposes approved schedules and immutable\npublication history, and Match-Day Operations consumes only the current live\npublication. Submission creates its pending review atomically when the approval\naddon is installed; there is no operator-visible intermediate state that\nrequires a separate \"start review\" action.\n\n## Phases 5.1.1 to 5.3: publication and live operations\n\nSchedule review decisions are command-only: ACLs are read-only and the review\nmodel rejects direct decision-field writes. Live publications are scoped and\nversioned per match day. Publication replacement uses a dedicated wizard,\nrequires a replacement reason, locks the match day during version allocation,\nand rejects stale confirmations.\n\nMatch-Day Control exposes readiness, the exact live publication, published\nmatches, court state, incidents, immutable sessions and operational deviations.\nOpening a day freezes the publication digest in a session. Live moves, delays,\npostponements and cancellations update only operational match fields; the\napproved publication and `published_slot_id` remain immutable. Every deviation\nrecords actor, reason, old/new slot, session and publication, and emits an audit\nevent.\n", "content_length": 2809, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "COMPETITION_ENGINE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "2c6a2ef0be5e1aece6060a09b33b5da37b58fc1a0bca7e3604aa9cde951df0b0", "size_bytes": 2809}

Live moves, delays,\npostponements and cancellations update only operational match fields; the\napproved publication and `published_slot_id` remain immutable.  {"content": "# Data Retention Policy\n\nLast updated: 2026-08-20\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nThis document defines the default retention windows for operational logs,\nstaged inbound deliveries, and generated report files stored by the federation\naddons.\n\n\n## Review Status\n\nThe policy remains the contract for terminal-state cleanup. Release review must verify the configured cron XML IDs, active defaults, date anchors, retention constants, attachment cleanup, and preservation of unresolved workflow records. A date update without those checks is not sufficient.\n\n## Scope\n\nThe current automated retention policy covers these repository-owned surfaces:\n\n- `federation.notification.log` records created by `sports_federation_notifications`\n- `federation.integration.delivery` records and their staged payload attachments\n  in `sports_federation_import_tools`\n- `federation.report.schedule.generated_file` attachments created by\n  `sports_federation_reporting`\n\nNon-terminal workflow records are intentionally excluded from automated purge.\nIf a delivery is still waiting for preview, approval, or live processing, it is\nretained until an operator resolves it.\n\n## Retention Windows\n\n| Surface | State / Condition | Retention Window | Cleanup Anchor | Cleanup Result |\n|---------|-------------------|------------------|----------------|----------------|\n| Notification logs | `pending` | 30 days | `create_date` | Delete old log row |\n| Notification logs | `sent` | 90 days | `create_date` | Delete old log row |\n| Notification logs | `failed` | 180 days | `create_date` | Delete old log row |\n| Inbound deliveries | `cancelled` | 90 days | `received_on` | Delete delivery and staged payload attachment |\n| Inbound deliveries | `processed` | 180 days | `processed_on` | Delete delivery and staged payload attachment |\n| Inbound deliveries | `processed_with_errors` | 180 days | `processed_on` | Delete delivery and staged payload attachment |\n| Inbound deliveries | `failed` | 365 days | `received_on` | Delete delivery and staged payload attachment |\n| Generated report files | Last successful export snapshot | 60 days | `last_run_on` | Clear stored file payload and filename, keep schedule |\n\n## Automation\n\nThe cleanup routines run through daily scheduled actions that ship with the\naffected addons:\n\n- `sports_federation_notifications.ir_cron_notification_log_retention`\n- `sports_federation_import_tools.ir_cron_federation_integration_delivery_retention`\n- `sports_federation_reporting.ir_cron_federation_report_schedule_retention`\n\nThese jobs are active by default and call the corresponding model cleanup\nhelpers during normal Odoo cron execution.\n\n## Operator Notes\n\n- Delivery retention only applies to terminal states, so unresolved inbound\n  partner handoffs remain visible in the operator checklist.\n- Report schedule retention clears the stored export artifact but preserves the\n  schedule definition, run metadata, and next execution date.\n- If audit, legal, or incident-response requirements require a longer window,\n  update the model retention constants and this document in the same branch.\n\n## Change Management\n\nWhen retention windows or cleanup scope change:\n\n1. Update this document in the same branch as the code change.\n2. Update the affected module README files and release/runbook guidance.\n3. Re-run `python3 ci/check_doc_freshness.py` and `python3 ci/check_markdown_links.py`.\n4. Re-run the affected module test suites to confirm the cleanup behavior still\n   matches the documented policy.\n\n## Execution evidence\n\nEvery automated retention run appends a `federation.retention.evidence` record with its policy code, timestamps, outcome, and affected-record counts. Evidence is read-only to federation managers and is retained independently from the records cleaned by the policy.\n\n\n## Recovery visibility\n\nFederation managers use **Administration → Retention and Recovery** to verify policy freshness and outcomes. Failure evidence is committed independently before the owning cron re-raises, so transaction rollback cannot erase the recovery record.\n", "content_length": 4126, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "DATA_RETENTION_POLICY.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "cd8948f93fddf169b520d7ddc9230528120079b4d4af545df3736bd0bc84f1f0", "size_bytes": 4128}

-{"content": "# Integration Contracts\n\nLast updated: 2026-08-20\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nThis document defines the stable partner-facing contracts currently supported by\nthe federation platform and the policy used to version, evolve, and deprecate\nthem.\n\nMachine-readable partner route definitions live in `openapi/integration_v1.yaml`.\nKeep the OpenAPI file, this document, and the route implementations aligned in\nthe same change set whenever a managed integration contract changes.\n\n## Contract Principles\n\n- Every external export or feed must expose an explicit contract identifier.\n- Version changes must be additive within a version whenever possible.\n- Breaking schema changes require a new contract version rather than silent\n  mutation of an existing response.\n- Deprecated routes or payloads remain available for at least one supported\n  release cycle after the replacement contract is published, unless security or\n  legal requirements force a faster removal.\n- Contract changes must be reflected in code, tests where applicable, this\n  document, and the roadmap or release notes in the same change set.\n\n## Authentication Strategy\n\nPublic tournament contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"`\n- intended for website visitors, public calendars, and read-only partner\n  consumption\n\nOperator-authenticated reporting exports:\n\n- `auth=\"user\"`\n- require an authenticated backend session\n- intended for federation operators using backend actions and reporting screens\n\nManaged partner contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"` routes protected by partner credentials\n- require `X-Federation-Partner-Code` and `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- enforce per-partner contract subscriptions before a payload is served or a\n  delivery is accepted\n- intended for explicit machine-to-machine integrations without sharing backend\n  user sessions\n\nImport contracts:\n\n- executed either through backend import wizards or through managed partner\n  delivery staging before entering the same wizard flow\n- guarded by dry-run preview, governance-job approval, and checksum matching for\n  live imports\n\n## Public Contracts\n\n## Tournament Feed\n\n- Canonical route: `/api/v1/tournaments/<slug>/feed`\n- Compatibility routes:\n  - `/api/v1/tournaments/<id>/feed`\n  - `/api/v1/competitions/<id>/feed`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_feed`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: v1`\n- Payload anchor:\n  - top-level `api_version = \"v1\"`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - top-level keys in the v1 payload are stable\n  - additive nested fields are allowed in v1 when they do not alter existing\n    semantics\n\n## Tournament Schedule Calendar\n\n- Canonical route: `/tournaments/<slug>/schedule.ics`\n- Compatibility route: `/tournament/<id>/schedule.ics`\n- Response type: `text/calendar`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_schedule_ics`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: ics_v1`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - calendar structure stays compatible with standard ICS consumers\n  - field enrichment should be additive inside event descriptions, not a change\n    to the ICS envelope\n\n## Authenticated CSV Contracts\n\nAll authenticated CSV exports expose these headers:\n\n- `X-Federation-Contract`\n- `X-Federation-Contract-Version`\n\n## Standings Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/standings/<tournament_id>`\n- Contract: `standings_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n- Notes:\n  - intended for downstream standings review and board-pack style extracts\n\n## Participation Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/participation/<season_id>`\n- Contract: `participation_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Summary Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance`\n- Contract: `finance_summary_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Event Handoff Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance/events`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Versioning anchor:\n  - detailed finance-event handoff rows expose a schema version column and the\n    matching response header contract version\n- Required handoff fields include:\n  - event identity and state\n  - handoff state\n  - fee type and amount\n  - invoice, external, accounting-batch, and reconciliation references\n  - source traceability\n  - exported, reconciled, and closed timestamps\n\n## Managed Partner Contracts\n\n## Contract Manifest\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/contracts`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- Payload includes:\n  - contract code, version, direction, transport, and route hint\n  - deprecation stage and replacement contract\n  - `available` flag for database-specific operational availability\n  - partner subscription state and last-used timestamp\n\n## Partner Finance Event Handoff\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`\n- Response type: `text/csv`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Optional query parameters:\n  - `limit` to request one bounded page of rows; defaults to `200` and caps at `500`\n  - `cursor` to resume after the last row from the previous page\n- Invalid `limit` or `cursor` values return `400` with the standard `data_validation` payload.\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: finance_event_v1`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: <schema version>`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code: <partner code>`\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Mode: cursor_page` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Count: <row count>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Has-More: true|false` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Page-Limit: <effective limit>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Next-Cursor: <timestamp>|<id>` when another page is available\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n\n## Inbound Delivery Staging\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/inbound/<contract_code>/deliveries`\n- Method: `POST`\n- Request type: JSON object\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n  - optional `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key` to safely reuse the same staged delivery for matching retries\n- Request fields:\n  - `filename`\n  - `payload_base64`\n  - optional `notes`\n  - optional `source_reference`\n- Response header on every successful delivery request:\n  - `X-Federation-Delivery-Outcome: created|checksum_reuse|idempotency_replay`\n- Response headers when an idempotency key is supplied:\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key: <normalized key>`\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotent-Replay: true|false`\n- Response fields:\n  - `delivery_outcome` with `created`, `checksum_reuse`, or `idempotency_replay`\n  - delivery identity and current state\n  - partner and contract codes\n  - echoed `idempotency_key` when present\n  - payload checksum\n  - contract route hint\n- Duplicate handling:\n  - the same partner, contract, and payload checksum reuse the active staged\n    delivery while it remains in preview or approval flow and report\n    `delivery_outcome = checksum_reuse`\n  - the same partner, contract, and idempotency key replay the original delivery\n    across all states, report `delivery_outcome = idempotency_replay`, and\n    still return `400` if the key is reused for a different payload\n\n## Import Contracts\n\nReusable import templates are versioned backend contracts and live under\n`federation.import.template`.\n\nCurrent template codes:\n\n- `clubs_csv`\n- `players_csv`\n- `seasons_csv`\n- `teams_csv`\n- `tournament_participants_csv`\n\nCurrent template version:\n\n- `csv_v1`\n\nManaged inbound delivery policy:\n\n1. A subscribed partner posts a base64 payload to the inbound delivery route for\n  the relevant contract.\n2. The system stages a `federation.integration.delivery` record, deduplicates\n  active resubmissions by checksum, and can also bind an explicit idempotency\n  key to the request for safer client retries.\n3. Operators open the staged delivery in the matching import wizard for preview.\n4. Approval and live execution continue through the standard governance-job\n  workflow already used for manual rollover imports.\n\nLive import policy:\n\n1. Run a dry-run preview for the uploaded CSV.\n2. Request approval, which creates a governance job tied to the file checksum,\n   target model, template, and preview results.\n3. Approve the governance job.\n4. Execute the live import only if the CSV checksum and selected template still\n   match the approved job.\n\nVerification policy:\n\n- governance jobs store preview totals, execution totals, and before/after\n  target-model record counts\n- live imports that partially succeed remain visible as\n  `completed_with_errors`\n- staged partner deliveries mirror preview, approval, completion, and failure\n  states so operators can reconcile inbound handoffs without leaving the app\n\n## Versioning Policy\n\n- Public JSON versions are encoded in both the path and the payload.\n- CSV and ICS contracts use stable routes plus explicit response headers.\n- Import templates use a version field on the template and a matching schema\n  snapshot on the governance job.\n- Breaking changes require a new contract identifier or version rather than a\n  silent replacement.\n\nEndpoint compatibility policy (v1):\n\n- `/integration/v1/contracts`: additive response changes only; remove fields\n  only in a new API version.\n- `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`: keep CSV column order and header\n  semantics stable for `finance_event_v1` until a new contract code/version is\n  published.\n- `/integration/v1/inbound/{contract_code}/deliveries`: keep\n  `delivery_outcome` semantics (`created`, `checksum_reuse`,\n  `idempotency_replay`) stable within v1.\n- JSON error envelopes for all managed integration endpoints must preserve the\n  typed shape `{error, error_code, correlation_id}` across minor releases.\n\nPartner onboarding references:\n\n- Golden request/response examples: `openapi/examples/INTEGRATION_GOLDEN_EXAMPLES.md`.\n- CI contract guardrails: `ci/check_openapi_contracts.py`.\n\n## Deprecation Policy\n\nThe working list of compatibility aliases, owners, review dates, and target\nsunset dates is maintained here and must be updated in the same change set as\nany contract-facing deprecation decision.\n\n| Surface | Canonical replacement | Target exit |\n|---|---|---|\n| `/tournaments`, `/tournaments/<slug>`, numeric tournament page routes | `/competitions`, `/competitions/<edition-slug>` | 2026-10-01 |\n| Numeric public tournament page routes | Edition routes under `/competitions/<edition-slug>` | 2026-10-01 |\n| Numeric or competition-named v1 tournament feeds | `/api/v1/tournaments/<slug>/feed` | 2026-10-01 |\n| Player import `name` column fallback | Explicit `first_name`, `last_name` columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Team import name fallbacks | `club_code` and explicit team naming columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Participant import tournament/team name fallbacks | `tournament_code` and `team_code` | 2026-10-15 |\n\nRemove a compatibility surface only after its replacement is documented,\ncovered by tests, and announced in the owning module README. If a target date\npasses without a removal decision, extend it here with the reason.\n\n- Slug-based public routes are canonical.\n- Numeric public routes remain compatibility shims and should not be used for\n  new integrations.\n- Legacy competition-named public feed routes remain compatibility aliases for\n  the tournament feed and are considered deprecated in favor of the canonical\n  tournament path.\n- Older CSV shapes should remain available for one supported release cycle once\n  a replacement contract is published.\n- Removals must be announced by updating this file, relevant READMEs, and the\n  roadmap in the same release window.\n\n## Integration configuration\n\nCI and local development use environment variables for SMTP, OAuth, partner\ntokens, webhooks, and object storage. partner-facing contracts currently supported by\nthe federation platform and the policy used to version, evolve, and deprecate\nthem.\n\nMachine-readable partner route definitions live in `openapi/integration_v1.yaml`.\nKeep the OpenAPI file, this document, and the route implementations aligned in\nthe same change set whenever a managed integration contract changes.\n\n## Contract Principles\n\n- Every external export or feed must expose an explicit contract identifier.\n- Version changes must be additive within a version whenever possible.\n- Breaking schema changes require a new contract version rather than silent\n  mutation of an existing response.\n- Deprecated routes or payloads remain available for at least one supported\n  release cycle after the replacement contract is published, unless security or\n  legal requirements force a faster removal.\n- Contract changes must be reflected in code, tests where applicable, this\n  document, and the roadmap or release notes in the same change set.\n\n## Authentication Strategy\n\nPublic tournament contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"`\n- intended for website visitors, public calendars, and read-only partner\n  consumption\n\nOperator-authenticated reporting exports:\n\n- `auth=\"user\"`\n- require an authenticated backend session\n- intended for federation operators using backend actions and reporting screens\n\nManaged partner contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"` routes protected by partner credentials\n- require `X-Federation-Partner-Code` and `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- enforce per-partner contract subscriptions before a payload is served or a\n  delivery is accepted\n- intended for explicit machine-to-machine integrations without sharing backend\n  user sessions\n\nImport contracts:\n\n- executed either through backend import wizards or through managed partner\n  delivery staging before entering the same wizard flow\n- guarded by dry-run preview, governance-job approval, and checksum matching for\n  live imports\n\n## Public Contracts\n\n## Tournament Feed\n\n- Canonical route: `/api/v1/competitions/<edition-slug>`\n- Compatibility routes:\n  - `/api/v1/competitions/<edition-slug>`\n  - `/api/v1/competitions/<id>/feed`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_feed`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: v1`\n- Payload anchor:\n  - top-level `api_version = \"v1\"`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - top-level keys in the v1 payload are stable\n  - additive nested fields are allowed in v1 when they do not alter existing\n    semantics\n\n## Tournament Schedule Calendar\n\n- Canonical route: `/competitions/<edition-slug>/divisions/<division-slug>/schedule.ics`\n- Compatibility route: `/competitions/<edition-slug>/divisions/<division-slug>/schedule.ics`\n- Response type: `text/calendar`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_schedule_ics`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: ics_v1`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - calendar structure stays compatible with standard ICS consumers\n  - field enrichment should be additive inside event descriptions, not a change\n    to the ICS envelope\n\n## Authenticated CSV Contracts\n\nAll authenticated CSV exports expose these headers:\n\n- `X-Federation-Contract`\n- `X-Federation-Contract-Version`\n\n## Standings Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/standings/<tournament_id>`\n- Contract: `standings_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n- Notes:\n  - intended for downstream standings review and board-pack style extracts\n\n## Participation Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/participation/<season_id>`\n- Contract: `participation_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Summary Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance`\n- Contract: `finance_summary_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Event Handoff Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance/events`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Versioning anchor:\n  - detailed finance-event handoff rows expose a schema version column and the\n    matching response header contract version\n- Required handoff fields include:\n  - event identity and state\n  - handoff state\n  - fee type and amount\n  - invoice, external, accounting-batch, and reconciliation references\n  - source traceability\n  - exported, reconciled, and closed timestamps\n\n## Managed Partner Contracts\n\n## Contract Manifest\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/contracts`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- Payload includes:\n  - contract code, version, direction, transport, and route hint\n  - deprecation stage and replacement contract\n  - `available` flag for database-specific operational availability\n  - partner subscription state and last-used timestamp\n\n## Partner Finance Event Handoff\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`\n- Response type: `text/csv`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Optional query parameters:\n  - `limit` to request one bounded page of rows; defaults to `200` and caps at `500`\n  - `cursor` to resume after the last row from the previous page\n- Invalid `limit` or `cursor` values return `400` with the standard `data_validation` payload.\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: finance_event_v1`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: <schema version>`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code: <partner code>`\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Mode: cursor_page` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Count: <row count>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Has-More: true|false` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Page-Limit: <effective limit>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Next-Cursor: <timestamp>|<id>` when another page is available\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n\n## Inbound Delivery Staging\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/inbound/<contract_code>/deliveries`\n- Method: `POST`\n- Request type: JSON object\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n  - optional `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key` to safely reuse the same staged delivery for matching retries\n- Request fields:\n  - `filename`\n  - `payload_base64`\n  - optional `notes`\n  - optional `source_reference`\n- Response header on every successful delivery request:\n  - `X-Federation-Delivery-Outcome: created|checksum_reuse|idempotency_replay`\n- Response headers when an idempotency key is supplied:\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key: <normalized key>`\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotent-Replay: true|false`\n- Response fields:\n  - `delivery_outcome` with `created`, `checksum_reuse`, or `idempotency_replay`\n  - delivery identity and current state\n  - partner and contract codes\n  - echoed `idempotency_key` when present\n  - payload checksum\n  - contract route hint\n- Duplicate handling:\n  - the same partner, contract, and payload checksum reuse the active staged\n    delivery while it remains in preview or approval flow and report\n    `delivery_outcome = checksum_reuse`\n  - the same partner, contract, and idempotency key replay the original delivery\n    across all states, report `delivery_outcome = idempotency_replay`, and\n    still return `400` if the key is reused for a different payload\n\n## Import Contracts\n\nReusable import templates are versioned backend contracts and live under\n`federation.import.template`.\n\nCurrent template codes:\n\n- `clubs_csv`\n- `players_csv`\n- `seasons_csv`\n- `teams_csv`\n- `tournament_participants_csv`\n\nCurrent template version:\n\n- `csv_v1`\n\nManaged inbound delivery policy:\n\n1. A subscribed partner posts a base64 payload to the inbound delivery route for\n  the relevant contract.\n2. The system stages a `federation.integration.delivery` record, deduplicates\n  active resubmissions by checksum, and can also bind an explicit idempotency\n  key to the request for safer client retries.\n3. Operators open the staged delivery in the matching import wizard for preview.\n4. Approval and live execution continue through the standard governance-job\n  workflow already used for manual rollover imports.\n\nLive import policy:\n\n1. Run a dry-run preview for the uploaded CSV.\n2. Request approval, which creates a governance job tied to the file checksum,\n   target model, template, and preview results.\n3. Approve the governance job.\n4. Execute the live import only if the CSV checksum and selected template still\n   match the approved job.\n\nVerification policy:\n\n- governance jobs store preview totals, execution totals, and before/after\n  target-model record counts\n- live imports that partially succeed remain visible as\n  `completed_with_errors`\n- staged partner deliveries mirror preview, approval, completion, and failure\n  states so operators can reconcile inbound handoffs without leaving the app\n\n## Versioning Policy\n\n- Public JSON versions are encoded in both the path and the payload.\n- CSV and ICS contracts use stable routes plus explicit response headers.\n- Import templates use a version field on the template and a matching schema\n  snapshot on the governance job.\n- Breaking changes require a new contract identifier or version rather than a\n  silent replacement.\n\nEndpoint compatibility policy (v1):\n\n- `/integration/v1/contracts`: additive response changes only; remove fields\n  only in a new API version.\n- `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`: keep CSV column order and header\n  semantics stable for `finance_event_v1` until a new contract code/version is\n  published.\n- `/integration/v1/inbound/{contract_code}/deliveries`: keep\n  `delivery_outcome` semantics (`created`, `checksum_reuse`,\n  `idempotency_replay`) stable within v1.\n- JSON error envelopes for all managed integration endpoints must preserve the\n  typed shape `{error, error_code, correlation_id}` across minor releases.\n\nPartner onboarding references:\n\n- Golden request/response examples: `openapi/examples/INTEGRATION_GOLDEN_EXAMPLES.md`.\n- CI contract guardrails: `ci/check_openapi_contracts.py`.\n\n## Deprecation Policy\n\nThe working list of compatibility aliases, owners, review dates, and target\nsunset dates is maintained here and must be updated in the same change set as\nany contract-facing deprecation decision.\n\n| Surface | Canonical replacement | Target exit |\n|---|---|---|\n| Player import `name` column fallback | Explicit `first_name`, `last_name` columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Team import name fallbacks | `club_code` and explicit team naming columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Participant import tournament/team name fallbacks | `tournament_code` and `team_code` | 2026-10-15 |\n\nRemove a compatibility surface only after its replacement is documented,\ncovered by tests, and announced in the owning module README. If a target date\npasses without a removal decision, extend it here with the reason.\n\n- Slug-based public routes are canonical.\n- Numeric public routes remain compatibility shims and should not be used for\n  new integrations.\n- Legacy competition-named public feed routes remain compatibility aliases for\n  the tournament feed and are considered deprecated in favor of the canonical\n  tournament path.\n- Older CSV shapes should remain available for one supported release cycle once\n  a replacement contract is published.\n- Removals must be announced by updating this file, relevant READMEs, and the\n  roadmap in the same release window.\n\n## Integration configuration\n\nCI and local development use environment variables for SMTP, OAuth, partner\ntokens, webhooks, and object storage. Copy `ci/integrations.env.example` to\n`ci/.env`; never commit credentials. The CI helper writes non-empty values to\nOdoo system parameters with the `integration.` prefix, including:\n\n- `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_USE_TLS`,\n  `EMAIL_FROM`;\n- `SENDGRID_API_KEY`, `MAILGUN_API_KEY`;\n- `OAUTH_GOOGLE_*`, `OAUTH_GITHUB_*`;\n- `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`;\n- `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `S3_BUCKET`, `S3_REGION`;\n- `ALLOWED_HOSTS`.\n\nRead global parameters through `ir.config_parameter` and do not log secret\nvalues. Upload malware scanning, when enabled, uses\n`sports_federation.attachment_scan.command` and\n`sports_federation.attachment_scan.timeout_seconds`; exit code `0` means clean,\n`10` means infected, and any other non-zero code means verification failed.\n\n## Notification matrix\n\nThe notification dispatcher is non-blocking and records delivery outcomes in\n`federation.notification.log`. Business actions trigger the following current\nnotifications:\n\n| Event | Recipient or audience | Channel |\n|---|---|---|\n| Season registration confirmed or returned | Submitting representative or club contact | Email |\n| Tournament published | Participant club and team contacts | Email |\n| Participant confirmed | Team and club contacts | Email |\n| Result submitted | Result validators | Activity |\n| Result approved or contested | Team/club contacts; managers for contests | Email |\n| Standing frozen | Participant club contacts | Email |\n| Finance event confirmed | Partner or club/player/referee contact | Email |\n| Referee assigned | Referee | Email |\n| Overdue referee confirmation or officiating shortage | Federation managers | Activity |\n\nDelivery failures must not roll back the business transaction. Failed sends are\nlogged for retry or operator investigation; dispatcher methods must not raise a\nbusiness validation error.\n\n\n## Public competition feed v1\n\n`GET /api/v1/competitions` and `GET /api/v1/competitions/<edition_slug>` expose only published, non-sensitive competition data. Confirm the target branch is merged and the working tree is clean enough to\n   identify the intended release diff.\n2. Confirm Docker services are healthy with the production compose file.\n3. Confirm enough disk space exists for both a PostgreSQL dump and a filestore\n   archive under `./backups/`.\n\n## Documentation Freshness\n\nBefore cutting a release, verify that the freshness-tracked docs still match the\nchange set whenever route ownership, architecture, CI policy, or operational\nguidance changed:\n\n```bash\npython3 addons/ci/check_doc_freshness.py\npython3 addons/ci/check_markdown_links.py\npython3 addons/ci/check_module_owners.py\npython3 addons/ci/check_openapi_contracts.py\n```\n\nIf the release changed any tracked surface, update the affected document or\narchive it in the same release branch before proceeding.\n\nIf the release changed portal privilege boundaries, reporting SQL view policy,\nor canonical public route ownership, review the affected record under `adr/`\nand update it in the same release branch when the decision changed.\n\nIf the release includes model, view, or controller ownership changes, confirm\nthe migration-review gate passes and that every affected module has either\nrelease-note coverage or an explicit migration script:\n\n```bash\npython3 addons/ci/check_migration_review.py --base-ref origin/main\n```\n\nFor the same release branch, record migration evidence and rollback notes in\nthis runbook:\n\n```bash\n# add the commands, outcomes, rollback triggers, and SQL/drop steps\n${EDITOR:-vi} addons/RELEASE_RUNBOOK.md\n```\n\n### Portal controller-load repair evidence\n\nThe portal repair removes the stale re-export of the deleted V1 workspace\ncontroller, restores the tournament-registration view in the manifest data\norder, and keeps officiating assignment visibility limited to live current\npublications. No database migration is required; the portal manifest is bumped\nfrom `19.0.4.0.0` to `19.0.4.1.0`.\n\n### Formatting-only model review evidence\n\nThe 2026-09-03 formatting change touched model files in\n`sports_federation_base`, `sports_federation_competition_core`,\n`sports_federation_format`, `sports_federation_import_tools`,\n`sports_federation_notifications`, `sports_federation_reporting`,\n`sports_federation_schedule_approval`, and\n`sports_federation_scheduling`. It made no schema, data, or workflow changes,\nso no database migration is required. The migration-review dry run must include\nthis record and pass before release promotion.\n\nDry-run evidence captured on 2026-08-23:\n\n```text\n./scripts/upgrade_sports_federation.sh --db odoo --dry-run\nExit code: 0\nUpgrade: sports_federation_base,...,sports_federation_portal,...,sports_federation_venues\nInstall: none\n```\n\nFocused verification:\n\n```text\nbash ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_portal\nExit code: 0; 116 tests run, 116 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors; 30 post-tests\n```\n\nRollback is the standard backup restore procedure in this runbook. Do not\nrestore the deleted V1 controller or broaden portal publication access as a\nrollback workaround.\n\n### Release-candidate readiness review\n\nThe release-candidate readiness contracts cover role-separated access,\nworkflow recovery actions, portal usability surfaces, performance profile\nmetadata, and the required release evidence files. Run the static lane before\nstarting database qualification:\n\n```bash\nscripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh static\n```\n\nThe complete candidate sequence is:\n\n```bash\nscripts/ci/run_release_candidate.sh --backup-dir /path/to/approved-backup\n```\n\nThe script performs the product-readiness and usability contract checks,\nrelease-baseline lanes, and (when an approved backup is supplied) the migration\nrehearsal. Record the candidate SHA, lane results, database names, and any\nrollback observations with the release ticket. Browser lanes require a Chrome\nexecutable; a candidate is not accepted when those lanes are silently skipped.\n\nIf the release changes addon responsibility boundaries or adds a new\n`sports_federation_*` module, update `MODULE_OWNERS.yaml` in the same release\nbranch and rerun the registry check before cutting the release.\n\nIf the release changes log retention, staged-delivery cleanup, or generated\nreport artifact handling, update `DATA_RETENTION_POLICY.md` in the same branch\nand confirm the affected cleanup crons still match the documented windows.\n\n## Pre-Release Verification\n\nRun the focused suites that cover the highest-risk federation workflows:\n\n```bash\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --suite portal_public_ops\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --suite finance_reporting\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --suite release_surfaces\n```\n\nIf the release changed retention jobs or cleanup scope, also re-run the\naffected module suites The\nreplacement ownership chain is `sports_federation_competition_core`,\n`sports_federation_registration`, `sports_federation_format`,\n`sports_federation_calendar`, `sports_federation_scheduling`,\n`sports_federation_schedule_approval`, and `sports_federation_matchday`.\n\nBefore upgrading a database that previously installed the legacy engine:\n\n1. Take the database and filestore backups described above.\n2. Run the upgrade script with `--dry-run` and confirm that the resolved module\n   list contains the chain and does not contain the removed addon.\n3. Run the upgrade in a disposable restore of the backup first, then verify\n   registration, format freeze, calendar capacity, scheduling, approval\n   publication, and match-day operations.\n4. Record the dry-run output and restore-drill result with the release ticket;\n   do not silently reinterpret legacy planner or published-schedule records.\n\nIf the restore drill or production upgrade fails, stop Odoo, preserve the\nfailed logs, restore the database and filestore backup, and restart the prior\nrelease. Do not reinstall the removed engine as an ad-hoc rollback; use the\nreviewed database migration or rollback procedure for the target release.\n\n### Legacy ownership-removal review record\n\nThe repository-side review for this ownership change was completed against the\nrecorded base commit before preparing the release patch. The following checks\nare the minimum evidence to attach to the release ticket:\n\n```bash\nbash -n addons/ci/run_tests.sh\nbash -n addons/scripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh\npython3 addons/ci/check_legacy_engine_removed.py\ngit -C addons apply --check addons/legacy_removal.patch\n```\n\nThe shell checks, loadability guard, and clean-worktree patch check must all\npass. The database restore drill remains mandatory before production upgrade;\nits output must be attached to the release ticket rather than inferred from\nrepository checks. No historical migration directory is reused for this\nownership removal, and no production record is silently rewritten.\n\nRollback is backup-based: stop the target release, preserve logs and the failed\ndatabase state for review, restore the pre-upgrade database and filestore, and\nrestart the previous release. If a data transformation is later required, it\nmust be introduced in a new reviewed migration with an explicit backfill and\nrollback plan; reinstalling the removed addon is not an approved rollback.\n\n## Backups\n\nThe upgrade script performs backups by default. It stores:\n\n- `modules.txt` with the exact install/upgrade module list\n- `<db>_<timestamp>.dump` as a PostgreSQL custom-format dump\n- `filestore_<db>_<timestamp>.tar.gz` when a filestore exists under\n  `./odoo-data/filestore/<db>`\n\nDo not use `--skip-backup` for production releases.\n\nRun the periodic restore drill against one of these backup directories before\nor during each release train using the restore checklist in this runbook:\n\n```bash\nbash addons/ci/restore_backup_drill.sh --backup-dir 2026-04-15_191410 --target-db odoo_restore_drill --dry-run\n```\n\n## Production Upgrade\n\nRun the upgrade and let the script restart the live Odoo service afterward so\nPython changes are loaded by the running web container:\n\n```bash\n./scripts/upgrade_sports_federation.sh --db odoo\n```\n\nFor a non-interactive upgrade that excludes demo data, use `--yes`. To include\nthe demo addon non-interactively, add `--install-demo`.\n\nThe script installs modules that are missing or uninstalled, upgrades modules\nthat are already installed, and restarts the Odoo service. It runs:\n\n- `odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d <db> -i <install_module_csv> -u <upgrade_module_csv> --stop-after-init`\n- `docker compose restart odoo`\n\nThe demo addon is excluded by default. Interactive runs ask whether\n`sports_federation_demo` should be installed. Use `--install-demo` when that\nchoice is intentional and the upgrade is non-interactive.\n\n## Post-Upgrade Verification\n\nVerify these operator checkpoints immediately after the upgrade:\n\n1. Open Federation > Reporting > Operator Checklist and confirm there are no\n   unexpected blocked queues.\n2. Open Federation > Reporting > Report Schedules and confirm there are no new\n   `Last Run Failed` schedules.\n3. Open Federation > Import Tools > Inbound Deliveries and confirm there are no\n   unexpected `failed` or `processed_with_errors` deliveries.\n4. Validate the public and portal release surfaces manually if the release\n   touched them:\n   - `/web/login`\n   - `/tournaments`\n   - `/tournaments/<slug>/register`\n   - `/my/teams/new`\n   - `/my/season-registration/new`\n   - `/my/compliance`\n5. Trigger one scheduled report manually from Federation > Reporting > Report\n   Schedules if the release touched reporting code.\n\n## Integration Partner Token Rotation\n\nAfter any release that modifies integration partner credentials, or on a\nscheduled rotation cycle, rotate partner tokens using the following procedure:\n\n**When to rotate:**\n- After upgrading `sports_federation_import_tools` (any release that changed\n  token storage, authentication, or the integration controller surface).\n- When the `token_rotation_required` flag is set to `True` on a partner record\n  (visible in Federation > Import Tools > Integration Partners).\n- On a periodic schedule — at minimum once per year or whenever a partner\n  personnel change occurs.\n\n**How to rotate (back-office procedure):**\n\n1. Open **Federation > Import Tools > Integration Partners**.\n2. Filter for partners where **Token Rotation Required** is checked, or where\n   **Last Rotated On** is older than the rotation policy window.\n3. For each partner, open the form and click **Rotate Token** (requires\n   Federation Manager group). Confirm the dialog.\n4. The wizard reveals the new raw token **once** (it cannot be retrieved again).\n   Copy it immediately and deliver it to the partner over a secure channel\n   (not email in plain text).\n5. The `token_rotation_required` flag clears automatically after a successful\n   rotation.\n\n**After a migration from plaintext storage:**\n\nIf `sports_federation_import_tools` was upgraded from a version prior to\n`19.0.1.2.0`, existing plaintext tokens were hashed in place and flagged for\nrotation by the post-migration script. Partners with `Token Rotation Required`\nset to `True` are still functional (their hashed token verifies correctly)\nbut should be rotated and re-issued at the next opportunity.\n\n**Verification:**\n\nAfter rotation, ask the partner to make one authenticated test call and confirm\na `200 OK` response to `/integration/v1/contracts`. A `401` response with\n`access_denied` indicates the token was not delivered correctly.\n\n## Rollback\n\nIf the upgrade must be rolled back:\n\n1. Stop or scale down the Odoo service to prevent new writes.\n2. Restore the PostgreSQL dump from the relevant backup directory.\n3. Restore the matching filestore archive.\n4. Restart the Odoo service.\n5. Re-run the post-upgrade verification checklist against the restored system.\n\nExample restore outline:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose stop odoo\ndropdb -U odoo odoo\ncreatedb -U odoo odoo\npg_restore -U odoo -d odoo backups/<timestamp>/odoo_<timestamp>.dump\ntar -xzf backups/<timestamp>/filestore_odoo_<timestamp>.tar.gz -C odoo-data/filestore\ndocker compose up -d odoo\n```\n\nAdjust database names and paths to match the selected backup directory.\n\n---\n\n## Upgrade Path Notes (per release train)\n\nThis section records DB migrations, new `ir.config_parameter` keys, deprecated\nfield removals, and module install order changes introduced in each release.\nAdd a subsection here for every release train that makes schema or behavioural\nchanges. The next release cycle must prioritize simpler operator workflows, clearer ownership boundaries, and production evidence over additional domain breadth.\n\n## Delivery Principles\n\n- Keep internal audit, security, revision, and concurrency safeguards.\n- Hide technical implementation concepts from normal club and tournament users.\n- Use guided defaults for common workflows and progressive disclosure for expert controls.\n- Keep every privileged portal write behind a model-owned scope check.\n- Treat migrations, restore readiness, observability, and documentation as release gates.\n- Prefer one authoritative document per concern. Delete completed mini-roadmaps and generated snapshots that duplicate tests or code.\n\n## Delivery Roadmap\n\nThe executable milestone sequence is maintained in\n[`docs/DELIVERY_ROADMAP.md`](docs/DELIVERY_ROADMAP.md). This repository roadmap\nremains the priority and policy source; the delivery roadmap defines concrete\ndeliverables, automation, and exit criteria.\n\n## Current Priorities\n\n### P0: Simplify competition and portal workflows\n\nStatus: In progress\n\n- Provide template-led setup for league, tournament-day, and cup formats.\n- Reduce user-facing lifecycle language to Draft, Ready, Live, and Finished while retaining richer internal states.\n- Keep stage graphs, schedule revisions, fairness tuning, and shared-day controls behind Advanced tools.\n- Make normal schedules preparable without Run module upgrades against a production-like database copy.\n- Record backup, restore, rollback, and migration evidence for each release candidate.\n- Resolve dependency-drift warnings before release, even when they are non-blocking.\n\n### P0: Security and ownership boundaries\n\nStatus: Ongoing\n\n- Maintain negative cross-club and direct-ID access tests for every portal write route.\n- public, portal, or partner integration route.\n\n### P1: Background-job reliability\n\nStatus: Planned\n\n- Standardize retry and backoff behavior.\n- Add dead-letter and operator recovery Trigger one scheduled report manually from Federation > Reporting > Report\n   Schedules if the release touched reporting code.\n\n## Integration Partner Token Rotation\n\nAfter any release that modifies integration partner credentials, or on a\nscheduled rotation cycle, rotate partner tokens using the following procedure:\n\n**When to rotate:**\n- After upgrading `sports_federation_import_tools` (any release that changed\n  token storage, authentication, or the integration controller surface).\n- When the `token_rotation_required` flag is set to `True` on a partner record\n  (visible in Federation > Import Tools > Integration Partners).\n- On a periodic schedule — at minimum once per year or whenever a partner\n  personnel change occurs.\n\n**How to rotate (back-office procedure):**\n\n1. Open **Federation > Import Tools > Integration Partners**.\n2. Filter for partners where **Token Rotation Required** is checked, or where\n   **Last Rotated On** is older than the rotation policy window.\n3. For each partner, open the form and click **Rotate Token** (requires\n   Federation Manager group). Confirm the dialog.\n4. The wizard reveals the new raw token **once** (it cannot be retrieved again).\n   Copy it immediately and deliver it to the partner over a secure channel\n   (not email in plain text).\n5. The `token_rotation_required` flag clears automatically after a successful\n   rotation.\n\n**After a migration from plaintext storage:**\n\nIf `sports_federation_import_tools` was upgraded from a version prior to\n`19.0.1.2.0`, existing plaintext tokens were hashed in place and flagged for\nrotation by the post-migration script. Partners with `Token Rotation Required`\nset to `True` are still functional (their hashed token verifies correctly)\nbut should be rotated and re-issued at the next opportunity.\n\n**Verification:**\n\nAfter rotation, ask the partner to make one authenticated test call and confirm\na `200 OK` response to `/integration/v1/contracts`. A `401` response with\n`access_denied` indicates the token was not delivered correctly.\n\n## Rollback\n\nIf the upgrade must be rolled back:\n\n1. Stop or scale down the Odoo service to prevent new writes.\n2. Restore the PostgreSQL dump from the relevant backup directory.\n3. Restore the matching filestore archive.\n4. Restart the Odoo service.\n5. Re-run the post-upgrade verification checklist against the restored system.\n\nExample restore outline:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose stop odoo\ndropdb -U odoo odoo\ncreatedb -U odoo odoo\npg_restore -U odoo -d odoo backups/<timestamp>/odoo_<timestamp>.dump\ntar -xzf backups/<timestamp>/filestore_odoo_<timestamp>.tar.gz -C odoo-data/filestore\ndocker compose up -d odoo\n```\n\nAdjust database names and paths to match the selected backup directory.\n\n---\n\n## Upgrade Path Notes (per release train)\n\nThis section records DB migrations, new `ir.config_parameter` keys, deprecated\nfield removals, and module install order changes introduced in each release.\nAdd a subsection here for every release train that makes schema or behavioural\nchanges. It is intended to keep\ncontrollers, record rules, tests, and workflow docs aligned with the code.\n\n## Canonical records\n\n| Record | Module | Primary owner | Create path | Canonical states | Ownership boundary | Notes |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| `federation.tournament` | `sports_federation_tournament` + `sports_federation_portal` | Federation competition operations | Backend UI, scheduling services, website publication helpers | `draft`, `open`, `in_progress`, `closed`, `cancelled` | Federation-owned season / competition scope | Portal tournament workspaces only expose active tournaments (`open`, `in_progress`) and only for teams inside the user's current whole-club or explicit team scope. |\n| `federation.match` | `sports_federation_tournament` | Federation competition operations | Backend UI, scheduling services, wizards | `draft`, `scheduled`, `in_progress`, `done`, `cancelled` | Federation-owned tournament/stage/group | Official standings inclusion is further gated by `include_in_official_standings` when `sports_federation_result_control` is installed. |\n| `federation.schedule.slot` | `sports_federation_calendar` | Calendar operations prepare capacity; scheduling assigns fixtures; approval publishes the resulting schedule | Match-day calendar and scheduling views | `available`, `break`, `blocked` | Federation-owned match day / playing-area scope | A slot belongs to one match day. Fixture assignment and overlap validation are enforced server-side. |\n| `federation.standing` | `sports_federation_standings` | Federation competition operations | Backend UI, recompute/freeze actions | `draft`, `computed`, `frozen` | Federation-owned tournament/stage/group | Only computed or frozen standings are publication candidates. |\n| `federation.tournament.participant` | `sports_federation_tournament` | Federation competition operations | Backend UI or confirmed tournament registration | `registered`, `confirmed`, `withdrawn` | Team's club within a federation tournament | Portal users do not write participants directly; confirmed registrations may create them. |\n| `federation.competition.entry` | `sports_federation_portal` | Shared: club representative submits, federation staff reviews | Portal form or backend UI | `draft`, `submitted`, `confirmed`, `rejected`, `cancelled` | Team must belong to one of the submitting user's represented clubs | This is the review buffer before participant creation. |\n| `federation.season.registration` | `sports_federation_base` + `sports_federation_portal` | Shared: club representative submits, federation staff confirms | Portal form or backend UI | `draft`, `submitted`, `confirmed`, `cancelled` | Team must belong to one of the submitting user's represented clubs | Portal extension adds `submitted`, `user_id`, and `rejection_reason`. Rejecting a registration returns it to `draft`; there is no persistent `rejected` enum. |\n| `federation.finance.event` | `sports_federation_finance_bridge` | Federation finance operations and approved workflow hooks | Backend UI or workflow automation | `draft`, `confirmed`, `settled`, `cancelled` | Source record remains authoritative; finance staff own settlement/cancellation | Season-registration confirmation and match finance hooks create events automatically. |\n\n## Archive behavior\n\nThe core master-data records now expose explicit archive and restore actions in\nthe backend UI so operational records do not disappear through ad hoc writes to\n`active`.\n\n| Record | Archive guardrail |\n| --- | --- |\n| `federation.club` | Clubs can only be archived after their active teams are archived. |\n| `federation.team` | Teams can only be archived when all linked season registrations are cancelled. |\n| `federation.season` | Open seasons must be closed or cancelled before they can be archived. |\n| `federation.tournament` | Open or in-progress tournaments must be closed or cancelled before they can be archived. |\n\n## Transition ownership\n\n| Record | Transition owners | Guardrails |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `federation.tournament` | Federation staff for lifecycle transitions; portal layer for read-only workspace access | Portal workspace helpers must revalidate both active-tournament scope and the caller's visible team or club scope before any elevated detail read. |\n| `federation.match` | Federation staff, scheduling services, result-control roles | Public routes are read-only. Match completion may trigger bracket advancement, and result-control transitions may trigger non-frozen standings recomputation. |\n| `federation.schedule.slot` | Calendar owns slot capacity and lifecycle; scheduling assigns fixtures; schedule approval publishes the resulting schedule | Slot availability and capacity are prepared by `sports_federation_calendar`; assignment validation is enforced by `sports_federation_scheduling`;
