Its stage-to-stage edges are represented by `federation.structure.stage.progression`, with `structure_id`, source-stage, and target-stage relations. This model must not reuse the competition engine's `federation.stage.progression` name: the engine model is tournament-oriented and has a different inverse relation contract (`tournament_id`). The distinction allows both addons to be installed in the same registry without field-resolution collisions.\n\nStage-graph ACLs are loaded through the addon's conventional `security/ir.model.access.csv` file. Format Studio's inherited view selects the stage tab structurally by its `stage_ids` field rather than by the translated page label.\n\n- `federation.tournament.round` (in `sports_federation_tournament`) — materialises a logical round inside a stage. Rounds own shared schedule metadata such as sequence and calendar date, and matches attach to them for per-round planning and reporting.\n\n- Round venue extensions (in `sports_federation_venues`) — add `venue_id` to `federation.tournament.round` so venue ownership sits on the same round object that already owns the schedule date and sequence.\n\n- Match bracket/linking fields — `federation.match` now includes: `round_id`, `round_number`, `bracket_position`, `bracket_type`, `source_match_1_id`, `source_match_2_id`, `source_type_1/2` and helper `next_match_ids`. These turn matches into first-class bracket nodes so full knockout trees can be created and wired together programmatically.\n\n- Full knockout bracket generation — the knockout service now constructs a full bracket tree (all rounds) rather than only first-round matches. Placeholder matches for later rounds are created and linked to their source matches (by `source_match_*`); when a match is completed the system will auto-populate winners/losers into the next round using the `action_done()` / `_advance_bracket_teams()` logic.\n\n- Round-robin enhancements — the round-robin service now returns explicit per-round pairings, supports `rounds_count` (repeat full cycles), always materialises `federation.tournament.round` records, and can derive round dates from `schedule_by_round`. Existing stage rounds are reused by sequence order, and when a `venue` string matches a `federation.venue` record the scheduler applies it to the round and linked matches. The service also attempts to alternate `male` / `female` fixtures within a round to provide rest.\n\nImplementation notes\n\n- Round constraints: the `sports_federation_venues` module extends `federation.match` so teams in the same `category` cannot play the same opponent more than once inside the same round. This prevents repeated pairings inside a shared round block.\n\n- Alternation policy: when scheduling by round the scheduler partitions same-gender fixtures and interleaves male/female matches where possible. Mixed-gender fixtures are appended after the alternation. This is a best-effort policy (it preserves determinism but will not re-seed teams).\n\n- Auto-advance: `federation.standing.action_freeze()` triggers any `federation.stage.progression` rules with `auto_advance=True` for the stage/group being frozen — this provides an automated pipeline from computed standings into new stage participants (and is safe-guarded by the progression rule's `state`).\n\n- Venue handling: the `venue` free-text field has been removed from `federation.match`. Use `venue_id` (Many2one to `federation.venue`) instead. The round-robin and knockout wizards accept a venue name string and resolve it to a `federation.venue` record to populate the generated rounds and linked matches.\n\nTesting and coverage\n\nAdd unit and integration tests covering the following:\n\n- `federation.stage.progression`: ensure `action_execute()` selects the correct teams across single-group and cross-group rules and that `seeding_method` options behave as documented.\n- `federation.tournament.template`: applying a template creates the expected stages, groups and progression rules.\n- Round-robin scheduling: `rounds_count`, `schedule_by_round`, automatic round materialisation, alternation of male/female fixtures, and repeat cycles.\n- Knockout bracket generation: bracket size determination, bye handling, and automatic wiring of placeholder matches and advancement on `action_done()`.\n- Round constraints: enforce no duplicate same-category pairings inside the same round.\n\n## Architecture and conventions\n\nThis technical note documents architecture, coding conventions, workflows, and extension points for the Sports Federation Odoo 19 custom addons collection located in the `odoo/` folder. It is intended for developers, integrators, and release engineers working on federation features: tournaments, matches, rosters, refereeing, results pipelines, and public website publication.\n\n### Shared workflow state helpers (2026-04-18)\n\nWhere one addon reuses the same workflow vocabulary across multiple models,\nkeep the selection tuples and state-role predicates in a small plain Python\nhelper module instead of repeating raw string tuples in each model.\n\n- `sports_federation_import_tools/workflow_states.py` now owns the inbound\n    delivery and import-governance lifecycle constants used by the delivery\n    model, governance job model, wizard mixin, migration backfill, and tests.\n- `sports_federation_governance/workflow_states.py` now owns the override\n    request and decision lifecycle constants used by the request, decision,\n    outcome, and test modules.\n- When new logic only needs to know the semantic role of a state, prefer a\n    helper predicate such as `is_import_job_approved(...)` over direct string\n    comparisons so future state changes stay localized.\n\n## Table of contents\n\n- Executive summary\n- High-level architecture and module responsibilities\n- Data model conventions and patterns\n- Workflows and state machines (tournament lifecycle, match-day, result pipeline)\n- Competition engine — algorithms, wizards, and deterministic behaviours\n- Controllers, portal, and public site patterns\n- Security model and record rules\n- Performance, scaling and operational concerns\n- Testing, CI and quality gates\n- Upgrade, migrations and deployment notes\n- Developer workflow: how to add models, wizards, views, and tests\n- Examples and reference snippets\n\n## Executive summary\n\nThe project is a modular suite of Odoo 19 addons implementing a sports federation management system. Modules are intentionally small and focused: `sports_federation_base` owns master data (clubs, teams, seasons), `sports_federation_tournament` implements tournament structure and match records, and the competition addons own registration, format, calendar, scheduling, approval, and match-day operations. Domain features (`people`, `rosters`, `officiating`, `result_control`, `standings`, `public_site`, `notifications`, `reporting`) extend core behaviour without mixing responsibilities.\n\nDesign goals\n\n- Keep modules decoupled and installable independently where practical.\n- Encode business logic in computed models and service/wizard classes rather than ad-hoc scripts.\n- Enforce separation of duties via groups and record rules (submit/verify/approve in the result pipeline).\n- Make scheduling deterministic and testable (repeatable outputs from the same inputs).\n\n## High-level architecture and module responsibilities\n\n- `sports_federation_base` — Master data: `federation.club`, `federation.team`, `federation.season`, `federation.season.registration`. Ownership of base security groups and global menus. Holds common `ir.sequence` definitions.\n- `sports_federation_tournament` — Tournament structure: `federation.competition`, `federation.tournament`, `federation.tournament.stage`, `federation.group`, `federation.tournament.participant`, and `federation.match`. Implements match lifecycle and basic match behaviour.\n- `sports_federation_format` and `sports_federation_scheduling` — Structure generation, deterministic fixture assignment, validation, and fairness services. Keep algorithmic code stateless and place transient entrypoints in the owning module's `wizards/` package.\n- `sports_federation_people` — Player and license models used for eligibility checks and rosters.\n- `sports_federation_rosters` — Season rosters and match sheet management.\n- `sports_federation_officiating` — Referee registry and assignment workflows.\n- `sports_federation_finance_bridge` — Lightweight finance events with source-linked,\n  idempotent hooks for registrations, result approval, sanctions, officiating,\n  and venue settlements.\n- `sports_federation_notifications` — Central email/activity dispatcher and\n    audit log for registration, publication, result, officiating, standings, and\n    finance workflow events.\n- `sports_federation_result_control` — Result submission, verification, approval, contest and correction flows.\n- `sports_federation_standings` — Standings computation, tie-break logic, and publishing controls.\n- `sports_federation_public_site` / `sports_federation_portal` — Website and portal layers for public pages and club self-service.\n\nInter-module rules\n\n- Use `depends` in `__manifest__.py` for compile-time coupling and prefer runtime loose coupling in service code.\n- Avoid importing models directly across modules in shared utils; reference them through the ORM (`env['federation.model']`).\n\nSecurity-group compatibility\n\n- Odoo 19 classifies application groups through `res.groups.privilege` records. Addons must assign a group with `privilege_id`; `category_id` belongs on the privilege and is no longer a valid field on `res.groups`.\n- Federation privileges should reference an existing module category such as `base.module_category_services` and remain in the addon security XML beside the groups they classify. This preserves the access-rights UI grouping without relying on the removed pre-Odoo-19 group field.\n\n## Data model conventions and patterns\n\n- Names: all domain models use the `federation.` prefix.\n- Fields: prefer explicit names (`home_score`, `away_score`, `match_date`, `venue_id`). Use `_id` for Many2one fields.\n- Sequences: centralize `ir.sequence` definitions under the modules that issue numbers (licenses, registrations, match references).\n- States: encode lifecycle using `state` selection fields. Implement transition methods (e.g., `action_confirm()`) that include invariant checks and post-transition side-effects (message_post, cron triggers).\n- Constraints and indexes: use `_sql_constraints` for DB-level uniqueness and `index=True` on frequently filtered fields.\n\nORM best practices\n\n- Use `@api.depends` for computed fields; mark heavy computed fields with `store=True` when the value is frequently filtered or sorted.\n- Use `read_group` for group-by aggregations instead of computing aggregates in Python loops.\n- When creating many records (e.g., fixtures for a large tournament), batch creations in transactions and avoid per-record flushes where possible.\n\n## Workflows and state machines\n\nThe canonical workflows live in `odoo/_workflows` (authoritative). Implementation notes below reflect the codebase expectations.\n\nTournament lifecycle\n\n- States: `draft → open → in_progress → closed | cancelled`.\n- Preconditions for `open`: participants registered/confirmed, ruleset assigned, optional venues configured.\n- Schedule creation typically moves the tournament to `in_progress` (explicit action required).\n- Archive and restore are explicit backend actions. Open or in-progress tournaments must be closed or cancelled before archiving, and only active draft tournaments linked to a season may be opened.\n\nMatch lifecycle and match-day operations\n\n- States: `draft → scheduled → in_progress → done | cancelled`.\n- Pre-match checks: both teams have confirmed match-sheets, required referee roles filled and confirmed, no suspensions on selected players, venue confirmed.\n- Officiating readiness is computed directly on the match from assignment state, rule-set referee counts, overdue confirmations, and referee certification validity so operators can filter or inspect staffing gaps without opening each assignment.\n- During match: record events (substitutions, cards) which feed the discipline and finance modules.\n\nResult pipeline\n\n- States: `not_submitted → submitted → verified → approved` (exceptions: `contested`, `corrected`).\n- Permissions: separate groups for submit/verify/approve to enforce audit and separation of duties.\n- Approved results are the only ones included in official standings computations.\n- The same user must not submit, verify, and approve the same result. Self-verification is blocked and approvers cannot approve their own submissions or the result they verified.\n- Approving, contesting, correcting, or resetting a result triggers automatic recomputation of linked non-frozen standings. Approved scores become immutable until the result is moved out of the approved state.\n\n## Competition engine — algorithms and wizards\n\nPrinciples\n\n- Determinism: given the same input (participant list, seeding, start datetime) the schedule generation must produce the same fixtures. Sort input participants by an unambiguous key (id or explicit seeding) before generation.\n- Testability: isolate algorithms in service classes and unit-test them with small deterministic datasets.\n\nRound-robin (circle method)\n\n- Supports odd/even participant counts (auto bye round for odd counts) and single/double round-robin.\n- Complexity: O(n^2) matches for n participants (n*(n-1)/2 for single round-robin).\n\nExample pseudocode (circle method)\n\n```python\ndef generate_round_robin(participants, double=False):\n    participants = sorted(participants, key=lambda p: p.seeding or p.id)\n    if len(participants) % 2 == 1:\n        participants.append(None)  # bye\n    n = len(participants)\n    rounds = []\n    for r in range(n - 1):\n        pairs = []\n        for i in range(n // 2):\n            a = participants[i]\n            b = participants[n - 1 - i]\n            if a is not None and b is not None:\n                pairs.append((a, b))\n        rounds.append(pairs)\n        participants = [participants[0]] + participants[-1:] + participants[1:-1]\n    if double:\n        return rounds + [reverse_pairs(r) for r in rounds]\n    return rounds\n```\n\nKnockout bracket generation\n\n- Seeding strategies: `natural` (order of participants) and `power_of_two` (map to nearest bracket size and set byes).\n- Ensure bracket seeding is deterministic and documented in the UI.\n\nWizards\n\n- Wizards (transient models under `wizards/`) do validations, produce a `summary` preview, and require explicit confirmation to persist matches. They must not perform destructive replacements unless the user explicitly enables `overwrite`.\n- Competition-generation wizards validate tournament state, the effective rule set, minimum participant counts, and stage/group ownership before creating matches. Overwrite mode is warning-first and should remain opt-in.\n\n## Controllers, portal, and public site patterns\n\nPortal patterns\n\n- Use a dedicated `federation.club.representative` model to map `res.users` → `federation.club` for portal ownership and record rules.\n- Controllers must perform ownership validation (`_get_clubs_for_user()`) before writes. Record rules are enforcement, controllers are defense-in-depth.\n- ORM-level ownership constraints should mirror controller checks for portal-created registrations so bypassing a controller does not widen access.\n- The tournament operations board (`/sports/tournament/<id>/operations`) extends these patterns with an Owl frontend. Portal access requires provable tournament-scoped activity (registration, participant, or visible match). Writes delegate to existing result-control action methods. The Owl app uses standalone `mount()` from `@odoo/owl`, not the backend webclient `mountComponent`, since it runs inside the website/portal frontend context. It mounts immediately so the board can render its own loading and error states, applies a 30-second timeout to the first payload fetch, and relies on a server-side payload that includes ranked action-queue rows, court summaries, next-step hints, and schedule labels so the browser stays presentation-focused.\n\nPublic site\n\n- Public controllers use `auth='public'` and `sudo()` for reads. Only expose non-sensitive fields (no emails/phones/notes) to public templates.\n- Enforce `website_published` and the relevant visibility toggle (`show_public_results`, `show_public_standings`) before serving direct public routes.\n- When a controller must deny a hidden portal or public route with 404, raise the HTTP exception (`raise request.not_found()`) instead of returning it, so fail-closed paths stay quiet in logs and match Odoo's expected flow.\n- Render public rich text through sanitized website field rendering rather than raw `t-raw` output.\n- Keep `public_slug` unique even while the public routes remain model-bound, so publication metadata and future external references cannot collide.\n\nCSRF and forms\n\n- All POST forms must include `csrf_token` and controllers must validate it.\n\n## Security model and record rules\n\nKey principles\n\n- Least privilege: create narrowly-scoped groups and map CRUD rights in `security/ir.model.access.csv`.\n- Record rules: express row-level ownership using domains (e.g., `('club_id','in', user.representative_ids.mapped('club_id').ids)`).\n- Avoid uncontrolled `sudo()` on write operations.\n\nGroups and separation of duties\n\n- Federation Staff (submit results)\n- Result Verifier (verify submitted results)\n- Result Approver (approve verified results)\n- Referee Coordinator (assign referees)\n- Portal Club Representative (portal users)\n\n## Performance, scaling and operational concerns\n\nLarge tournaments and match volumes\n\n- Match generation: create matches in batches using `create()` on list-of-dicts to minimize ORM overhead. Consider raw SQL insert for extremely large volumes but keep referential integrity and Odoo cache considerations in mind.\n- Indexes: ensure `tournament_id`, `stage_id`, `group_id`, `match_date`, and `state` fields are indexed.\n- Aggregation: compute standings incrementally or via nightly cron for large datasets. Prefer `read_group` for real-time small aggregate queries.\n\nBackground and asynchronous work\n\n- Use `ir.cron` for scheduled recomputes. For heavy parallel work consider `queue_job` or an external worker queue.\n\nMemory and worker tuning\n\n- For large batch jobs run them on a dedicated worker with increased memory limits and tuned `limit_time_cpu` and `limit_time_real` values.\n\n## Testing, CI and quality gates\n\nTest types\n\n- Unit tests: service classes and algorithms (no DB or minimal mock DB). Keep these fast and deterministic.\n- Integration tests: Odoo testcases exercising ORM-level behaviour and workflows.\n- Functional tests: simulate portal and public flows (controller-level) when needed.\n\nCI recommendations\n\n- Run module tests in CI and fail PRs on test regressions.\n- Include a lint step (flake8/black for Python where applicable) and XML/manifest validation.\n- The repository CI entrypoint is `ci/run_tests.sh`; the GitHub workflow at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` reuses that script and runs Black/Flake8 from `requirements.txt`.\n- `ci/run_tests.sh` also provides named suites (`competition_core`, `portal_public_ops`, `finance_reporting`) so maintainers can run the same focused coverage locally and in GitHub Actions.\n- The runner supports a frontend-only mode (`--frontend-module`) that performs XML/QWeb parsing, JavaScript syntax and QUnit-registration checks, asset checks, portal accessibility/mobile checks, and selected HTTP tests without scheduling or standings suites.\n- `--affected-from <ref> --include-dependents` resolves changed addons from git and expands their manifest reverse-dependency closure before testing.\n- Each run retains `test_failures.log`, `expected_diagnostics.log`, `infrastructure.log`, and `full.log`; `--keep-on-failure` additionally preserves runtime artifacts and writes exact inspection commands.\n- Public-site, portal, and reporting performance hotspots should carry explicit `assertQueryCount(...)` budgets in their regression suites; the current enforced budgets are summarized in `TESTING_GUIDE.md`.\n- Do not commit runtime credentials. Keep local CI values in `ci/.env`, commit only `ci/.env.example`, and let CI generate ephemeral values at runtime.\n- Integration environment variables: maintain `ci/integrations.env.example` with the common external-integration keys (SMTP, SendGrid/Mailgun keys, OAuth client IDs/secrets, Slack webhook, Twilio credentials, AWS S3 keys). Keep real values out of VCS and populate `ci/.env` locally or via your secret store in CI runs.\n- Contributor-facing local setup, suite selection, and script validation commands live in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nExample test command\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n```\n\n## Upgrade, migrations and deployment notes\n\nManifest and data maintenance\n\n- Keep `__manifest__.py` `version` and `data` accurate. Prefer small, focused upgrade scripts to large one-off DB migrations.\n- For breaking model changes provide a dedicated migration script (`openupgrade` style) and document steps.\n- `ci/check_migration_review.py` should pass whenever model, view, or controller ownership changes are present. Treat a passing run as evidence that migration scripts or release-note surfaces were updated in the same change set.\n- Migration-sensitive branches must record dry-run evidence and rollback notes in `RELEASE_RUNBOOK.md`.\n- `ci/check_constraint_index_contracts.py` validates curated constraint/index contracts for major workflow models. Keep `ci/contracts/constraint_index_contracts.json` aligned when those models evolve.\n- `ci/check_openapi_contracts.py` validates managed integration and public-feed OpenAPI contracts plus required golden examples (`openapi/examples/INTEGRATION_GOLDEN_EXAMPLES.md`).\n- Standings recompute now supports asynchronous, idempotent queue execution through `federation.standing.recompute.job`; use correlation IDs (`federation_correlation_id`) when invoking queue workers or replaying failed jobs.\n- Integration API, scheduled reporting crons, and notification flows propagate correlation IDs for cross-module incident tracing.\n- Keep `ROADMAP.md` and `RELEASE_RUNBOOK.md` on the same active `Release train:` value so roadmap commitments, upgrade handling, and operator checklists stay synchronized.\n\nPre/post hooks\n\n- Use `pre_init_hook` and `post_init_hook` (registered in `__manifest__`) for data transformations where required. Keep hooks idempotent and well-tested.\n\nBackups and rollback\n\n- Always perform full DB and filestore backups prior to upgrades. Test restore paths in your staging environment.\n\n## Developer workflow: add/modify checklist\n\nArchitecture decisions\n\n- Repository-level architectural choices that cut across portal trust\n    boundaries, reporting SQL views, or public route ownership live in `adr/`.\n- Update the relevant ADR in the same change set when one of those core\n    decisions materially changes.\n\nWhen introducing a new feature follow this minimal patch checklist:\n\n1. Add model code: `models/<file>.py`. Export in `models/__init__.py`.\n2. Add `security/ir.model.access.csv` and any `security/*.xml` record rules.\n3. Keep `STATE_AND_OWNERSHIP_MATRIX.md` aligned with any lifecycle or portal-ownership change.\n\nPR checklist (required)\n\n- Tests included and passing\n- `security/ir.model.access.csv` updated\n- `__manifest__.py` updated (if needed)\n- Documentation/README updated\n- Small, focused commits and descriptive PR message\n\n## Examples and reference snippets\n\nWizard skeleton (python)\n\n```python\nclass FederationRoundRobinWizard(models.TransientModel):\n    _name = 'federation.round.robin.wizard'\n    _description = 'Round Robin Schedule Wizard'\n\n    tournament_id = fields.Many2one('federation.tournament', required=True)\n    use_all_participants = fields.Boolean(default=True)\n    summary = fields.Text(compute='_compute_summary')\n\n    def action_generate(self):\n        service = RoundRobinService(self.tournament_id)\n        schedule = service.generate()\n        # create matches in batches\n        match_vals = []\n        for round in schedule:\n            for a, b in round:\n                match_vals.append({\n                    'tournament_id': self.tournament_id.id,\n                    'home_team_id': a.id,\n                    'away_team_id': b.id,\n                    'state': 'scheduled',\n                })\n        self.env['federation.match'].create(match_vals)\n\n```\n\nSQL constraints example (in model):\n\n```python\n_sql_constraints = [\n    ('unique_match_participants', 'UNIQUE(tournament_id, home_team_id, away_team_id, match_date)', 'Duplicate match')\n]\n```\n\n## Observability and logging\n\n- Use named loggers: `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` and log at appropriate levels (INFO for normal milestones, WARNING for recoverable issues, ERROR for exceptions).\n- Use `message_post` on records for an audit trail of user-driven state changes.\n\n## Security reminders\n\n- Avoid using `sudo()` to bypass authorization for write operations. -{"content": "# Testing Guide\n\nLast updated: 2026-09-02\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\n\nThis guide explains the project's test taxonomy, how to write tests for each\ncategory, and how to keep query-budget assertions current.\n\nPerformance budgets and explain snapshots are maintained here with the test\npatterns below. A query-count increase is a regression unless the test and the\nbudget are updated together with a reason.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Test Taxonomy\n\nThe project uses three test classes depending on what is being tested:\n\n### `TransactionCase` — ORM-level unit and integration tests\n\nUsed for: model methods, computed fields, `@api.constrains` validators,\nwizards, services, and controller methods that are tested by injecting a mock\n\nEach test runs inside a savepoint that is rolled back after the test, so data\n\nfrom odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase\n\n\n    @classmethod\n    def setUpClass(cls):\n        super().setUpClass()\n        cls.club = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create({\n            \"name\": \"Test Club\",\n            \"code\": \"TC01\",\n        })\n\n    def test_code_must_be_unique(self):\n        with self.assertRaises(Exception):\n            self.env[\"federation.club\"].create({\"name\": \"Dup\", \"code\": \"TC01\"})\n            self.env.cr.flush()\n```\n\n**Put shared fixtures in `setUpClass`.** Fixtures created there are shared\nacross all test methods (and rolled back as a unit at the end of the class).\nFixtures created inside individual test methods are rolled back after each\nmethod.\n### `HttpCase` — end-to-end HTTP smoke tests\n\nUsed for: verifying that routes return the expected HTTP status code, CSRF\ntoken handling, portal login flows.\n\nRequires a real database and a running Odoo HTTP server. These tests must be\ntagged `@tagged(\"-at_install\", \"post_install\")` so they run after all modules\nare loaded.\n\n```python\nfrom odoo.tests.common import HttpCase, tagged\n\n@tagged(\"-at_install\", \"post_install\")\nclass TestPublicSiteHttpSmoke(HttpCase):\n    def test_tournaments_list_returns_200(self):\n        response = self.url_open(\"/tournaments\")\n        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)\n```\n\nHTTP tests are significantly slower than `TransactionCase` tests and require\n`sports_federation_portal` to be installed. Use the\n`unittest.SkipTest` pattern to skip gracefully when optional modules are absent:\n\n```python\n@classmethod\ndef setUpClass(cls):\n    super().setUpClass()\n    with cls.registry.cursor() as cr:\n        env = api.Environment(cr, SUPERUSER_ID, {})\n        if not env.ref(\"sports_federation_portal.group_federation_portal_club\",\n                       raise_if_not_found=False):\n            raise unittest.SkipTest(\"sports_federation_portal not installed\")\n```\n\n### `TransactionCase` with a mock `request` — controller unit tests\n\nUsed for: testing controller methods that call `request.env` without running an\nHTTP server. Inject a `SimpleNamespace` as the request stub and patch the\n`request` module attribute.\n\n```python\nfrom types import SimpleNamespace\nfrom unittest.mock import patch\n\nclass TestCompetitionsApiJson(TransactionCase):\n\n    def test_rate_limit_blocks_after_limit(self):\n        request_stub = SimpleNamespace(\n            env=self.env,\n            httprequest=SimpleNamespace(remote_addr=\"198.51.100.1\", headers={}),\n        )\n        controller = PublicTournamentHubController()\n        with patch(\n            \"odoo.addons.sports_federation_public_site\"\n            \".controllers.public_competitions.request\",\n            request_stub,\n        ):\n            result = controller.competitions_api_json()\n        self.assertIn(\"tournaments\", result)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 2. This pattern is used\nthroughout `sports_federation_portal/tests/`.\n\n```python\nfrom odoo import SUPERUSER_ID, api\nfrom odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase\n\nclass TestPortalOwnership(TransactionCase):\n\n    @classmethod\n    def setUpClass(cls):\n        super().setUpClass()\n        cls.portal_group = cls.env.ref(\n            \"sports_federation_portal.group_federation_portal_club\"\n        )\n        cls.club_a = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create(\n            {\"name\": \"Portal Club A\", \"code\": \"PCA\"}\n        )\n        cls.club_b = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create(\n            {\"name\": \"Portal Club B\", \"code\": \"PCB\"}\n        )\n\n        def _make_user(name, login):\n                cls.env[\"res.users\"]\n                .with_context(no_reset_password=True)\n                .create({\n                    \"login\": login,\n            )\n        cls.user_a = _make_user(\"User A\", \"usera@example.com\")\n\n\n## Maintained performance budgets\n\nThese are the current CI budgets for the most sensitive read paths:\n\n| Path | Budget |\n|---|---:|\n| `federation.tournament.get_public_featured_tournaments(limit=4)` | 1 query |\n| `federation.tournament.get_public_live_tournaments(limit=4)` | 1 query |\n| `federation.tournament.get_public_recent_result_tournaments(limit=4)` | 3 queries |\n| `federation.tournament.get_public_schedule_sections()` | 4 queries |\n| `federation.team.roster.line._portal_get_available_players()` | 7 queries |\n| `federation.report.schedule._build_season_portfolio_rows()` | 3 queries |\n| `federation.report.schedule._build_club_performance_rows()` | 4 queries |\n| `federation.report.snapshot._compliance_pending_total()` | 1 aggregate query |\n| scheduling validation smoke | ≤ 25 seconds |\n\nThe authoritative tests are in the competition, public-site, portal,\nreporting, and domain test suites. limit is 1 in this test\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Query-Count Budgets\n\nSeveral test suites assert exact query counts to catch N+1 regressions:\n\n```python\ndef test_public_discovery_helpers_stay_within_query_budget(self):\n    with self.assertQueryCount(1):\n        featured = self.env[\"federation.tournament\"].get_public_featured_tournaments(limit=4)\n    with self.assertQueryCount(3):\n        recent = self.env[\"federation.tournament\"].get_public_recent_result_tournaments(limit=4)\n```\n\n**Rules:**\n- `assertQueryCount(N)` fails if the block executes more or fewer than `N`\n  queries. Fewer queries is also a failure because it may indicate a test\n  regression (e.g., empty dataset masking missing queries).\n- Budgets live in the maintained performance section of this guide. If you\n    lower a budget, update that section.\n- If your change legitimately increases a query count, update the assertion\n    and add a comment explaining why, and update the budget table in this guide.\n\n---\n\n## 4. EXPLAIN Snapshot Tests\n\nFor critical query paths, the CI runs `ci/check_explain_snapshots.py`, which\ncompares `EXPLAIN` output against stored snapshots in `ci/explain_snapshots/`.\n\nTo add a new snapshot:\n\n```bash\n# Connect to the CI database and run EXPLAIN\ndocker compose exec db psql -U odoo -d odoo_ci_test -c \\\n  \"EXPLAIN SELECT ... FROM federation_tournament WHERE ...\"\n# Save the output to ci/explain_snapshots/<descriptive_name>.txt\n```\n\nA snapshot regression (e.g., a sequential scan replacing an index scan) fails\nCI. Review the output, add the necessary index, or update the snapshot with\na comment explaining the regression is acceptable.\n\n---\n\n## 5. What to Test for Each Change Type\n\n| Change type | Required test |\n|---|---|\n| New model field | `test_<model>_<field>_<rule>` validating the constraint or default |\n| New `@api.constrains` | One passing case + one failing case |\n| New computed field | Verify the value before and after the triggering field changes |\n| New wizard | End-to-end test: create input records → call wizard → assert output records (counts, states) |\n| New controller route | Either an HTTP smoke test (200/404) or a mock-request unit test |\n| Portal write | Always add a cross-club access-denial test in addition to the happy path |\n| Standings / schedule logic | `assertQueryCount` + correctness assertion for a minimal dataset |\n| Rate limiting | Frozen-time test: N requests pass, N+1 is blocked; verify `Retry-After` header |\n\n---\n\n## 6. Running Tests in CI\n\n```bash\n# Run the suite that covers your changed module\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n\n# Run just one module (faster when iterating)\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_standings\n\n# Run participant readiness discovery guard (fails if post-tests are not discovered)\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --suite rosters_readiness_guard\n\n# Equivalent explicit form when you need direct control\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_rosters --test-tags sf_rosters_participant_readiness --require-post-tests 1\n\n# Skip browser bootstrap when the run has no HttpCase/browser coverage\nCI_SKIP_BROWSER_BOOTSTRAP=1 bash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n\n# Frontend-only feedback loop: portal accessibility/mobile templates and\n# selected HTTP rendering tests\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --frontend-module sports_federation_portal\n\n# Detect changed addons and expand to all manifest reverse dependents\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --affected-from origin/main --include-dependents\n\n# Retain failed containers, database, filestore, generated config, and commands\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_portal --keep-on-failure\n\n# Run all suites (used in final PR validation)\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh\n```\n\nThe CI runner produces a results block at the end:\n\n```\n\nEvery run also writes `test_failures.log`, `expected_diagnostics.log`,\n`infrastructure.log`, and `full.log` under `ci/logs/<timestamp>/`. A failed\n`--keep-on-failure` run writes `retained-container-commands.sh` with exact\ninspection and cleanup commands; successful runs clean up automatically.\n════════════════════════════════\n  RESULTS\n════════════════════════════════\n  Exit code:     0\n  Tests run:     62\n  Tests passed:  62\n  Tests failed:  0\n  Test errors:   0\n════════════════════════════════\n```\n\nA non-zero exit code means the CI gate failed. Check the container logs for\nthe failing test name and traceback:\n\n```bash\ndocker logs <container-name> 2>&1 | grep -A 20 \"FAIL\\|ERROR\"\n```\n\n### Discovery-safe tag convention\n\nFor high-risk regression suites, add an explicit class-level tag in addition to the usual install timing tags:\n\n```python\nfrom odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase, tagged\n\n@tagged(\"-at_install\", \"post_install\", \"sf_<module>_<feature>\")\nclass TestFeature(TransactionCase):\n    ...\n```\n\nUse lowercase snake-case tags prefixed with `sf_` (example: `sf_rosters_participant_readiness`).\nThis enables deterministic CI selection and allows `--require-post-tests` gating to detect discovery regressions early.\n\n### Critical suite registry\n\nThe CI runner enforces a minimum discovered post-test count for critical suites.\nThis prevents false-green runs where discovery is broken and no tests execute.\n\nGitHub Actions now also runs a dedicated integration matrix lane for\n`people_rosters_rules` and `ops_and_notifications` so cross-module behavior is\nvalidated on every push and pull request.\n\n| Suite | Default minimum post-tests | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `competition_core` | 1 | Core workflow sanity gate |\n| `portal_public_ops` | 1 | Portal/public ownership and route guard |\n| `finance_reporting` | 1 | Finance and reporting guard |\n| `release_surfaces` | 1 | Broad release surface guard |\n| `people_rosters_rules` | 1 | Domain rules and roster workflow guard |\n| `ops_and_notifications` | 1 | Operations and notification guard |\n| `rosters_readiness_guard` | 1 | Explicit tag `sf_rosters_participant_readiness` |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Test File Conventions\n\n- One test file per logical area in `tests/` (e.g., `test_round_robin.py`,\n  `test_knockout.py` — not one giant `test_all.py`).\n- File names: `test_<noun>.py` (noun = model name, workflow name, or feature).\n- Class name: `Test<Topic>` (e.g., `TestRoundRobin`, `TestPortalOwnershipGuard`).\n- `setUpClass` creates shared fixtures; individual test methods create only what\n  they uniquely need.\n- Test method names: `test_<what>_<expected_outcome>` (e.g.,\n  `test_duplicate_code_raises_validation_error`).\n- Register new test files in `tests/__init__.py` with `from . import test_myfile`.\n\n\n## Release performance qualification\n\nThe release-candidate pipeline runs the maintained query-budget lane after the core, portal, and public qualification lanes:\n\n```bash\nscripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh performance\n```\n\nThe versioned registry is `ci/performance_budgets.json`. The contract checker verifies the exact targeted test classes, preventing a renamed class from silently turning the lane into an empty run. Budget increases require measured evidence in `RELEASE_RUNBOOK.md`. Synthetic data must be identified as synthetic.\n\n## Release baseline qualification\n\nAfter committing the candidate and confirming that no tracked changes remain,\nrun the complete baseline gate:\n\n```bash\nscripts/ci/run_release_baseline.sh\n```\n\nThis wraps the authoritative RC lanes and records lane evidence under\n`artifacts/release/baseline/`. A lane failure records failed evidence before the\nscript exits. Do not use this wrapper to hide or bypass individual RC failures.\n\n\n## Migration and rollback qualification\n\nThe release migration rehearsal uses versioned invariants from\n`ci/release_invariants.json` and runs role-separated acceptance against the\nupgraded database:\n\n```bash\nscripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh acceptance\nscripts/ci/run_migration_rehearsal.sh --help\n```\n\nKeep invariant names stable once evidence has been archived. Add a count or\nintegrity check when a new release-critical ownership boundary is introduced.\nDo not remove a check merely to accommodate unexplained migration drift.\n", "content_length": 16581, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "TESTING_GUIDE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "f19f72a77426acf51c85ded083584d836afb23af798cf9723b997648a5d51c2e", "size_bytes": 16787}
-{"content": "# Troubleshooting Guide\n\nLast updated: 2026-05-18\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nReview cadence: Every release train\n\nThis guide documents known issues, their root causes, and the recommended\nrecovery steps. Always check this file before escalating to a developer.\n\n---\n\n## Quick Diagnostic Checklist\n\nBefore diving into a specific symptom, run these checks first:\n\n```bash\n# 1. All containers running?\ndocker compose ps\n\n# 2. Any Python errors in the Odoo log?\ndocker compose logs odoo 2>&1 | grep -i \"error\\|traceback\\|exception\" | tail -20\n\n# 3. PostgreSQL accepting connections?\ndocker compose exec db pg_isready -U odoo\n\n# 4. Scheduled actions healthy?\n# Check in the back office: Settings → Technical → Automation → Scheduled Actions\n# Look for any action where \"Last Execution\" shows a failure icon.\n```\n\n---\n\n## Symptom Index\n\n| Symptom | Section |\n|---|---|\n| Match form crashes with `UndefinedColumn` | [§1](#1-match-form-crashes-with-undefinedcolumn) |\n| Standings not recomputing after result approval | [§2](#2-standings-not-recomputing-after-result-approval) |\n| Notifications not sending | [§3](#3-notifications-not-sending) |\n| Import wizard dry-run always fails | [§4](#4-import-wizard-dry-run-always-fails) |\n| Rate limit buckets never cleared | [§5](#5-rate-limit-buckets-never-cleared) |\n| CI container fails to start PostgreSQL | [§6](#6-ci-container-fails-to-start-postgresql) |\n| Portal page shows 403 / `AccessError` | [§7](#7-portal-page-shows-403--accesserror) |\n| Public JSON feed returns `500` | [§8](#8-public-json-feed-returns-500) |\n| Player shows `is_eligible = False` after license activation | [§9](#9-player-shows-is_eligible--false-after-license-activation) |\n| Finance events not exporting to partner | [§10](#10-finance-events-not-exporting-to-partner) |\n| Reporting schedule stuck in `running` | [§11](#11-reporting-schedule-stuck-in-running) |\n| Roster assignment_ready False with no clear reason | [§12](#12-roster-assignment_ready-false-with-no-clear-reason) |\n\n---\n\n## 1. Match Form Crashes with `UndefinedColumn`\n\n**Symptom**: Opening or saving a match record raises a `ProgrammingError:\ncolumn \"xyz\" of relation \"federation_match\" does not exist`.\n\n**Cause**: A `store=True` computed field was added to the match model in a\nnew release but the database column was never created because the module was\nnot upgraded after the code change.\n\n**Fix**:\n\n```bash\n# Upgrade the affected module(s) to create the missing column\ndocker compose exec odoo odoo \\\n  -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf \\\n  -d odoo \\\n  -u sports_federation_tournament,sports_federation_result_control \\\n  --stop-after-init\ndocker compose restart odoo\n```\n\n**Prevention**: always run `upgrade_sports_federation.sh` (or `-u <module>`)\nafter pulling code that adds or changes stored computed fields. A missing\ncolumn never appears in `--test-enable` output but will crash the live form.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Standings Not Recomputing After Result Approval\n\n**Symptom**: A result is approved (`result_state = approved`,\n`include_in_official_standings = True`) but the standings table is unchanged.\n\n**Cause A**: The standings record for the affected tournament/stage/group is\nin `frozen` state. Frozen standings are never recomputed automatically.\n\n**Fix A**:\n\n1. Open **Federation → Standings** and locate the relevant standings record.\n2. Verify `state = frozen`.\n3. Click **Unfreeze** (requires Federation Manager group).\n4. Click **Recompute**.\n5. Verify the standings are correct, then re-freeze.\n\n**Cause B**: The `@api.depends` chain on the standings recompute trigger is\nmissing the field that changed.\n\n**Fix B**:\n\n1. Check which field on `federation.match` changed (e.g. `home_score`).\n2. Verify it appears in the `@api.depends` decorator on\n   `_trigger_recompute` or the equivalent compute method in\n   `sports_federation_standings/models/federation_standings.py`.\n3. If missing, add the field to the depends list and upgrade the module.\n\n**Cause C**: The automatic trigger code path was skipped because the result\nwas approved via a raw ORM write (`record.write({\"result_state\": \"approved\"})`)\ninstead of the `action_approve_result()` method. This can happen during\nbulk imports.\n\n**Fix C**: Trigger a manual recompute from the standings form.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Notifications Not Sending\n\n**Symptom**: Expected emails (result approval, roster confirmation, referee\nassignment) are not delivered.\n\n**Cause A**: SMTP server is not configured or is misconfigured.\n\n**Fix A**:\n1. Open **Settings → Technical → Email → Outgoing Mail Servers**.\n2. Verify the server entry exists and is active.\n3. Click **Test Connection**. If it fails, correct the host, port, and\n   credentials.\n4. Check `docker compose logs odoo | grep -i smtp` for connection errors.\n\n**Cause B**: `sports_federation_notifications` module is not installed.\n\n**Fix B**:\n```bash\ndocker compose exec odoo odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo \\\n  -i sports_federation_notifications --stop-after-init\n```\n\n**Cause C**: The notification dispatcher scheduled action is disabled.\n\n**Fix C**:\n1. Open **Settings → Technical → Automation → Scheduled Actions**.\n2. Find the federation notification scan action.\n3. Click **Run Manually** to test, then re-enable if it was disabled.\n\n**Cause D**: The email ends up in the mail queue but is not sent because the\nqueue runner is not processing.\n\n**Fix D**:\n```bash\n# Force the mail queue to flush\ndocker compose exec odoo odoo \\\n  -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo \\\n  --load=base,mail --stop-after-init \\\n  -e \"self.env['mail.mail'].process_email_queue()\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. Import Wizard Dry-Run Always Fails\n\n**Symptom**: Running a dry-run in **Federation → Import Tools → Import Wizard**\nraises a duplicate key or unique constraint error on every attempt, even for\na fresh payload.\n\n**Cause**: Stale rows in the staging table (`federation.import.staged.delivery`\nor the module-specific staging model) from a previous failed import still\noccupy the unique key slot.\n\n**Fix**:\n1. Open **Federation → Import Tools → Inbound Deliveries**.\n2. Filter for `state = staged` deliveries from the failing batch.\n3. Archive or delete the stale staged rows.\n\nAlternatively, trigger the cleanup scheduled action:\n1. Open **Settings → Technical → Automation → Scheduled Actions**.\n2. Run **Federation: GC Staged Deliveries** manually.\n\n**Prevention**: the GC scheduled action runs daily. If it is disabled (see §5),\nstale rows accumulate quickly.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Rate Limit Buckets Never Cleared\n\n**Symptom**: The `federation.request.rate.limit` table grows unboundedly.\nPublic API calls succeed less frequently than expected even from legitimate\ncallers whose rate-limit window has expired.\n\n**Cause**: The `Federation: GC Rate Limit Buckets` scheduled action is\ndisabled.\n\n**Fix**:\n1. Open **Settings → Technical → Automation → Scheduled Actions**.\n2. Find **Federation: GC Rate Limit Buckets**.\n3. Set **Active** = True and **Interval** to 1 Hour (the default).\n4. Click **Run Manually** to clear the backlog immediately.\n\n**Verify** bucket cleanup is working:\n```bash\ndocker compose exec -T db psql -U odoo -d odoo \\\n  -c \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM federation_request_rate_limit;\"\n# Should decrease after the GC action runs\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. CI Container Fails to Start PostgreSQL\n\n**Symptom**: Running `bash addons/ci/run_tests.sh` fails immediately with\na PostgreSQL startup error: `address already in use` or `port 5432 already\nin use`.\n\n**Cause**: The development Docker Compose stack is already running and its\n`db` service occupies port 5432 (if the CI uses host networking) or the same\nDocker network.\n\n**Fix**:\n\n```bash\n# Option A: stop the dev stack before running CI\ndocker compose down\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n\n# Option B: use a different network (check ci/run_tests.sh --help for options)\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core --network ci_net\n```\n\nAfter CI completes, restart the dev stack:\n```bash\ndocker compose up -d\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. Portal Page Shows 403 / `AccessError`\n\n**Symptom**: A portal user navigates to a federation portal page and receives\na 403 error or an `AccessError` in the logs.\n\n**Cause A**: The user's `res.users` record is not linked to a\n`federation.club.representative` record for the club that owns the resource.\n\n**Fix A**:\n1. Open **Federation → Portal → Club Representatives**.\n2. Verify a record exists for the user and the correct club.\n3. If missing, create it (see [WORKFLOW_CLUB_ONBOARDING.md](\n   _workflows/WORKFLOW_CLUB_ONBOARDING.md)).\n\n**Cause B**: The portal record rule for the affected model uses the wrong\ndomain expression (developer error introduced by a recent change).\n\n**Fix B**:\n1. Check **Settings → Technical → Security → Record Rules** for rules on the\n   affected model.\n2. Verify the domain matches the expected club-scoping pattern\n   (`club_id.representative_ids.user_id`, etc.).\n\n---\n\n## 8. Public JSON Feed Returns `500`\n\n**Symptom**: `GET /competitions/api/json` returns HTTP 500 instead of JSON.\n\n**Cause A**: A new required computed field on `federation.tournament` throws\nan exception when the tournament has incomplete data.\n\n**Fix A**: Check the Odoo log for the traceback:\n```bash\ndocker compose logs odoo 2>&1 | grep -A 30 \"competitions/api/json\"\n```\nFix the underlying data or guard the computed field with a `try/except`.\n\n**Cause B**: The rate-limit table has a corrupt bucket (e.g. `hit_count < 0`).\n\n**Fix B**:\n```bash\ndocker compose exec -T db psql -U odoo -d odoo \\\n  -c \"DELETE FROM federation_request_rate_limit WHERE hit_count < 0;\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 9. Player Shows `is_eligible = False` After License Activation\n\n**Symptom**: A license is set to `state = active` but the player's\n`is_eligible` computed field remains `False`.\n\n**Cause A**: Odoo's compute cache is stale. This can happen after a direct\ndatabase write (e.g. during a migration or import) that bypasses the ORM.\n\n**Fix A**:\n```bash\n# Force recompute of is_eligible for all players\ndocker compose exec odoo odoo shell -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo <<'EOF'\nenv['federation.player'].search([])._compute_is_eligible()\nenv.cr.commit()\nEOF\n```\n\n**Cause B**: The player also has an active suspension sanction in\n`sports_federation_discipline`. Suspension overrides the license-active state.\n\n**Fix B**: Check **Federation → Discipline → Sanctions** for an active\nsuspension for the player. If the suspension is resolved, run the\nreinstatement action (see [WORKFLOW_PLAYER_LICENSE.md](\n_workflows/WORKFLOW_PLAYER_LICENSE.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 10. Finance Events Not Exporting to Partner\n\n**Symptom**: A partner calls `GET /integration/v1/finance-events` and\nreceives an empty list even though events exist in the system.\n\n**Cause A**: Events are still in `draft` state. The integration export endpoint\nreturns only `confirmed` or `exported` events.\n\n**Fix A**: Federation finance staff must confirm the pending events:\n**Federation → Finance → Finance Events → filter `state = draft` → Confirm**.\n\n**Cause B**: The partner's `X-Federation-Partner-Code` header does not match\nthe code stored on the `federation.integration.partner` record.\n\n**Fix B**: Verify the partner code with the administrator. The export route\nreturns `access_denied` (not an empty list) for authentication failures.\nIf the response is an empty list with status 200, the authentication succeeded\nbut no confirmed events match the filter.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Reporting Schedule Stuck in `running`\n\n**Symptom**: A report schedule shows `state = running` indefinitely; no report\nis generated and no error is visible.\n\n**Cause**: The Odoo worker that started the report generation crashed (e.g.\nOOM kill, container restart) mid-execution, leaving the state flag uncleared.\n\n**Fix**:\n1. Open **Federation → Reporting → Report Schedules**.\n2. Set the stuck schedule back to `draft` or `ready` via the developer mode\n   form editor, or use:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose exec odoo odoo shell -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo <<'EOF'\nenv['federation.report.schedule'].search([('state','=','running')])\\\n  .write({'state': 'ready'})\nenv.cr.commit()\nEOF\n```\n\n3. Trigger the schedule manually to confirm it completes.\n\n**Prevention**: monitor the **Reporting → Report Schedules** list after every\ncontainer restart.\n\n---\n\n## 12. Roster `assignment_ready` False with No Clear Reason\n\n**Symptom**: A roster line shows `assignment_ready = False` but the\n`readiness_feedback` field is empty or unhelpful.\n\n**Cause**: The eligibility service (`federation.eligibility.service`) failed\nsilently or the `readiness_feedback` compute method has a gap for a new\nblocking condition that was added without a corresponding feedback string.\n\n**Fix**:\n1. If this is a new condition that lacks feedback, add the missing feedback\n   string in `sports_federation_rosters/models/roster_line.py` →\n   `_compute_readiness_feedback`.\n\n---\n\n## Getting Further Help\n\nIf none of the above applies:\n\n1.
