sanctions |\n| `sports_federation_venues` | Venue booking passthroughs |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.fee.type`\n\nA catalogue of fee categories.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Fee type name |\n| `code` | Char | Unique code |\n| `category` | Selection | registration / fine / reimbursement / other |\n| `default_amount` / `currency_id` | Monetary | Default amount |\n| `active` | Boolean | In use |\n| `notes` | Text | Description |\n\n### `federation.finance.event`\n\nAn individual financial occurrence.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Event title |\n| `fee_type_id` | Many2one | Fee category |\n| `event_type` | Selection | Type classification |\n| `amount` / `currency_id` | Monetary | Actual amount |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / confirmed / settled / cancelled |\n| `source_model` / `source_res_id` | Char / Integer | Origin record |\n| `season_id` | Many2one | Resolved season scope for planning and reporting |\n| `partner_id` | Many2one | Related partner |\n| `club_id` / `player_id` / `referee_id` | Many2one | Federation entity |\n| `invoice_ref` / `external_ref` | Char | External references |\n| `handoff_state` | Selection | pending_export / exported / reconciled / closed |\n| `accounting_batch_ref` / `reconciliation_ref` | Char | Accounting handoff references |\n| `notes` | Text | Details |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → confirmed → settled / cancelled.\n- **Handoff state machine**: pending_export → exported → reconciled → closed.\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Source traceability** — Every finance event links back to its originating record\n   (registration, sanction, assignment) via model/res_id.\n2. **Fee catalogue** — Standardised fee types with default amounts.\n3. **Accounting-ready** — `invoice_ref` and `external_ref` keep the bridge ready\n   for future accounting integration while the current lightweight workflow ends\n   in `settled`.\n4. **Idempotent automation** — source-driven helpers reuse or reactivate matching\n  draft finance events instead of duplicating them on workflow re-entry.\n5. **Multi-entity** — Covers clubs, players, and referees.\n6. **Accounting handoff governance** — finance events now track export,\n   reconciliation, and closure checkpoints for downstream accounting workflows.\n7. **Season intelligence support** — finance events infer a season scope from\n  their source record whenever possible so reporting and budget views can roll\n  up actuals without duplicate data entry.\n8. **Operator-safe batch invoicing** — list-view \"Create Invoices\" now reports\n  per-event failures instead of silently skipping exceptions, so reconciliation\n  issues are visible immediately.\n\n### `federation.season.budget`\n\nPlanning baseline per season and fee type.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `season_id` / `fee_type_id` | Many2one | Budget scope |\n| `budget_amount` | Monetary | Planned amount |\n| `actual_amount` | Monetary | Confirmed and settled actuals for the same scope |\n| `actual_event_count` | Integer | Count of matching actual finance events |\n| `variance_amount` / `variance_pct` | Monetary / Float | Planned vs actual variance |\n| `notes` | Text | Budget commentary |\n\nThe backend exposes season budgets under Federation > Finance and provides a\nstat button that opens the scoped finance events behind the variance figures.\n\n## Accounting Handoff Contract\n\nThe finance bridge now supports an explicit accounting handoff workflow:\n\n- `action_mark_exported()` marks confirmed or settled events as exported\n- `action_mark_reconciled()` requires settlement and an exported handoff state\n- `action_close_handoff()` closes only reconciled, settled events\n\nDetailed handoff CSV contract:\n\n- route: `/reporting/export/finance/events`\n- contract id: `finance_event_v1`\n- includes schema version, handoff state, accounting batch reference,\n  reconciliation reference, source traceability, and execution timestamps\n\n## Season Registration Finance Hooks\n\nThe finance bridge now auto-creates a finance event when a\n`federation.season.registration` record moves into `confirmed`.\n\n- Default fee type code: `season_registration`\n- Creation mode: idempotent; reconfirming a registration reuses the same source\n  record and does not create duplicates\n- Source traceability: events use `source_model = federation.season.registration`\n  and `source_res_id = <registration id>`\n- Reconciliation support: auto-created events also receive a deterministic\n  `external_ref` using the fee-type code and source record identity\n\n## Result Approval Finance Hooks (Rules)\n\nmatch_result_hooks.py extends `federation.match` with:\n\n- **`result_fee_type_id`** (Many2one → `federation.fee.type`): optional; when set,\n  a `federation.finance.event` (charge) is automatically created when\n  `action_approve_result()` completes.\n- **`result_finance_event_ids`** (computed): finance events created with the\n  configured result fee type for this match.\n- **`action_approve_result()`** override: calls the base result pipeline and then\n  fires the auto-event through the idempotent source helper.\n\n## Discipline Fine Hooks\n\n`sanction_finance_hooks.py` extends `federation.sanction` so that:\n\n- sanctions of type `fine` automatically create a `federation.finance.event`\n- the default fee type code is `discipline_fine`\n- fine events inherit subject references from the sanction or disciplinary case\n- changing the fine amount updates the linked draft finance event instead of\n  creating a second one\n\n## Referee Reimbursement Hooks\n\n`referee_reimbursement_hooks.py` extends `federation.match.referee` so that:\n\n- assignments reaching `done` automatically create a reimbursement event\n- the default fee type code is `referee_reimbursement`\n- reverting the assignment out of `done` cancels the draft reimbursement event\n- returning to `done` reuses the same source-traceable reimbursement event\n\n## Venue Booking Hooks\n\n`venue_finance_hooks.py` extends `federation.match` so that:\n\n- scheduled matches with a venue automatically create a venue booking charge\n- the default fee type code is `venue_booking`\n- removing the venue or unscheduling the match cancels the draft venue event\n- the manual `action_create_venue_finance_event()` helper now reuses the same\n  source event instead of failing on duplicate creation\n\n### Migration note (v19.0.1.2.0)\n\nThe finance bridge now depends on `sports_federation_venues` and adds automatic\nhooks for discipline fines, completed referee assignments, -{"content": "# Sports Federation Club Roles and Portal\n\nVersion: 19.0.4.1.0\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nRole-oriented self-service portal for club representatives, officials, and tournament operators.\n\n## Primary user journeys\n\n### Club representative\n\n- manage club teams and players\n- submit season and tournament registrations\n- prepare and activate rosters\n- complete match sheets and readiness tasks\n- nominate officials\n- review result actions and deadlines\n\n### Official\n\n- view assignments\n- confirm or decline within the authorized scope\n- access relevant match information\n\n### Tournament operator\n\n- use the tournament operations board\n- monitor courts, matches, readiness, and action queues\n- execute scoped result and operational actions\n\n## Trust boundary\n\nAll privileged portal writes must use a model-owned method and the shared `federation.portal.privilege` boundary. Controllers validate input and resolve scope but do not perform raw elevated business writes. See `adr/0001-portal-trust-boundaries.md`.\n\nEvery new privileged route requires:\n\n1. positive in-scope coverage\n2. negative out-of-scope coverage\n3. direct-ID or guessed-record coverage\n4. model/helper ownership assertions when elevation is used\n5. CSRF enforcement for state-changing browser or JSON-RPC routes\n\n## Portal UX direction\n\nThe landing page should remain task-first. Common tasks are teams, registrations, upcoming matches, and action items. Specialist tools should be progressively disclosed instead of presented as an undifferentiated module catalogue.\n\n## Operations board\n\nThe board loads through scoped JSON-RPC, supports polling and structured failures, and exposes only matches and actions available to the current user. Server-side checks remain authoritative.\n\n## Tests\n\nThe module includes HTTP smoke, ownership, access-denied, team, player, roster, registration, officiating, result, accessibility, mobile, operations-board, and end-to-end portal workflow tests.\n\n## Consolidated documentation\n\n`PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_COVERAGE.md`, `PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_TEST_MATRIX.md`, and `ROADMAP_RC.md` are deleted. Their durable rules are consolidated here and in ADR-0001; the test files are the authoritative live coverage map.\n\n## competition portal\n\nThe active competition portal is edition-based. Participation comes from\ncompetition entries and finalized participant sets. Match-day schedule data is\nrendered only from each match day's current live publication. +{"content": "# Sports Federation Club Roles and Portal\n\nVersion: 19.0.4.1.0\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nRole-oriented self-service portal for club representatives, officials, and tournament operators.\n\n## Primary user journeys\n\n### Club representative\n\n- manage club teams and players\n- submit season and tournament registrations\n- prepare and activate rosters\n- complete match sheets and readiness tasks\n- nominate officials\n- review result actions and deadlines\n\n### Official\n\n- view assignments\n- confirm or decline within the authorized scope\n- access relevant match information\n\n### Tournament operator\n\n- use the tournament operations board\n- monitor courts, matches, readiness, and action queues\n- execute scoped result and operational actions\n\n## Trust boundary\n\nAll privileged portal writes must use a model-owned method and the shared `federation.portal.privilege` boundary. Controllers validate input and resolve scope but do not perform raw elevated business writes. See `adr/0001-portal-trust-boundaries.md`.\n\nEvery new privileged route requires:\n\n1. positive in-scope coverage\n2. negative out-of-scope coverage\n3. direct-ID or guessed-record coverage\n4. model/helper ownership assertions when elevation is used\n5. CSRF enforcement for state-changing browser or JSON-RPC routes\n\n## Portal UX direction\n\nThe landing page should remain task-first. Common tasks are teams, registrations, upcoming matches, and action items. Specialist tools should be progressively disclosed instead of presented as an undifferentiated module catalogue.\n\n## Operations board\n\nThe board loads through scoped JSON-RPC, supports polling and structured failures, and exposes only matches and actions available to the current user. Server-side checks remain authoritative.\n\n## Tests\n\nThe module includes HTTP smoke, ownership, access-denied, team, player, roster, registration, officiating, result, accessibility, mobile, operations-board, and end-to-end portal workflow tests.\n\n## Consolidated documentation\n\n`PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_COVERAGE.md`, `PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_TEST_MATRIX.md`, and `ROADMAP_RC.md` are deleted. Their durable rules are consolidated here and in ADR-0001; the test files are the authoritative live coverage map.\n\n## competition portal\n\nThe active competition portal is edition-based. Participation comes from\ncompetition entries and finalized participant sets. Match-day schedule data is\nrendered only from each match day's current live publication. Draft schedules,\nreview evidence and superseded publications are intentionally unavailable.\n\nPrimary routes:\n\n- `/my/competitions`\n- `/my/competition-entries`\n- `/my/match-days`\n- `/sports/match-days/<id>/operations`\n\nLegacy tournament workspace routes are redirect-only and render no V1 data.\nThe backend tournament-registration action is loaded before the menus that use\nit, so a fresh module install and an upgrade both build the registration menu\nwithout relying on stale database metadata.\n\n\n## Accessible error recovery and focus management\n\nPortal forms move keyboard focus to server-rendered error summaries, connect\ninvalid controls to that summary with `aria-describedby`, and announce the\nsummary through an assertive live region. -{"content": "# Sports Federation Public Site\n\nPublic website coverage for tournaments, now integrated into the main\nTournaments navigation instead of a separate Competitions surface.\n\n## Purpose\n\nThis module turns published tournaments into a coherent public product for fans,\nclubs, and media. It provides a tournament hub, overview pages, schedule and\nresults pages, standings snapshots, team profile pages, JSON feed access, and\ncalendar export while keeping older competition URLs working.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `website` | Odoo website framework |\n| `sports_federation_portal` | Main tournament website hub and navigation |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournaments, matches, participants |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings data |\n| `sports_federation_venues` | Venue information |\n| `sports_federation_result_control` | Approved result visibility |\n\n## Model extensions\n\n### `federation.tournament`\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `website_published` | Boolean | Enables public visibility |\n| `public_slug` | Char | Legacy public slug retained for tournament feed and redirect compatibility |\n| `public_description` | Html | Long-form website description |\n| `public_featured` | Boolean | Marks the tournament for featured hub sections |\n| `public_editorial_summary` | Text | Short editorial summary for cards and overview layouts |\n| `public_pinned_announcement` | Text | Announcement banner content for the overview page |\n| `public_hero_image` | Binary | Hero image for the public overview page |\n| `show_public_results` | Boolean | Enables the public results page |\n| `show_public_standings` | Boolean | Enables the public standings page |\n\nKey helper methods expose canonical public URLs, published tournament queries,\nteam/result/standings/schedule datasets, JSON feed payloads, and ICS calendar\nexport content.\n\n### `federation.team`\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `public_slug` | Char | Canonical public slug used in `/teams/<slug>` |\n\nTeam helpers provide stable team profile URLs and public tournament links.\nTheir public slug resolver accepts an extra publication domain so controller\nlookups can fail closed before rendering profile, follow, feed, or calendar\nsurfaces.\n\n### `federation.season`\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `website_published` | Boolean | Enables season-wide discovery on the website |\n| `public_slug` | Char | Canonical public slug used in `/seasons/<slug>` |\n| `public_summary` | Text | Short summary used on season discovery pages |\n| `public_description` | Html | Long-form season landing page content |\n\nSeason helpers provide canonical season URLs, featured and recent tournament\nqueries, editorial aggregation for season landing pages, and fail-closed public\nslug resolution for published-season routes.\n\n### `federation.public.editorial.item`\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `publication_state` | Selection | draft / scheduled / published / archived |\n| `content_type` | Selection | highlight / announcement / update |\n| `publish_start` / `publish_end` | Datetime | Optional publication window |\n| `season_id` / `tournament_id` / `team_id` | Many2one | Public anchor for the item |\n| `summary` | Text | Card-friendly editorial summary |\n| `body_html` | Html | Long-form editorial content |\n\nEditorial items let operators schedule season-, tournament-, or team-linked\nhighlights without editing website templates.  {"content": "# Competition Registration\n\nThe Registration Desk manages team entries for a competition edition and division.\n\n## Team selection\n\nWhen creating or editing a competition entry, the team dropdown is limited to:\n\n- active teams;\n- teams eligible for the selected division's category and gender;\n- teams that are not already entered in the same registration window.\n\nThe available-team list is computed per division and the form applies it as a\nselection domain. The model also validates the same rules on create and write,\nso direct ORM or API requests cannot bypass the desk filter. Changing a window\nclears an existing team selection when it is no longer valid.\n\nEligibility uses the tournament module's existing `search_eligible_teams()` and\n`get_team_eligibility_error()` APIs. No historical registration entries are\nrewritten by this filtering; it only affects new selections and invalid direct\nwrites.\n\n## Regression tests\n\nThe regression coverage is in\n`tests/test_registration_team_selection.py`. +# Public Competition API
+
+Owner: Federation Platform Team
+Last updated: 2026-09-04
+
+Clubs can consume non-sensitive published data through:
+
+```text
+GET /api/v1/competitions
+GET /api/v1/competitions/<edition-slug>
+```
+
+The detail feed aggregates published divisions, teams, schedule sections,
+approved results, standings, brackets, and canonical links. It excludes contact
+details, personal data, internal notes, discipline records, unpublished
+schedules, and unapproved results.
+
+Responses advertise contract version `v1` and allow 60-second caching. Club
+representatives use **My Account > Data API** or `/my/data-api` for live examples.

+print_odoo_failure() {
+  local exit_code="$1" logfile="${ODOO_LOGFILE:-$repo_root/odoo-rc.log}"
+  echo "ERROR: Odoo RC lane '$lane' failed with exit code $exit_code." >&2
+  if [[ -f "$logfile" ]]; then
+    echo "--- Odoo failure summary ---" >&2
+    grep -E "(^|[[:space:]])(ERROR|CRITICAL)[[:space:]]|FAIL:|ERROR:|[0-9]+ failed|[0-9]+ error" "$logfile" | tail -n 120 >&2 || true
+    echo "--- Last 200 Odoo log lines ---" >&2
+    tail -n 200 "$logfile" >&2 || true
+  fi
+  return "$exit_code"
+}
+
+run_odoo() {
+  local logfile="${ODOO_LOGFILE:-$repo_root/odoo-rc.log}"
+  : > "$logfile"
+  if "$@"; then return 0; else local rc=$?; print_odoo_failure "$rc"; return "$rc"; fi
+}
